### Established signatures, contexts and reuse

- Engine signatures are `AttachedAttacks(*PermanentBinding) EventPattern`,
  `AttachedBlocks(*PermanentBinding) EventPattern`,
  `AttachedAttacksUnblocked(*PermanentBinding) EventPattern`, and
  `AttachedAttacksOrBlocks(*PermanentBinding) EventPattern`.
  Each requires a valid named binding. The union is one ability, not two grants.
- RON accepts battlefield `TriggerA` with `WhenACreatureAttacks`,
  `WhenACreatureBlocks`, or `WhenACreatureAttacksAndIsntBlocked`, each with
  `SinglePermanent(HostPermanent)` on an Aura. `Or` accepts exactly one attack
  and one block event over that same host, in either order. Other event names,
  subjects, unions and unbound reads reject during declaration compilation.
- `scope.hostCombat` identifies one lexical producer. Both
  `Trigger_ThatCreature` and `Trigger_ThatPermanent` lower to its saved host.
  Each factory creates its own `PermanentBinding` in the existing instance
  binding map. Inner delayed unblocked/death event producers retain priority
  over the corresponding outer aliases. Future-step bodies retain outer facts.
- RON owns shape, arity, context checks and aliases. The engine owns event
  membership and capture. `GenericTriggered.CheckEventType` consults an optional
  private typed-pattern matcher; existing patterns keep their single-type checks.
  No broad event-list API or current caller was removed.
- Reused services: native attacker/blocker/unblocked events, the singular-block
  flag, `EventSourceIsAttachedTo`, `eventPermanentCapture`, `capturedPermanent`,
  `From`, pending-trigger controller snapshots, resolution maps, optional mana
  payment, combat removal, temporary layers, future-step capture, stack copies
  and game clones. No parallel scheduler, zone service or payment system exists.
- Detection requires a present unphased creature at the attached event visit;
  explicit stale incarnations reject. Resolution cannot follow a returned host.
  Reattachment cannot change pending subjects. Phasing uses existing exact
  reference behavior; phase cycles retain the visit. Source departure and control
  changes do not erase pending bodies or change their original controller.
  Missing subjects do not stop independent later actions. No new LKI property,
  replacement-order or simultaneous-zone contract was needed.

CR 508.1, 509.3a/g and 603.2/603.3a establish declaration timing, singular block

### Supported contract and reuse boundary

- Engine API:
  `TargetOtherThanSavedPermanent(binding *PermanentBinding) PermanentTargetOption`.
  Use it with typed permanent target declarations. Definition inspection checks
  the saved reference, including nil bindings and producer dominance. Missing,
  zero or incomplete runtime visits give no candidates. A valid saved visit
  excludes only that incarnation, regardless of current control or attachment.
  A returned card's new visit does not inherit the exclusion.
- RON accepts `Other(eventRef)` in ordinary battlefield trigger singular
  permanent target filters, including nested `And` and numbered target groups.
  The reference must lower to `permanentEvent`; the factory builds its option
  from that instance's `PermanentBinding`. Host combat aliases, attached-tap
  captures and combat-opponent aliases use the existing reference compiler.
  Existing source aliases still use `TargetOtherThanSource()` unchanged.
  Direct hosts, prior targets, resolving choices, death-card references,
  unbound/wrong-type/tuple aliases, disjunctions and delayed target scopes reject.
- RON owns spelling, arity and context. The engine owns exact visit comparison
  and event query facts. `capturedTriggerTargetFacts` extends the existing
  snapshot collector; `targetEventQuery` extends the existing player query with
  permanent bindings. Placement, modal availability, copy retargeting and
  resolution use these facts without executing an action, making a payment or
  replacing the live resolution frame.
- Stack objects reuse `capturedPermanents`; existing stack-copy and clone map
  services keep facts separate. Pending events keep detection-time subjects.
  Reattachment, source departure/control changes and phase cycles cannot replace
  a subject. Target departure/return, phasing and protections retain normal
  resolution legality. Missing legal targets remove the trigger before payment.
- Reused services: typed event captures, exact references, target groups,
  APNAP placement/order, target protections, retained source information,
  `ControllerOfWithLKI`, `PowerOfWithLKI`, `DamageSourceOf`, `DamagePayment`,
  `PayActionOrElse`, damage prevention/replacements, temporary
  `AssignsNoCombatDamage`, cleanup, stack copying and game cloning.
  No parallel event, zone, payment or replacement service was added.

CR 400.7 supplies return identity; CR 603.3a/d supplies controller and target
placement; CR 608.2b supplies target rechecks; CR 608.2h supplies departed host
information. CR 702.26b/d makes a phased host unavailable for the damage action,
while a phase cycle keeps its visit. The existing damage-payment service allows
a departed host's saved source information and rejects a currently phased host.
The target exclusion itself reads identity and needs no characteristic LKI.
No simultaneous-operation or replacement-order contract changed.

Fastbond remain separate known source investigations. All RON records and their
hashes stay unchanged; no vocabulary snapshot refresh is required.
No Go definition, startup registry, generator or broad DSL function was removed.

### Supported signatures, boundaries and engine reuse

RON accepts one battlefield Aura `TriggerA` with:

`WhenAPlayerActivatesAnAbility(AnyPlayer,
And([AbilityOfPermanent(HostPermanent), HasTapSelfInCost, NonManaAbility]))`.

The three operands can appear in any order, exactly once. HostPermanent needs
the existing Aura scope. `Trigger_ThatActivatedAbility` binds one exact activated
stack object and supplies CounterAbility or ControllerOfAbility in the same
resolving body, including optional payment branches. Other player/source/filter
forms, disjunctions, tuple symbols, absent/duplicate operands, incompatible
aliases, cross-rule reads and delayed RON ability reads reject at compilation.
The event does not manufacture player or permanent event aliases.

New engine API:

- `BindAbility(name string) *AbilityBinding`.
- `FromAbility(binding *AbilityBinding) AbilityRef`.
- `ActivatedAbilityEvent().FromAttachedPermanent().WithTapCost().NonMana()`.
- `ActivatedAbilityEvent().WithAbility(binding *AbilityBinding)`.
- `core.GameEvent.ActivatedAbilityID uuid.UUID` for completed stack activations.

`ron` owns spelling, operand validation and the lexical ability event plan.
The existing target-ability plan remains intact; a typed reference plan selects
its target or event producer. Every factory call builds a fresh event binding.
`mage` owns exact activation identity, matching and typed reads. The new binding
uses a private key in existing stack-identity resolution frames. Existing
snapshot, delay, cloning, APNAP, counter, cost transaction and combat services
remain the only execution paths. No parallel event/payment/stack service,
card-name branch, Go-card fallback, live ability grant, skipped rule or partial
production registry was introduced.

Mana activations emit no stack identity. A targeted mana-producing ability is
nonmana and emits one. Tap filtering reads the existing written tap-symbol
cost flag. Failed payments and illegal tap activations emit no completed event.
The host filter checks the Aura's exact current attachment and event incarnation.
Capture occurs at detection, before trigger placement. A copied activation
creates no new activation event. A copied trigger retains the saved ability,
while its controller pays its own optional cost. Pending source control changes
do not change the original trigger's payer. Countering never refunds the tap cost.

CR 602.2a–b supplies stack identity and payment timing; CR 603.3a/b supplies
controller capture and APNAP placement; CR 605.1a/3b/5a supplies mana classification;
CR 701.6a–b supplies countering without refunds; CR 400.7 and 702.26b/d supply
return identity and phasing. Source LKI is not required to counter a still-present
ability; source departure cannot erase the saved stack object. Missing or departed
abilities supply no subject, and later instructions continue. Clones and delayed
engine bodies keep their own frames. No replacement-order or simultaneous-operation
contract changed.

### Contract, exact context and reuse boundary

Engine signature:
`WhenCombatPairUntilEndOfCombat(subject PermanentRef, filter PermanentFilter,
opponent *PermanentBinding, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.
It saves the watched incarnation and creator controller at resolution, before
future events. Each matching pair captures its opponent at detection, before
APNAP placement. The body receives a separate saved resolution frame with that
capture. Source control changes and ability removal do not end the subscription.
Source departure and phasing prevent new matches; a phase cycle preserves the
visit. Departure/return cannot transfer a watched or opposing identity.
Pending bodies survive source departure and subscription expiry. A missing or
phased opponent prevents its action but does not stop subsequent instructions.

`TriggerSystem.ClearEndOfCombat()` removes only combat-bounded subscriptions
when native EndCombat priority has finished, before effect expiry and combat
reset. Cleanup also removes unused subscriptions. First-strike grants created
by the body remain active until their own turn-end expiry. Copies and clones
keep independent frames, resources and effect lifetimes.

RON signature: `CreateTriggerUntil(Or([WhenACreatureBlocksACreature(
SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent), filter), WhenACreatureBecomesBlockedByACreature(
SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent), filter)]), ActionList([...]), UntilEndOfCombat)`.
It accepts the two directions in either order, with identical operands and the
existing combat-pair creature-filter grammar, in resolving permanent-source
contexts. Trigger_ThatOtherCreature and the existing Trigger_ThatOtherPermanent
alias read the delayed body's opponent. Bindings are fresh per factory.
Host subjects, single-direction events, other durations, malformed operands,
empty bodies, noncreature filters and incompatible/unbound aliases reject.
The engine additionally supports typed watched targets, proved with a synthetic
spell; this does not broaden the RON adapter.

RON owns spelling, role checks and lexical bindings. The engine reuses
filteredCombatPairPattern matching/capture, DelayedTrigger persistence, stack
placement, exact reference services and capturedDelayedBody. The duplicated
step/departure snapshot code was extracted to captureDelayedBody without a
behavior change. A shared compileCombatPairEvent plan retains ordinary printed
pair triggers and their text-layer path. Optional payment, mana rollback,
keyword layers and native first-strike damage remain existing services.
No parallel event system, global result, card-name branch or fallback was added.

CR 603.7a–e supplies arming, duration, exact visits and creator control;
CR 603.3b supplies APNAP placement; CR 511.2 supplies combat-phase expiry;
CR 400.7 and 702.26 supply return identity and phasing. LKI cannot restore a
subject for an action. No new replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation
contract was needed; native combat uses the existing damage batches.

### Contract, signatures, contexts and reuse

Engine additions:

- `DiscardCountInto(binding *NumberBinding) DiscardCardResultOption` on
  `Discard(player PlayerRef, amount ResolutionValue, options ...DiscardCardResultOption)`.
- `ReturnChosenGraveyardCardsToHand(graveyard PlayerRef, amount ResolutionValue,
  filter CardFilter) ResolvingEffect`.

The count option requires one nonnil binding and rejects mixed count/card-result
options. A required choice reads the amount once, caps it to the hand, selects
distinct original visits and uses the shared mandatory fallback for invalid or
incomplete selections. `snapshotHandGroup`, `chooseHandDiscards` and
`discardActionsTogetherWithEvents` supply identity, ordering and replacements.
Completed library destinations count; cancellation and returned visits do not.
Nonpositive amounts and missing players clear the count. Existing fixed-discard,
card-result and per-player result callers retain their paths.

The return service saves matching current graveyard visits at resolution. The
effect controller selects distinct cards before movement. Short graveyards
supply available cards; invalid choices use the first remaining candidate.
New cards cannot join the selection. Departure and return cannot supply a saved
visit. The existing graveyard movement service gains an internal destination
callback: all selected cards enter their owners' hands before zone observations,
then one EvtCardsLeftGraveyard reports the actual batch count. Existing public
MoveCardsFromGraveyard callers retain their prior event timing.

RON accepts `DiscardNumberCards(Integer(n))` for nonnegative n and
`DiscardNumberCards(ValueX)` with a bound X. A direct DiscardACard or
DiscardNumberCards instruction can produce the symbol NumCardsDiscardedThisWay
in its remaining lexical action list. A later direct producer supplies a new
binding. Branch-local producers cannot escape; existing delayed bodies can
capture the result. `ReturnNumberCardsFromPlayersGraveyardToHand(
NumCardsDiscardedThisWay, AnyCard, player)` accepts existing singular player
references. Other return amounts/filters and other producer shapes need adapters.
Unbound values, malformed declarations, incompatible players and out-of-scope
reads reject before factory use. Factories allocate fresh typed result bindings.
Shared number frames retain isolation through resolutions, copies, clones and
delayed captures. No global last-action slot or game-time declaration panic exists.

RON owns syntax, roles, source diagnostics and lexical plans. The engine owns
choices, exact visits, actual results, replacement batches and movement. X mana
locking, spell-copy controller/identity and resolving spell exile are reused.
CR 701.9a–c, 608.2c–d, 609.3 and 400.7 supply the rules contracts. This shape
has no new battlefield LKI/phasing subject, target-announcement choice, cost
rollback or replacement-order subsystem. Existing payment and replacement
services retain those responsibilities.

### Exact supported signatures, contexts and dependencies

Engine API:
`WhenReceivesDamageThisTurn(PermanentRef, PermanentFilter, *NumberBinding,
ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`. The subject must be present and unphased at
installation. Its exact incarnation is saved. A matching permanent damage source
and positive actual event amount produce one pending body per event until
cleanup. The creator's source and controller remain saved. Current recipient
control or characteristics cannot retarget the subscription. Departure/return
cannot supply it; a phase cycle preserves it. Queued bodies survive expiry and
departure. Each stack body receives its own saved amount inside the captured
frame. Copies and clones keep independent frames; copy controllers retain the
ordinary shared stack-copy behavior.

RON shape:
`CreateTriggerUntil(WhenAPermanentDealsDamageToAPermanent(filter,
SinglePermanent(ref)), ActionList(nonempty_actions), UntilEndOfTurn)` in ordinary
resolving bodies. Supported singular permanent refs and the existing permanent
damage-source filter adapter are reused. The inventory record uses
`And([IsAttacking, IsCardtype(Creature)])`. `Trigger_ThatMuch` is a symbol bound
only to this body's damage amount, including nested saved bodies. Unbound,
malformed, escaped and unrelated event aliases reject. Other subjects,
durations and event contexts remain unsupported.

Engine reuse: `captureDelayedBody`, exact permanent refs, `damageFilterSource`,
`DamageSourceIsAttacking`, native damage/replacement batches, pending trigger
placement, `eventAmountCapture`, saved-number maps, stack copies, game clones,
cleanup and waiting source categories. No parallel damage system, custom payment
path, global last-action state, fallback or partial production registry was
introduced. Existing cost rollback and replacement ordering remain owned by
those shared services. Inventory roles now identify the delayed damage event,
source filter and exact recipient ref. Waiting queries preserve the watched
visit and nested installation source reads without running actions.

Rules evidence: CR 120.4 and 120.8 (actual damage after prevention/replacement;
zero damage), 400.7 (new objects after zone movement), 603.7a–e (installation,
stated duration, identities and creator control), and 702.26b,d (phasing).

  `DelayedStepPattern` via `stepPattern{EvtMainPhase, true}`.
  `AtNext(YourMainPhase, body)` consumes the next actual own main-phase event,
  regardless of its precombat flag. Skipped phases do not emit events; extra
  phases can satisfy it. Cleanup preserves this one-shot schedule. Creation is
  during resolution, detection queues for priority, and later events do not
  repeat it. The existing engine owns source/controller capture, pending
  placement, phasing, copies, clones and schedule lifetime.
- RON: `CreateFutureTrigger(AtTheBeginningOfPlayersNextMainPhase(You),
  ActionList(nonempty-actions))` in existing resolving action contexts.
  The exact bare You argument is required. Other players, targeted delayed
  bodies and empty lists remain rejected. Scope and spelling stay in ron.

  ManaValueOfSpell(bound-singular-spell-reference))` in ordinary resolving
  bodies, including delayed bodies. Existing typed targets and spell-event
  bindings supply the reference. Invalid or unbound references, choice of
  color, multiple productions, entry and draw-replacement contexts reject.
- `compileSpellManaValue(Node, scope) (valueFactory, error)` shares exact

### Supported shapes, dependencies and engine contract

Top-level permanent static `If(condition, rules)`, `Unless(condition, rules)`
and `IfElse(condition, trueRules, falseRules)` require nonempty branch lists.
They compose the already supported conditional PermanentRuleEffect attack,
untap and spell-target forms, EachPlayerEffect untap limits,
ReplaceWouldDealDamage redirection, and conditional layer declarations.
Each family keeps its exact prior subjects and operation shape. Layer parts
are validated together and retain the existing same-layer restriction and
shared type-layer membership service. Bare keywords, resolving actions,
triggers, targets, payments, unsupported collection rule operations and
unsupported protection forms still reject. Both branches compile before a
factory is available. No declaration is silently dropped.

The added prevention shape is exactly
`PreventDamage(DamageWouldBeDealtByAPermanentToRecipient(filter,
Permanent(ThisPermanent)), [PreventThatDamage])` in a conditional static body.
Combat-pair source filters and other prevention events remain unsupported here.
No target, event or lexical result binding is introduced. All factory calls
build separate abilities and registration state.

Engine signature:
`PreventDamageFromMatchingPermanentsIf(subject PermanentRef,
from PermanentFilter, condition StateCondition) StaticRule`.
The condition and subject must pass definition validation. Zero source filters
retain the existing any-permanent meaning. The reusable engine service also
supports AttachedPermanent; the new RON prevention shape is source-only.
The shared static replacement cycle installs the declaration even when the
condition is false. Each match and waiting-source query checks the current
source controller and exact incarnation. Earlier replacements can change the
condition before rechecks. False conditions supply no waiting subject.
Source departure or phasing stops prevention; phase-in restores it; a returned
source cannot restore an old cycle. Existing source filter LKI, unpreventable
damage, simultaneous packet scope, attachment identity and clone services are
reused. No new payment, replacement ordering or batch system was added.
Rules read: CR 604, 611.3a–c, 615 and the established 616 replacement contract.
API and rules documentation describe only this supported boundary.

### Exact contract, dependencies and engine reuse

New engine API: `BandedWith(subject PermanentRef) PermanentSet`.
It selects present current band members in battlefield order. The source and
all members must match their exact combat incarnations. Unbanded attackers
supply no members; one-member bands include their subject. Missing contexts,
nil subjects and absent visits supply no members at execution. Definition
validation rejects nil and unbound subjects. Combat membership has no LKI
fallback. A returned visit cannot replace an old subject or combat participant.
Ability loss keeps the band. Combat removal, departure and phasing remove band
membership; phase-in cannot restore it. Clones read their own combat state.

RON shape: `BandedWith(permanentRef)` in ordinary resolving contextual
collections, including nested nonempty And/Or lists and existing source, host,
target, choice and event reference scopes. Entry and draw replacement contexts
reject this adapter. Static prevention and payment declarations remain separate.
The compiler uses compilePermanentRef and builds operands per factory instance.
There is no card-name branch, mutable declaration state or global action result.

The engine reuses FormAttackingBand, IsAttackingIncarnation, band removal,
PermanentRef, definition traversal, contextual set composition and saved frames.
Waiting delayed traversal now retains explicit source operands in BandedWith;
it does not read combat or execute actions. Existing AtNext, Until,
GrantEachKeyword, target legality, spell/trigger copies, phasing and clone
services keep their existing behavior. Temporary grants save recipients at
resolution. Later combat removal, source departure, control changes and a phase
cycle do not change those saved recipients; zone return cannot inherit a grant.
No payment, replacement ordering or simultaneous damage mechanism was added.

The native BandFormer path forms bands after individual attack events but before
pending attack bodies resolve. Skirmishers needs its event identity at detection
and its collection at resolution, so no attack event or band timing change is
required. The explicit ExecuteAttackers path can likewise form a band before
placing and resolving pending triggers.

### Supported signatures, context and engine reuse

RON supports exactly one operation in
`AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent, [EntersWithLayerEffectOfChoice(options)])`.
`options` is a nonempty list of nonempty modification lists. Each list can use:

- `SetCopiablePT(PT(integer, integer))`.
- `AddCopiableCardtype(permanentType)`.
- `AddCopiableCreatureType(subtypeSymbol)`.
- `AddCopiableAbility([fixedKeywords])`, with a nonempty supported keyword list.

The adapter validates every option, including unchosen options. Host, resolving,
static-layer, empty, malformed, dynamic and unknown declarations reject.
It creates fresh abilities per factory and has no card-name dispatch.

Engine API: `ChooseCopiableVariantAsEnters(variants ...[]CopyModification) Ability`,
`CopySetPowerToughness(power, toughness int) CopyModification`,
`CopyAddSubTypes(subtypes ...string) CopyModification`, and
`CopyAddKeywords(keywords ...core.Attr) CopyModification`.
Existing `CopyAddCardTypes` supplies type addition. Fixed P/T changes base
values and keeps existing characteristic definitions; it does not implement
copy exceptions that remove those abilities.

The engine reuses `battlefieldEntryAction`, the shared replacement service,
`CopiableValues.WithModifications`, fresh definition plans,
`BuildEntryCopyWithText`, physical printed provenance and `replaceEntryDefinition`.
Stable declaration-origin/ordinal keys prevent a variant rule from applying
again after rebuilding its definition in the same entry event. Copy replacement
priority precedes variant choices; same-priority replacements keep the existing
affected-player choice. Option labels show characteristics. Preview builds make
no game choices. Invalid answers or a missing player use the first option.

Selected values become copiable under CR 707.2. Copies acquire the entry rule and
make a new choice under CR 707.5–6; copied additions remain. Counters and ordinary
layer effects do not enter the snapshot. Source control changes and phase cycles
do not repeat entry. Return starts with printed physical rules and a new visit.
Permanent spell copies retain token identity, owner and controller. There is no
new cost, damage, LKI query, APNAP policy or simultaneous-operation mechanism.
Existing batch entry makes all choices before registering any entrant.

### Supported signatures, contexts and engine boundary

- `ChooseNumberAsEnters(minimum, maximum int) AsEntersBattlefieldAbility`:
  nonnegative ordered integer bounds; entry controller chooses before
  registration. Missing players and invalid answers use the minimum.
- `MayChooseNumber(subject PermanentRef, minimum, maximum int) ResolvingEffect`:
  resolving controller chooses; decline keeps state. Saves the subject visit and
  rechecks after the offer and the numeric choice. Absent, returned or phased
  subjects supply no update. Successful updates refresh existing layers.
- `ChosenNumberOf(subject PermanentRef) ResolutionValue`: pure exact-visit
  current/phase/departure information. Missing choices supply zero. An integer
  plus a presence flag belongs to each Permanent; clones/LKI copy both by value.
- RON: one `AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent,[ChooseANumberBetween(min,max)])`;
  `MayAction(ChooseANumberBetween(min,max))` in resolving battlefield source
  bodies; bound symbol `TheChosenNumber` in static values, including `Minus`;
  source `PermanentLayerEffect` with separate `SetPower(value)` and
  `SetToughness(value)`, at most one of each, under the number entry declaration.
  Unsupported mixed lists, duplicate declarations, malformed bounds, nonpermanent
  entry, payments, zone-source bodies and unbound/granted reads reject early.

decision, visit rechecks and information read. Existing source references, entry

Before editing, stated the exact supported syntax, engine/compiler boundary and
acceptance cases: either player, the paid source in a self-targeted graveyard,
current resolution membership, rollback, copies, clones, complete event batches,
invalid forms and atomic collection loading.

### Supported contract and reuse boundary

- RON accepts `Exile([EachCardInGraveyards(InAPlayersGraveyard(SinglePlayer(ref)))], [])`
  in resolving action bodies. `ref` uses existing singular resolving player
  references with their lexical target/event/action/source scopes. No new binding
  producer is introduced. Factories create references from their own instance
  bindings. Ordinary and delayed action bodies share this adapter.
- Multiple graveyard players, characteristic selection filters, modifiers,
  `NumberCardsInGraveyards`, entry operations, activation/resolution costs and
  `ThePermanentsSacrificedThisWay` remain rejected by their respective contexts.
  Sword of the Ages must not exile a whole graveyard in place of its paid cards.
- Public engine signature: `ExileGraveyardFor(PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`.
  It resolves its player once, selects current graveyard cards and saves visits.
  Private shared signature:
  `(*Game).exileGraveyardVisitsTogether(uuid.UUID, []capturedCard, uuid.UUID)`.
  The holder, saved visits and attributing source are separate operands.
- All eligible saved visits leave before exile insertion, and all exile insertions
  precede zone events. Missing, returned, wrong-zone and duplicate visits cannot
  move. One `EvtCardsLeftGraveyard` reports the completed count; empty batches
  send no departure events. Cards added by event observers cannot join the batch.
  Cards are face up and keep ownership and source attribution.
- Existing `exileGraveyardCardsTogether` captures current visits and delegates
  to this service. Existing transaction choices, locks and rollback stay in the
  cost subsystem. `MoveCardsFromGraveyard` and singular exile callers keep their
  existing contracts. No payment result or linked exile declaration is added.
- Explicit source reads in the typed player supply waiting delayed references.
  Queries do not read graveyards or move cards. Existing current/LKI controller
  reads keep exact source visits after phasing or departure. Return cannot
  replace the saved source. Copies and clones use existing frames and zone state.
- RON owns grammar, declaration checks and lexical binding; mage owns saved
  visits, zone movement, event timing, ownership, delayed reads and clone state.
  Reused definition inspection, player references, graveyard visits, ExileCard,
  zone events, payment transactions and source-information services. No global
  last-action slot, card-name branch, fallback or partial production registry.

CR 400.7, 404, 406.2–3 and 603.10 supply the identity, visibility and observation
contracts. Exile is neither destruction nor sacrifice. Graveyard cards do not
use battlefield phasing or regeneration. No new replacement-order policy is
added beyond the existing graveyard-exile service. No source-data defect was
found; no RON records or vocabulary source hashes changed.

Corrected one extra parenthesis in the synthetic delayed fixture. No gameplay

### Contract, signatures and reuse boundary

- Engine: `ExileMatchingPermanentCost(filter PermanentFilter, text string) Cost`.
  Requires one present matching permanent controlled by the payer; source
  inclusion is allowed. Zero filter and empty text fail definition validation.
- Pure `CanPay` checks do not choose, move, tap or consume resources. Tapped
  creatures can pay; phased or wrong-controller subjects cannot. Target
  protections, indestructible and regeneration cannot stop an exile choice.
- Shared `costPaymentTransaction.validate` copies the cost and uses the real
  payer to choose on isolated state. It saves one `capturedPermanent`, including
  incarnation. `Commit` uses the existing total-payment preflight before live
  mana/tap/life expenditure. Returned, phased, changed-controller and missing
  visits cannot replace the choice. Two exile costs cannot use one departed visit.
- Reused `exilePermanent` for face-up exile, ownership, attributing source,
  departure information and zone events. Tokens leave and send an exile zone
  event without leaving a persistent exile card. This is not sacrifice or death.
  Existing replacement ordering and zone batching policies are unchanged.
- RON: `Exile([APermanent(filter)], [])` in ordinary activation cost groups and
  nonmodal `CastEffect(AdditionalCastingCost(...))` for instants/sorceries with
  `SpellActions`. One conjunctive `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))` is
  required. Characteristic filters and nonempty nested And/Or lists reuse the
  matching tap-payment filter compiler. Controller clauses under Or, duplicate
  controllers, other players, malformed declarations, modifiers and plural
  subjects reject. Inventory assigns the subject's child `permanent_filter`.
- Each factory gets separate cost/ability definitions. Transaction choices stay
  private to the payment. This resultless payment does not occupy the existing
  graveyard-exile result plan. Copies do not repeat payment; clones keep separate
  zones and pending source frames. Source departure, return or phasing cannot
  redirect the later counter instruction to another visit.
- RON owns grammar, context validation and diagnostics. Mage owns choices, visit
  identity, transactions and movement. Saved exile numeric/card/subtype results,
  entry payments, optional RON exile payments and resolving APermanent exile
  remain unsupported. No fallback, card-name branch, global action slot,
  production subset registry or Go definition removal was added.

CR 118, 601.2h, 602.2b, 400.7 and 406 supply payment, identity and destination
contracts. No source defect was found or corrected. All twelve RON sources and
semantic source hashes remain unchanged.

### Contract, exact shape and reuse boundary

Engine signature:
`NewSourceCounterManaAbility(color core.Color, counter core.CounterType) *ManaAbility`.
One immutable typed plan is inspected by definition validation and consumed by
`ManaAbility.currentProductions`. Requires one concrete mana type and valid
permanent counter kind. Returns fresh production slices. Pure live source
queries do not use LKI, choose, tap, add mana, emit events or spend counters.
Missing/phased sources and nonpositive counts return no production. An explicit
zero production entry would be incorrect because the legacy shared production
service normalizes such entries to one mana. Tap status does not change the
quantity an ability could produce. Manual zero activation still pays its tap
cost and remains a mana ability, without a stack object or mana event.

RON supported signature/context:
`Activated(TapPermanent(ThisPermanent), ActionList([AddManaRepeated(<fixed mana symbol>, TheTotalNumberOfCountersOfTypeAmongPermanents(<permanent counter type>, SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent)))]))`
on a battlefield permanent. Fixed symbols are ManaProduceW/U/B/R/G/C. Uses the
existing counter spelling/type adapter. One source tap cost, one action and one
source singleton only. Host/target/event references, plural subjects, colors of
choice, mixed productions/actions/costs, modifiers and ordinary resolving
counter-mana declarations reject. Existing source context checks apply. Semantic
inventory already assigns value, permanent_counter_type, permanent_filter and
permanent_reference correctly; tests confirm these roles.

The fresh factory creates its own ability and typed plan. The plan contains no
mutable game state; clones query their own counters and pools. Return supplies
new counters, phasing keeps counters, and current control supplies activation
and payment rights. Shared source discovery, solver, automatic payment,
transactions, mana type replacements, bonuses and tapped-for-mana events are
reused without parallel implementations. Three counters plus Mana Flare supply
four mana; the existing event reports the source's three mana with its replaced
type, and the bonus is separate. No new replacement ordering was introduced.

No fallback, card-name branch, skipped rule, partial production registry,
last-action slot, declaration panic or Go definition deletion was added.
No DSL function was removed; no removal caller audit was needed. Cutover gates
remain closed. All twelve RON sources and vocabulary source hashes are unchanged;
only the vocabulary loader baseline changes.

### Contract, supported shape and reuse boundary

Engine API:

`ReturnCardToBattlefieldInto(card CardRef, controller PlayerRef, result *PermanentBinding, options ...BattlefieldEntryOption) ResolvingEffect`

The existing `ReturnCardToBattlefield` and its callers keep their signatures.
Both constructors use the same effect and entry-option builder. The shared
internal graveyard-entry service now returns its actual successful entrant;
it does not recover a result by looking up a physical card ID after movement.
Blocked entry, missing operands and changed graveyard visits save no result.
Every execution clears an older value first. Normal replacement preparation,
entry choices, owner/control, tapped options and event ordering stay in mage.

RON exact producer/context:

`PutGraveyardCardOntoBattlefield(Ref_TargetGraveyardCard, [EntersNormally])`

or one `EntersUnderPlayersControl(<existing supported player reference>)`,
with an existing singular creature-only graveyard target, in an ordinary
resolving action list. A later symbol
`ThePermanentPutOnTheBattlefieldThisWay` is a typed permanent reference.
Existing permanent actions, conditions and information readers consume it.
A fresh plan and PermanentBinding belong to each lexical producer and factory
instance. Later producers shadow earlier results only in their continuation.
Branch-local producers cannot export a result. A delayed body retains the
producer in scope at creation even if a later return fails. Forward, missing,
malformed and incompatible references reject during compilation. Entry and
draw-replacement result contexts reject. Unsupported entry modifiers still reject.

Reused PermanentBinding/From, exact incarnation information and LKI, existing
resolution maps, clone and stack-copy services, delayed frame capture, and
waiting permanent-source enumeration. No new mutable subsystem state or global
last-result slot. Live actions require the saved present, unphased visit.
A phase cycle preserves it; a later returned card cannot replace it. LKI reads
keep original facts without permitting an action on an absent object.
CR 400.7/400.7j, 603.6d and 614.12/614.12a supply the identity and entry contracts.
No payment/refund or simultaneous-operation ordering was added by this slice.

The complete affected records were inspected in FEM (Soul Exchange), LEG
(Takklemaggot), ATQ (Tawnos's Coffin), and all six Animate Dead reprints
(LEA, LEB, 2ED, 3ED, CED, CEI; six records, counted as one name). Animate Dead
has two result reads per record. The vocabulary reports 15 result occurrences
across all four names. No source record or vocabulary snapshot was changed.

### Supported signatures, scope and reuse boundary

Engine additions:

- `PermanentPaymentFact { Filter PermanentFilter; Result *NumberBinding }`.
- `ExileMatchingPermanentCostWithFacts(filter PermanentFilter, text string,
  facts ...PermanentPaymentFact) Cost`.

Each filter is evaluated on the exact selected permanent immediately before
live exile. Current layered characteristics count. Each result saves one or
zero. Definition checks require nonzero filters and distinct non-nil outputs.
The existing constructor and callers retain their behavior. Engine activation
and additional casting cost contexts use the same service; bare resolving
payment results reject until their own contract exists.

RON accepts one existing
`CastEffect(AdditionalCastingCost(Exile([APermanent(filter)], [])))` on a
nonmodal instant or sorcery, and
`If(APermanentWasExiledThisWay(characteristics), [actions])` in its resolving
body or supported delayed bodies. The payment still requires one conjunctive
You-control clause. Historical filters accept card types/colors with negations,
creature/land/enchantment subtypes with supported negations, IsNonToken, and
nonempty nested And/Or lists. Subtype family validation prevents invalid names.
Each predicate has its own immutable plan and fresh per-factory NumberBinding.
No prior payment, source, branch or predicate can replace another predicate.

RON owns spelling, signature/context validation and per-instance lowering.
The engine extends the exact existing cost transaction and exile service.
Validation chooses and locks the visit on an isolated game. Commit checks the
full payment again and reevaluates characteristics before departure, then
publishes facts through `paidNumbers`. Failed payment publishes no facts.
Copies use the paid frame without another payment; cloned pending stack and
delayed frames remain independent. Later return, type loss or source departure
cannot change a saved result. Phasing makes a locked subject ineligible; a
phase cycle preserves its visit.

CR 118.10, 601.2h and 400.7 support payment separation, complete payment and
object identity. No zone, replacement-ordering or simultaneous-operation
service was replaced. APNAP behavior stays with existing services; this shape
has one payer and one paid permanent. LKI consumers use the captured match,
not the exiled card's printed characteristics. No global last-action slot,
card-name dispatch, fallback or declaration-time gameplay was introduced.

Activation, entry, optional, plural and resolving payment producers remain
separate RON adapters. Unless/IfElse and non-characteristic historical filters
are not accepted by this adapter. Full Soul Exchange remains rejected with its
original +2/+2 instruction; the production record was not simplified.

- A successful detection saves event.SourceID's exact battlefield incarnation

### Supported shape, engine contract and reuse boundary

RON resolving bodies accept exactly
`CreatePermanentRuleEffectUntil(subject, [CantAttack],
DuringPlayersNextTurn(player))`. CantAttack is one symbol, the duration has one
typed player operand, and the subject uses the existing typed permanent compiler.
Source, host, target and combat-pair event references retain their established
scopes. Wall of Dust reads Trigger_ThatOtherPermanent and its controller at
resolution. Wrong arity, malformed/unbound operands, mixed operations and other
durations reject before game execution. Other operations with this duration,
static, entry and payment contexts gain no adapter.

Engine API:
`CantAttackDuringNextTurn(subject PermanentRef, player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`.
It saves one present unphased visit, one valid player and the installation turn.
Missing runtime operands install nothing. Definition validation rejects nil or
unbound operands. Departure facts cannot supply an actionable subject. Explicit
source operands remain visible to waiting delayed source queries.

The shared effect manager starts each saved window in BeginActiveTurn before
actual turn actions and removes it in the cleanup expiration stage. Selection
alone does not start a turn. Skipped turns do not consume the window; extra turns
do. Skipped untap, extra upkeep and repeated turn entry do not alter it. The rule
stays through the end step and ends before cleanup state-based actions/priority.
Each installed rule and clone keeps separate window state. CR 500.7, 500.11,
514.2–3 and 611.2a–c supply the timing and identity contract.

Reused typed references, combat-pair detection-time saved bindings, target
legality, shared turn drivers, cleanup, attack rules, permanent incarnation checks,
waiting source inspection, stack copies and engine clone services. The installed
attack rule remains separate from abilities. Source loss or phasing cannot end
it. Later control changes cannot redirect its player. Subject return cannot
inherit the old rule; phasing keeps an installed rule but prevents actions.
No new payment, replacement ordering, simultaneous movement or counter subsystem.
RON owns spelling and scope; mage owns the reusable lifecycle and legality.

### Contract and reuse boundary

RON supports battlefield `TriggerI(event, condition, body)` for the existing
source/host singular block, becomes-blocked-by and exact two-direction union.
Conditions accept nonempty nested And/Or and these exact leaves:
`NumPermanentsPassFilter(GreaterThanOrEqualTo(Integer(n)), properties, relation)`
with fixed n >= 0, and `NoPermanentsPassFilter(properties, relation)`.
Relations are IsBlockingAttacker(permanentRef) and
IsBlockedByDefender(permanentRef). Property collections accept supported resolving
property filters, nonempty And/Or and Other(permanentRef). Creature subtype
families are checked. Unbound operands, other comparisons, empty groups and
unsupported contexts remain declaration errors.

Engine signatures:
`PermanentSetCountAtLeast(subjects PermanentSet, minimum int) StateCondition`;
`PermanentSetIsEmpty(subjects PermanentSet) StateCondition`.
Definition checks reject nil sets, negative minima and unbound saved operands.
Queries read current membership without choices or mutation. StateContext now
carries permanent event facts. WithInterveningIf supplies detection snapshots;
IfState supplies the resolving frame. A separate query view cannot replace or
inherit the live permanent-binding frame. Copies and clones keep their own facts.
Waiting delayed queries retain explicit source operands without evaluating them.

Reused pair event snapshots/aliases, typed refs, WithInterveningIf, pending/stack
lifecycle, BlockersOf/BlockedAttackersOf, set union/intersection/difference,
property filters, temporary keyword layers and shared clone/copy services.
RON owns spelling, declaration validation and per-factory binding allocation;
mage owns pure queries and event/resolution mechanics. CR 603.4, 509.1g–i,
509.2a, 400.7 and 702.26 supply timing/identity boundaries. LKI cannot supply
combat membership or an actionable returned source. Source loss does not cancel
a pending condition. New current blockers can satisfy its resolution check.
No new cost, replacement-order, APNAP or simultaneous-movement service.

### Contract and reuse boundary

RON accepts the exact resolving shape:
`MayAction(SearchLibrary([FindNumberCardsOfType(Integer(n),
And([IsSupertype(Basic), IsCardtype(Land)])), RevealFoundCards,
PutFoundCardsIntoHand, Shuffle]))`, for fixed n >= 0. The two filter leaves
can appear in either order. Activation, spell and trigger action bodies use
existing frames. Explicit PlayerActions accepts the same optional shape and
supplies its saved action player. Wrong arity/order, called instruction symbols,
dynamic or negative bounds, other filters/destinations, entry and cost contexts
remain declaration errors. Direct bounded SearchLibrary without MayAction is
not added. Semantic inventory distinguishes the count and library-card filter.

Engine API:
`MaySearchLibraryToHand(player PlayerRef, maximum int, filter CardFilter)
ResolvingEffect`. Definition validation rejects nil/unbound refs and negative
bounds. The filter is reusable; RON owns the basic-land restriction and spelling.
Decline makes no card choice, reveal, move or shuffle. Acceptance finds zero
through the bound and shuffles once, even for zero, empty and no-match searches.
The player reference resolves once. Missing players have no effect.

The engine saves matching library visits after acceptance. Choices are distinct
and use canonical candidate objects. Nil, foreign and duplicate choices end
selection. All choices precede movement, and all chosen visits are rechecked.
Departure/return cannot supply a chosen visit or join the initial search.
Public reveal precedes owner hand movement; all moves precede individual zone
events; shuffle follows. No draw, land play or casting payment is substituted.
Copies use their resolving controller; clones keep separate libraries, visits,
waiting frames and public reveal history. Explicit player source operands stay
visible to waiting delayed queries without choices or movement. Saved LKI
controller reads cannot follow a returned source.

### Supported contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

RON accepts one `AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent,
[PayAnyAmountOfLifeUpto(maximum)])` on a permanent. The cap supports nonnegative
Integer, recursive Plus, supported static battlefield count filters, and one
conjunctive graveyard count with a supported characteristic card filter and
InAPlayersGraveyard(Opponent or SinglePlayer(You)). Graveyard operands can reverse.
Optional paired CDA_Power(TheLifePaid)/CDA_Toughness(TheLifePaid) require a creature
and this producer. Duplicate, mixed, unbound, malformed, host, activation,
resolving and non-CDA result contexts reject. Static declaration order does not
turn this saved source result into an imperative resolving binding.

Engine APIs: `PayLifeUpToAsEnters(maximum ResolutionValue) Ability`,
`PTEqualsEntryLifePaid() ContinuousEffect`,
`EntryLifePaidOf(subject PermanentRef) ResolutionValue`, and
`CountGraveyardCardsAmong(players PlayerSet, filter CardFilter) ResolutionValue`.
RON owns spelling, cap syntax and result scope. The engine owns choice, payment,
entry replacement, scalar visit state and queries. No card-name branch or global
last-payment slot was added. Existing callers and the broad DSL remain intact.

The cap is read before the choice; legal bounds include zero even with
nonpositive life. Invalid answers or failed rechecks save zero. Shared life-cost
transactions check payment before commit and use the life-loss event service.
Entry cancellation before payment makes no choice; cancellation afterward does
not refund payment. Copy replacements run first; competing entry replacements
use the affected player's order and apply once. Batch entrants finish payments
before entry observations; one payer cannot spend the same life twice.

The saved result applies in layer 7a, before later base overrides, bonuses,
counters and switches. Ability removal/restoration uses the existing CDA service.
Other zones read zero. LKI and phasing keep exact visit facts; return and entry
copies pay anew. Clones keep separate results and life totals. ZoneSystem.Clone
now copies the entering permanent, so an in-progress choice clone cannot mutate
the original. Player-set graveyard counts skip missing/duplicate players and
retain typed source reads in waiting queries without choices or mutation.

countCharacteristicPT, card P/T queries, departure/phase facts and delayed frames.

### Established contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

Engine signatures:

- `func (s DamageSource) TargetsPermanent(permanent *Permanent) bool`
- `func PreventDamageFromSpellsTargeting(subject PermanentRef) StaticRule`
- `func PreventDamageFromSpellsTargetingIf(subject PermanentRef, condition StateCondition) StaticRule`

RON accepts static
`PreventDamage(DamageWouldBeDealtByASpellToRecipient(TargetsPermanent(ThisPermanent),
Permanent(ThisPermanent)), [PreventThatDamage])`, including supported static
If/Unless/IfElse bodies. Both refs must be the source. Exactly one symbol operation
is required. Malformed arities, unknown refs, host/target/event refs, other filters,
other recipients, resolving and payment contexts reject. Inventory classifies
TargetsPermanent as a spell-damage filter with a permanent-reference operand.

The engine captures announced target visits from the live stack object and at
resolution entry, before target legality removes recipients from resolving
instructions. Actual spell-source identity is required. Facts survive stack
removal, retained source bindings and target illegality. Return cannot supply an
old target; phase cycles keep identity. Copies capture their own targets and stack
IDs. Resolution arrays, snapshots and game clones keep separate arrays.

Reused DamageSource exact identities, capturedPermanent, target incarnation
maps, shared target legality/copy services, source snapshots, static subject and
condition queries, cycle replacement lifetime, pure waiting queries, damage
batches, replacement priority/rechecks and unpreventable handling. RON owns

### Established contracts and boundaries

Engine signatures:

- `UntappedLandCountAtTurnStart(player PlayerRef) ResolutionValue`.
- `PermanentStartedTurnUntapped(subject PermanentRef) StateCondition`;
  supports only This and rejects nil or other subjects during definition checks.
- `Game.StartedTurnUntapped(id, incarnation uuid.UUID) bool`, also on TrackerReader.
- Existing `Game.UntappedLandsAtTurnStart(uuid.UUID) int` keeps its signature;
  uncaptured turns return zero. Existing tracker setters and other callers remain.

Game.BeginActiveTurn is the shared capture boundary. It applies beginning-of-turn
expiry and current layers, then captures each present unphased visit's untapped
status and both players' untapped land counts. It captures once per turn/active
player before phasing and untapping. It also runs for skipped untap steps and
extra turns; drivers must consume skipped turns first. Direct doUntap callers use
this same boundary. The former count capture after phasing-in was removed.
Queries never capture. Later taps, land changes, control changes and departure
cannot change facts. Uncaptured new turns cannot read the old turn's counts.
Copies keep saved trigger players and visits; clones copy independent maps.

Source history is a past fact, so a pending trigger reads the saved incarnation
when the source leaves or phases out. Return cannot supply the old visit for an
action; new visits have no history until the next turn. Synthetic historical
GainLife tests distinguish historical checks from live-source requirements.
Counter actions still require their saved present unphased visit.

RON supports ordinary resolving
`TheNumberOfPermanentsOnTheBattlefieldAtBeginningOfTurn(And([IsUntapped,
IsCardtype(Land), ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(playerRef))]))`.
All three clauses must occur exactly once, in any order. Player refs use existing
lexical scopes, including the saved upkeep event player. Entry and draw replacement
contexts reject. Other historical filters and plural player selectors remain
unsupported. Inventory walks the new value's argument as a permanent filter.

RON also supports the symbol StartedThisTurnUntapped in the existing source-only
own-upkeep PermanentPassesFilter TriggerI shape. Ordinary action-body validation
and intervening-if detection/resolution checks remain. Other subjects, constructor
forms and events reject. RON owns spelling and shape; mage owns history and visits.
Reused typed player/source refs, definition validation, layer application,
turn boundaries, pending trigger frames, payment transactions, finite shields,
damage replacement pipeline and copy/clone services. No Go factory fallback,
card-name branch, parallel history subsystem or production partial registry.

### Contract, lowering and reuse boundary

Engine API: `SourceCounterCap(counter core.CounterType, limit int)
ContinuousEffect`, attached with `WithStaticAbility`. Definition validation
requires a valid counter kind and nonnegative limit. Current runtime static
abilities supply caps. No game-time declaration panic or saved registration.
Multiple caps for one kind use the lowest limit; other kinds are unaffected.
Shared layer removal/restoration, factory rebuilding and effect cloning preserve
rule lifecycle and instance separation.

RON accepts exactly `PermanentRuleEffect(ThisPermanent,
[CantHaveMoreThanNumberCountersOfType(Integer(nonnegative), counterType)])`.
The existing permanent-counter adapter supplies typed counters. Host, target,
collection, dynamic-bound and multiple-operation forms remain unsupported.
Inventory assigns the bound a value role and the counter a permanent-counter role.
RON owns spelling and declaration shape; mage owns prohibition and state changes.

CR 101.2 gives the prohibition precedence over permission. Counter placements
use CR 122.6 and the existing affected-player replacement pipeline (CR 616.1).
The cap limits the final amount after all replacements and adds no selectable
replacement. Integrated shared single placement, batch commit and entry counters,
including entry's synthesized extra-counter types. Exact-visit checks before
and after replacement choices prevent departed, phased and returned visits
from supplying the original placement. Batch preparation remains simultaneous.

CR 704.5r removes excess counters at the existing state-based boundary when
a cap becomes active on an object with too many counters. Current ability reads
cover gained/restored and copied rules. Layer application does not remove them.
Phasing suspends the check; phase-in restores it. Return supplies a new visit.
The direct low-level AddCounter API remains a documented pipeline bypass.
Reused current runtime abilities, layers, counter replacements/removal, entry
copying, exact incarnations, copy-on-write game cloning and atomic loader services.

Local `data/LEG.json` confirms the full Oracle counter-cap text. Local CR 101.2,
122.6, 616.1 and 704.5r establish the rule contract. No RON source or vocabulary
snapshot changed. No Go definition, old DSL export, authoring workflow or startup
registry was removed; their completion gates remain closed.

### Contract, supported shape and reuse boundary

Engine signature: `EntersTappedFor(players PlayerSet, filter PermanentFilter)
Ability`, attached with `WithAbility`. Definition validation requires a nonnil,
valid typed player set and a permanent source. Current source control supplies
You. Ownership does not select entrants. Source departure, ability removal,
face-down status and phasing disable the rule; restoration and a new visit use
current abilities and control. The filter's zero value matches all permanents.

RON supports one battlefield declaration:
`ReplaceWouldEnter(APermanentWouldEnterTheBattlefield(And([type predicates,
ControlledByAPlayer(Opponent)])), [EntersTapped])`. The outer And requires one
controller clause and at least one type predicate. Type predicates are
`IsCardtype(type)`, `IsNonCardtype(type)`, and nonempty nested And/Or lists.
The sole operation must be the EntersTapped symbol. Other players, entry event
families, operations, conditional rules and resolving contexts remain errors.
RON owns spelling, shape and lexical validity; mage owns matching and entry.

`battlefieldEntryAction` saves replacement objects keyed by source ID, exact
incarnation and ability ID. Candidates are rebuilt from current runtime abilities
and join the shared default-priority replacement tier. Copy replacements run
first. The affected controller chooses the ordinary replacement order. Each rule
applies once per event; execution rechecks the live source after the choice.
Multiple sources and returned visits keep separate identities. There are no
card-name branches, global last-entry slots or game-time declaration panics.

An isolated clone applies existing layers to a proposed entrant. It includes
copy-modified characteristics and typed source-only composed static modifications
of the entrant. The entrant's general static effects do not start before entry.
The live battlefield, stack, life and event queues do not receive this proposal.
The RON filter reads projected card types and control. Other entry query families
need their own adapters and evidence; untyped legacy callback effects have no
self-subject contract for newly acquired projection effects.

The replacement sets tapped status before entry observers. Shared token batches
prepare every entrant before registration and observations. No tap event is
emitted. Reused the shared replacement pipeline, copy priority, layer service,
permanent cloning, typed PlayerSet/You references, current runtime abilities,
entry batches, factory plans, casting rollback and atomic registry replacement.
No Go definitions, DSL services or authoring/startup paths were removed because
the runtime and removal gates remain closed. No RON source changed, so the
vocabulary snapshot needs no refresh.

Local `data/LEG.json` confirms Kismet's exact Oracle text: artifacts, creatures
and lands the opponents control enter tapped. Land Equilibrium's complete text
requires its separate post-entry sacrifice sequence. Sword of the Ages's Oracle
includes exiling the artifact, which its RON record omits. This compared-candidate
source defect remains deferred with that slice; no unrelated source was changed.

### Exact supported shapes and reuse boundary

New native signature:

`PutThenSacrificeFor(players PlayerSet, entrant, counted PermanentFilter,
minimum ResolutionValue) Ability`.

RON supports static `ReplaceWouldPutAPermanentOnTheBattlefield` with:

- `APlayerWouldPutAPermanentOnTheBattlefield(playerFilter, entrantTypeFilter)`.
- Exactly one `Opponent` symbol and one `ControlsNum` in the player's `And` list.
- `ControlsNum(GreaterThanOrEqualTo(TheNumberOfPermanentsOnTheBattlefield(
  And([typeFilters..., ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))]))), countedTypeFilter)`.
- Type filters are `IsCardtype`, `IsNonCardtype` and nonempty nested And/Or lists.
  The source count needs one controller clause and at least one type predicate.
- Exactly two operations, in order:
  `WouldPutPermanentOnBattlefield_PutPermanentOnBattlefield`, then
  `PlayerAction(WouldPutAPermanentOnBattlefield_ThatPlayer,
  SacrificeAPermanent(countedTypeFilter))`.
- The sacrifice filter has the same structural definition as the actor's count
  filter. Other predicates, players, comparisons, values, operations, resolving
  declarations and unbound references remain compile-time errors.

Semantic inventory records separate retained entry event, player predicate,
comparison, count, operation, actor and sacrifice roles, while reusing type and
player filter roles. Definitions validate player/value dependencies and a
permanent source. Factories allocate fresh card and ability IDs.

The entry context now carries the actor before replacements run. Direct entry
and singular/batch graveyard/exile returns keep explicit actors; callers without
a separate actor default to the entry controller. Existing event ActorID and
controller contracts are preserved. Matching counts the actor's current,
unphased controlled subjects before entry. The entrant does not count.
`CountPermanents(PermanentsControlledBy(You, filter))` reads the minimum in the
live source-controller frame. Existing isolated projection supplies entrant
types after copy replacements.

Each source visit and ability ID supplies a stable replacement identity.
Runtime abilities, source phasing, departure, face-down status and ability
removal govern availability. Execution rechecks after replacement choice. Once
applied, each proposed entrant saves its own actor and filter. Source departure
cannot erase that instruction. Cancelled entry discards the continuation.
Successful entry observations precede sacrifice. Batches register and observe
all entrants before any continuation. Nested retained sequences finish in reverse
replacement order. Copy-on-write access, including phased objects, consumes the
current visit's continuation without changing a clone. Permanent cloning copies
the continuation slice.

`SacrificeChosenBy` executes through `ApplyEffect` in a separate actor frame.
It reuses required permanent selection, exact visit binding, current control,
phasing, sacrifice replacement, ownership, zone batching and events. Single
candidates need no decision callback. A chosen returned card cannot supply an
old visit. The entrant is an eligible choice if the actor controls it. Caller
resolution bindings are restored. There is no new zone/cost system, global
last-action slot, card-name branch or gameplay declaration panic.

### Exact shape, engine ownership and dependencies

RON accepts top-level permanent rules
`NoMoreThanNumberCreaturesCanAttack(Integer(nonnegative))` and
`NoMoreThanNumberCreaturesCanBlock(Integer(nonnegative))`. It rejects symbols,
wrong arity, negative literals, raw literals, dynamic values, resolving actions
and conditional bodies. Inventory assigns each argument the numeric value role.
Factories construct fresh static declarations.

Engine APIs: `LimitAttackDeclarations(int) StaticRule` and
`LimitBlockDeclarations(int) StaticRule`. Definition validation requires a
battlefield source and a nonnegative limit. Shared continuous-effect activity
and exact printed declaration visits supply the source lifecycle. There is no
new cached rule registry, LKI service, cost system or global last-action slot.
The lowest active limit applies; zero permits no declarations. No limit removes
creatures already in combat or governs entry into combat without a declaration.

The capped attack planner counts independent printed and resolved requirements,
then uses stable proposal preference among equal weights. Current creature type,
control, phasing, tap status, summoning sickness, attack restrictions and Island
Sanctuary constrain eligibility. Omitted taxed attackers are not forced to pay.
Selected attackers retain existing payment and post-payment identity checks.
Uncapped caller behavior is retained.

The existing blocker planner bounds selected creature rows. Multi-blocking and
attacking-band pairs use one creature slot. Existing pairs remain fixed and
reserve distinct blocker slots. Evasion, capacity, minimum blocker counts and
maximum requirements remain shared contracts. Completion queries do not mutate
combat, player choices, RNG or source state. Shared lifecycle and effect cloning
keep departure, return, ability removal/restoration and clones independent.

Rules evidence: local CR 508.1a–d and 509.1a–c. Local `data/LEG.json`
confirms Caverns of Despair's exact two Oracle clauses, 2RR cost and World
Enchantment type. No source defect was found in Caverns of Despair. No RON source changed; vocabulary hashes need no refresh.
Sword of the Ages's documented artifact-exile omission remains deferred.
Go-card removal and unused DSL removal remain behind the existing cutover gate.

### Failing-first evidence and card-to-test mapping

RON gameplay tests first failed on unsupported
`NoMoreThanNumberCreaturesCanAttack`. Native tests first failed on missing
`LimitAttackDeclarations` and `LimitBlockDeclarations` APIs. Expanded attack
legality evidence then failed because an Island Sanctuary-barred requirement
could displace a legal flyer; the capped planner now checks that restriction
before ranking requirements. An initial factory test expected both numeric

### Exact contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

Engine API:

`SacrificeAnyMatchingCostInto(filter PermanentFilter, text string,
power *NumberBinding, cards *CardsBinding) Cost`.

RON supports one `SacrificeAnyNumberOfPermanents(filter)` producer in an ordinary
`Activated` or `ActivatedWithModifiers` cost, including a nested `And` cost list.
The filter has exactly one conjunctive
`ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))` clause. Supported characteristic
predicates supply other membership conditions. Missing, duplicate or alternative
controller clauses, repeated plural producers and invalid filters reject.
Casting, resolving and entry declarations retain their separate adapters.
Native result declarations require named, non-nil bindings and distinct producers;
unsupported native casting/resolution result contexts reject.

RON owns syntax validation, the scoped producer plan and fresh per-factory
`NumberBinding`/`CardsBinding` allocation. The engine owns selection, exact visit
checks, payment rollback, replacement processing, simultaneous movement and
saved facts. The ordinary action payment transaction locks a count and distinct
legal subjects on its validation game. Its existing preflight checks the complete
payment before live resources are spent. Zero is legal, including an empty
candidate set. Invalid answers fail. Present matching controlled subjects can
include the ability source. Return, phasing, changed control and changed
membership cannot substitute for a locked choice. Cost-list siblings keep their
existing payment order; the plural producer's subjects use one sacrifice batch.

The existing controller-sacrifice service now has a private completed-result
callback. Its former count and no-result callers retain their signatures and
behavior. Replacements and owner graveyard-order choices precede movement.
Token status and power are saved after those choices, from the complete
pre-movement battlefield. Negative power remains negative. Each successful
sacrifice saves its first resulting public-zone visit before deferred zone and
sacrifice events. Tokens add power but supply no retained card. Replacement
exile counts as payment; cancellation fails the whole transaction.

Existing transaction result maps publish facts only on success. Existing stack,
copy, clone and delayed frames transport them. `FromCards` enforces the captured
zone visit, so return cannot supply a prior card. Zero choices save zero and an
empty result. No new global last-action slot, mutable card-definition state,
Go-card fallback or partial production registry was added. No DSL function or
Go card definition was removed outside its cutover gate.

Rules evidence: local CR 601.2h, 602.2b, 701.21a and 400.7j. Local `data/LEG.json`
confirms Sword must exile the artifact as well as the creature cards; its RON
omits the artifact. Local `data/ATQ.json` confirms Gaea's Avenger must count
opponents' artifacts, whereas its RON uses You. Both source defects remain
explicit future work. No RON source changed; vocabulary source hashes need no
refresh. `inventory.go` now classifies the plural producer's filter in cost
context; the entry role is unchanged.

### Exact supported shape and reusable boundary

Native API:

`SacrificeSourceAndAnyMatchingCostInto(filter PermanentFilter, text string,
power *NumberBinding, cards *CardsBinding, source *CardBinding) Cost`.

RON groups one `SacrificePermanent(ThisPermanent)` with one
`SacrificeAnyNumberOfPermanents(filter)` in an `And` activation cost list,
including nested And lists. ActivatedWithModifiers uses the same cost path.
The optional filter keeps one conjunctive
`ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))` restriction and existing supported
characteristic predicates. Multiple source sacrifices, nonsource references,
ThisPermanent(), duplicate optional producers and malformed filters reject.
The mandatory source is a separate subject, not a member of the optional group.
Standalone plural costs retain their original source-inclusion behavior.

Each factory builds independent number, card-set and source-card bindings.
The RON plan owns syntax, filter validation and grouping. The engine owns the
mandatory source lock, choice bounds, distinct optional visits, movement and
result publication. Source identity is locked before mana payment. Current
control, presence, phasing and matching optional characteristics are checked
through the shared total payment. Zero optional subjects still sacrifice the
source, with zero power and an empty optional card set.

`controllersSacrificePermanentsResult` prepares all replacement and owner
ordering choices before movement, reads power from the complete battlefield,
and moves all members before observations with simultaneous departure LKI.
The source can supply a live static power bonus until the batch moves. Optional
power excludes the mandatory source. Nontokens save new graveyard or exile
visits; token subjects contribute optional power only. A token source saves no
card. Cancellation of either member fails the transaction without live partial
payment. Indestructible and regeneration do not stop sacrifice.

The existing payment transaction now publishes the separate source CardBinding
alongside optional NumberBinding/CardsBinding results. Existing FromNumber,
FromCards, FromCard, stack copies, game clones and delayed frames carry them.
Later payments, returned objects and characteristic changes cannot overwrite a
prior frame. Definition validation rejects duplicate source-result producers,
including a prior standalone source result followed by a combined producer.
Spell additional costs and resolving payment groups remain rejected contexts.
No new zone, replacement, layer, event or result-storage subsystem was added.

Rules evidence: local CR 601.2h, 602.2b, 701.21a, 400.7j and 608.2h. These
establish whole payment, activation timing, control/owner sacrifice movement,
public-zone continuation and object information. The native API deliberately
keeps mandatory and optional results separate; full Sword result interpretation
belongs to the pending consumer slice.

### Exact supported contract and reuse boundary

Top-level creature rules accept both CDA_Power(value) and CDA_Toughness(value),
with the same position-free value:

`Plus(Integer(n), TheNumberOfPermanentsOnTheBattlefield(filter))`

The fixed integer is the left operand and may be negative. Count filters reuse
the characteristic-safe leaf whitelist and nonempty nested And/Or. Controller
restrictions are conjunctive ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You)) or
ControlledByAPlayer(Opponent). Repeated identical restrictions are allowed;
incompatible restrictions and restrictions beneath Or reject. Other static
contexts keep their existing selector boundary. Dynamic offsets, reversed
operands, nested arithmetic, unequal axes, single-axis additive declarations,
noncreatures and resolving-action CDAs reject during compilation.

New engine signatures, all returning ContinuousEffect:

- `PTEqualsCountPlus(filter PermanentFilter, offset int)`
- `PTEqualsControlledCountPlus(filter PermanentFilter, offset int)`
- `PTEqualsOpponentCountPlus(filter PermanentFilter, offset int)`

These extend countCharacteristicPT with fixed offset and opponent scope.
CountBattlefield, characteristic filter matching, GetPlayer/GetOpponent,
CardPowerToughness, source-incarnation binding, layer reset, copy/clone support,
and departure snapshots remain shared services. Opponent scope checks that the
controller exists before selecting its opponent; the native unknown-owner test
first observed 4/4 instead of the required offset-only 1/1 and caught this need.
There is no second layer or zone store, mutable factory binding, card-name
execution branch, global result slot, runtime declaration panic or Go fallback.
Existing count and entry-result CDAs retain their behavior.

Owner supplies the all-zone context outside the battlefield and stack; spells
use their current controller. Battlefield control and type layers precede the
live 7a count. Ability removal restores printed values. Bonuses, counters and
switching apply after the CDA. Phased members do not count; phased sources keep
their saved values. Return binds a new source visit. Copies and clones keep
separate state. Departed source LKI retains final P/T; public-zone card queries
use current counts. These are pure static queries. Target announcement, new
payment results, delayed bindings, replacement ordering and simultaneous
operations are not added by this slice. Real casting failure still tests the
existing payment rollback boundary.

Rules evidence: local CR 208.2a, 604.3/604.3a and 613.4a–d were read. Existing
count-CDA contracts supply CR 109.5, 400.7 and 702.26b–d identity/context rules.

### Established contract and reuse boundary

Engine signatures:

- `IfRepeatedManaPaid(PlayerRef, ManaCost, ResolutionValue, ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`
- `UnlessRepeatedManaPaid(PlayerRef, ManaCost, ResolutionValue, ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`
- `PayRepeatedManaOrElse(PlayerRef, ManaCost, ResolutionValue, ResolvingEffect, ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`

RON signatures are `PayManaForEach(manaList, count)/2` inside
`MayCost(cost)/1` or `PlayerMayCost(player, cost)/2`. An adjacent nonempty
`If`/`Unless` or two-body `IfElse` consumes bare CostWasPaid/CostWasntPaid.
Fixed mana supports generic amounts and W/U/B/R/G. X, malformed lists and
negative generic operands reject. Counts reuse compileInstanceValue and its
binding checks: fixed nonnegative integers, typed counter information and
existing resolving arithmetic/values. Negative dynamic counts become zero.
Casting/activation costs, mandatory payments, entry and replacement contexts
remain outside this adapter. Conditions cannot escape their continuation.

Extend the existing resolutionManaPayment declaration. Read the count once
before the offer and multiply every component into one complete cost. Zero
requires acceptance. Overflow fails before choices or spending. Reuse
unlessPaidEffect, ManaCostPayment, mana spending policies, the mana solver and
shared action-payment transaction. Decline or failure selects the unpaid body;
activation reductions do not apply. The payment does not save a global result.
Continuation values are read when their own actions execute, so Cyclone damage
uses its counter count after payment, separately from its saved payment cost.

Definition inspection validates typed operands and traverses both branches.
Properties combine both continuations. Waiting delayed queries include the
payer, count and both bodies without reading amounts or making choices.
Existing source references supply live, departure and phase information for
exact visits. Return cannot replace a source. Copies retain their own payer;
clones keep independent mana, counters and pending frames. Existing counter and
damage replacement/batch services own their rules; no second subsystem was added.

Local CR 118.2–3, 118.5 and 605.3a–b were read for complete payment, zero
acknowledgment and resolution mana abilities. Existing exact-information
contracts supply CR 400.7 and 608.2h. Local data/ARN.json Oracle text matches the
complete Cyclone RON requirements. No source-data defect or RON edit was needed.
Vocabulary syntax, all source hashes and occurrence counts are unchanged; only
its loader baseline is refreshed, removing Cyclone's former rejection.

### Established signatures and contexts

Engine APIs:

- `PayChosenManaInto(player PlayerRef, result *NumberBinding) ResolvingEffect`.
  Resolves the specified player, chooses nonnegative generic mana, and publishes
  the actual successful payment. Zero, absent payer, invalid input and failed
  payment clear the result. Amount choice is the optional decision; there is no
  second may-pay offer. Shared transactions keep complete payment, mana abilities,
  spending restrictions and rollback. Activation reductions do not apply.
- `NonnegativeNumberChooser` with `ChooseNonnegativeNumber(reason string) int` is
  an optional typed direct-input interface. Existing Player callers are preserved.
  Without direct input, shared bounded choices select finish or append a digit.
  Digit limits prevent integer overflow. The supported range is the engine's
  nonnegative integer representation, with no damage or current-pool bound.
- `DealDamageWithPreventionFrom(source DamageSourceRef, recipient
  DamageRecipientRef, amount ResolutionValue, prevention ResolutionValue)
  ResolvingEffect`. Extends the existing singular damage effect. One local
  prevention candidate participates in shared affected-player ordering, rechecks
  and redirection. It applies once and leaves no shield or global replacement.
  Nonpositive damage has no event; nonpositive prevention changes nothing.
  Prevention prohibitions use the existing engine service.

RON shapes in ordinary resolving ActionList sequences:

- bare symbol `PayAnyAmountOfMana`, or direct
  `PlayerAction(playerRef, PayAnyAmountOfMana)`;
- bare `AmountOfManaPaidThisWay` after a local producer;
- `PermanentDealsDamageAndPreventSomeOfIt(permanentRef, value,
  singularRecipient, preventionValue)`, using existing typed permanent,
  recipient and instance-value adapters.

Every producer owns a fresh per-factory NumberBinding and exports it only to
its lexical continuation. The latest local producer supplies subsequent reads;
branch-local producers cannot escape. Copies, cloned resolutions and delayed
captures use existing number frames. Entry, replacement, casting/activation
payment contexts and PlayerActions list adapters stay separate. Malformed tuple
spellings, unbound reads, invalid player/permanent references and plural recipients
reject at compilation/definition validation. No game-time declaration panic,
card-name branch, Go-card fallback or partial production registry was introduced.

Shared services reused: compilePlayerRef, compilePermanentRef,
compileDamagePacketRecipient, compileInstanceValue, compileActionSequence;
NumberBinding, existing frame capture/clone services; tryResolutionCostPayment,
action payment transactions, mana solver and spending policies; damageFromEffect,
singular damage outcomes, replacementCandidates and shared prevention ordering.
Private replacement/damage methods accept optional local candidates and retain
all current callers. Waiting delayed declarations include payer, damage source,
recipient and both values without making choices or reading amounts.

Local CR 118.2–3, 118.5, 605.3a–b, 615.1–12 and 616.1–2 were read. Existing
CR 400.7/608.2h exact source-information contracts supply LKI and phase behavior.
