### Contract, signatures and reuse boundary

RON supports exactly `PayManaCostOfPermanent(ThisPermanent)` or, in an Aura,
`PayManaCostOfPermanent(HostPermanent)` in ordinary nonmana `Activated` and
`ActivatedWithModifiers` cost slots, directly or within a cost `And`.
`compilePermanentManaCost(Node, scope)` uses `compilePermanentRef`, permits
only source/host reference kinds, and builds a fresh engine cost per factory.
Targets, event/choice/loop references, plural subjects, bad arity and tuple
reference spellings reject. Casting, entry, resolving, grant and mana-producing
contexts remain explicit adapter gaps. A new test first demonstrated that a
mana-producing body was accepted; it now rejects before declaration lowering
because its dynamic cost needs separate mana-solver metadata.

Engine API: `PermanentManaCostPayment(subject PermanentRef) Cost`.
`lockPermanentManaCosts([]Cost, sourceID, controller uuid.UUID, *Game)
([]Cost, error)` converts dynamic components to fixed ManaCostPayment values
for both ActionDefinition.CanActivate and prepareActionPaymentTransaction.
The source and subject must be present and unphased at the read. Source
incarnation and attachment incarnation use existing typed-reference services.
Payment cannot use LKI. Copy characteristics, including permanent-spell copies,
supply the cost. Face-down objects and absent costs are unpayable; `{0}` is
payable. Every X is zero. The cost declaration has no mutable chosen state.

Read and lock precede shared payment choices and mana production. Subsequent
host departure, reattachment or cost changes cannot replace the locked total.
The next activation reads again. All mana components join one total before
activation increases/reductions and affordability checks. This prevents reuse
of one mana for two components. Existing aggregation owns the hybrid array.
No new mana solver, spending, zone, counter, untap or replacement service exists.
Shared mana planning, total-cost validation and commit rollback remain owners.
Stack copies do not repay; pending effects retain the exact source visit.
Clones and factory instances keep separate zones, resources and counters.

Dependencies reused: PermanentRef, This, AttachedPermanent, EffectContext source
capture, ManaCostPayment, addActionManaCost, modifyActivationManaCost,
CanAfford, prepareActionPaymentTransaction, lockPaymentCostsWithManaPolicy,
prepareCostPaymentTransaction, mana planning, shared payment rollback and
existing definition inspection. All current callers retain their signatures.

### Contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

Engine API:
`PreventDamageCausedByTargetingThisTurn(subject PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect`.
It saves the present, unphased subject visit and installs unlimited prevention
until cleanup. Definition inspection validates its typed reference. The rule
survives its installing source's departure and does not follow a returned subject.
A phase cycle keeps the saved visit. Waiting prevention queries expose that visit
without damage, choices or installation.

RON resolving action lists accept exactly:

```text
CreatePreventDamageUntil(
  ASpellOrAbilityWouldCauseASourceToDealDamageToRecipient(
    TargetsPermanent(permanentRef), AnyDamageSource, Permanent(permanentRef)),
  [PreventThatDamage], UntilEndOfTurn)
```

Both references must lower to the same singular typed plan. Existing lexical
source, host, target and event/result binding checks apply. Different plans,
unbound references, other source/cause filters, recipient kinds, operations and
durations reject. The compiler owns spelling, arity, scope and lowering.
Inventory assigns a separate `damage_cause_filter` role. No entry or payment
adapter was added.

`ResolutionState.Begin` saves a typed internal `damageCause` with stack ID and
exact permanent target visits for either a spell or ability. It does not change
`DamageSource` identity, characteristics, controller or LKI. A spell can make a
different permanent deal damage. All prepared single and simultaneous damage
packets save their cause before replacement choices. Common replacement paths
and selected-source batch redirection retain it when an action changes amount
or recipient. The shared prevention matcher then rechecks both cause and current
recipient. Combat and damage without a resolving stack frame supply no cause.
Snapshots and clones copy target arrays; clearing the frame clears the cause.
Copies keep separate stack identities and their own targets.

Dependencies reused: PermanentRef plans and instance bindings, capturedPermanent,
ResolutionState/StackObject target incarnation maps, existing damage assignments,
DamageSystem, damagePreventionRuleReplacement, EffectManager replacement choice
and rechecks, batch prevention, selected-source redirection, shared prevention
prohibitions, cleanup, waiting-reference and delayed source-read services.
No parallel damage, payment, zone, source-LKI or replacement-order service was
added. Existing callers keep their signatures. No Go-card fallback, card-name
branch, global last-action result, runtime declaration panic or partial registry
was added. No DSL export or Go card definition was removed.

### Exact supported contract and engine reuse

Engine signatures:

- `TargetHasSubtype(subtype string) PermanentTargetOption`
- `TargetRequiredSubtypes(target Target) []string`

The option enforces one permanent subtype and saves that requirement in private
immutable target data. Distinct requirements apply together; duplicates appear
once in declaration order. Returned lists are independent. An empty result
means no proof is supplied, not that the target domain is unrestricted.
Opaque filters, negative predicates and disjunctions do not supply positive
constraints. No domain is inferred from the battlefield or chosen UUIDs.

RON lowers `IsCreatureType(symbol)` in permanent target filters, directly or
within nested And, through existing name normalization to the typed option.
Singular, fixed-count and X-count target groups use it. Existing controller,
card-type, combat and other filters remain conjunctive restrictions. The
predicate keeps its prior subtype semantics; no extra card-type test is added.
IsNonCreatureType, Or, Aura enchant filters and other contexts keep their
existing behavior. Malformed forms and incompatible spell-filter/action uses
reject. CanTargetOnly still rejects in production contexts.

Selection and resolution use current subtypes. The declaration stays fixed
through subtype changes, target departure/return, phasing and source sacrifice.
Existing visit and phasing checks control actions. Copies, clones, factory
instances and count/random wrappers preserve the constraint without sharing
mutable query results. Zero-choice groups retain their declaration. A future
whole-domain consumer must read all applicable declarations; aligned selected
TargetSpecs alone omit groups with zero chosen targets.

RON owns spelling, tuple/symbol validation and lowering. The engine owns the

### Implementation, signatures and reuse boundary

New engine APIs:

- `(*Game).AbilityTargetSource(card Card, ability Ability, declared []Target) Card`
- `TargetSourceAbility(source Card) (id uuid.UUID, declared []Target, known bool)`

The source-information view keeps a saved declaration ID and separate target
list. Input and returned slices cannot change that list. Empty known lists
remain distinct from absent identity. Nil/zero-ID inputs and spell/static
abilities cannot create a new ability view. Target specifications retain their
existing ownership contract. Stack object IDs distinguish executions; source
incarnation identity remains with the shared information view. No new global
last-action slot or card-specific executor exists.

Integration covers ordinary/grouped/modal activations, cost-time target
validation and forced/random/opponent target choices, target-dependent
CanActivate queries, ordinary/modal pending triggers, delayed declarations,
ability-copy retargeting, game clones, mana resolution bodies and interactive
snapshot/heuristic/search queries. Delayed scheduling assigns a declaration ID
once; queries do not allocate an identity or make a choice. Copied targets keep
announced counts. Legacy copy callers without a saved view retain their path.

The initial source wrapper exposed printed colors during announcement. A new
regression assertion failed when a source changed to blue could target a
creature with protection from blue. The correction uses the existing current
source-characteristic and exact LKI service. Resolution retains ability facts
while replacing source characteristics with current/phase/departure facts.
Returned sources cannot supply the former visit's characteristics.

The graveyard activation caller omitted target validation and aligned resolution
specs. A new regression assertion, with its source bound through the existing
lookup API, failed because an illegal target paid the exile cost. This slice

Contract stated before editing: retain and enforce immutable positive/negative

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

Engine APIs:

- `PermanentTargetDomain`, with private immutable fields.
- `SubtypeDomain(string) PermanentTargetDomain` and
  `NonSubtypeDomain(string) PermanentTargetDomain`.
- `AllPermanentDomains(...PermanentTargetDomain) PermanentTargetDomain` and
  `AnyPermanentDomain(...PermanentTargetDomain) PermanentTargetDomain`.
- `UnknownPermanentDomain() PermanentTargetDomain`.
- `TargetWithDomain(PermanentTargetDomain) PermanentTargetOption`.
- `TargetRequiresSubtype(Target, string) bool`.

`ron` owns the AST adapter `compileTargetSubtypeDomain(Node)` and validates
`IsCreatureType(symbol)`, `IsNonCreatureType(symbol)` and nonempty nested
`And([..])` / `Or([..])` in supported permanent target and EnchantPermanent
contexts. Other supported filters supply unknown leaves and keep their existing
live predicates and typed options. Existing RON subtype normalization applies.
This adds no implicit creature card-type restriction. Land/enchantment subtype
predicates and nonpermanent/union-recipient declarations supply no creature
subtype proof. Fixed creature/land Aura markers retain their existing behavior.

`mage` owns enforcement and proof. Existing TargetHasSubtype constraints join
the immutable formula. Subtype assignments permit multiple subtypes per permanent;
negative predicates can eliminate union branches. Contradictory subtype formulas
supply no proof. False is absence of proof, not proof of a nonmatching domain.
The query has no game parameter, runtime filter evaluation, choices, LKI reads,
resource changes or randomness. Constructors copy input slices.

PermanentTarget.Possible and Filter enforce the domains even if additional
public filters are replaced. Bindings, fixed/X counts, zero-choice groups, random
and opponent-choice wrappers retain them. Definition validation traverses domains
through count wrappers. Existing attachment checks use Filter and do not target
an attached host. Typed Aura bindings require UnwrapTarget to accept bindings;
land Aura spell/object text checks now use that shared adapter. Spell text
compatibility retains exact domain structure. Existing source-relative options,
resolution visit checks, copies, clones and target protections remain in charge.

Rules evidence: local CR 115.1a–d, 115.3, 115.6, 115.8 and 303.4a–d establish
separate declarations, count/mode behavior, Aura targets and attachment legality.
No new payment, LKI, event ordering, replacement or simultaneous-operation
contract was needed. Whole-spell/ability CanTargetOnly consumers are still gated.

### Contract, boundaries and engine reuse

New engine API:

```go
func NewCreatedTokenLink() *CreatedTokenLink
func CreateTokenCopiesLinked(player PlayerRef, count ResolutionValue,
    token TokenDefinition, link *CreatedTokenLink) ResolvingEffect
func TokensCreatedWith(link *CreatedTokenLink, source PermanentRef) PermanentSet
```

One immutable declaration identifies the producing ability group. Each accepted
token saves that declaration and the source's exact captured battlefield visit
before entry observations. Repeated creation accumulates members; zero adds none
and does not clear previous members. A different declaration or source visit
selects a different group. Current collections exclude phased and departed tokens.
Source departure, phasing and controller changes do not clear the saved group.
Return supplies a new source visit. Pending and delayed resolutions can still
create/read tokens for the old visit. Copied activations use their own resolving
controller for token ownership but retain the original source group. Card copies
of tokens do not inherit creation history. Scalar history fields are copied by
`clonePermanentInto`, including copy-on-write mutations in either game branch.

RON scans the source's rules for one `CreateTokens/2` producer and a strict symbol
`TheCreatedTokens`. It stops at token instructions because token abilities have
their own source scope. Missing/ambiguous producers and spell sources reject.
Existing supported creature-token syntax and modifiers remain strict. A linked
producer lowers to `CreateTokenCopiesLinked`; resolving contextual collections
lower to `TokensCreatedWith(link, This)`, including
`Exile([EachPermanent(TheCreatedTokens)], [])`. Entry, static and replacement-body
collections remain rejected. Native link declarations reject nil/zero links and
missing operands during definition validation. Runtime data stays in the game,
not in the immutable declaration or compiler plan.

Reused shared definition factories, ability cloning, token construction, entry
replacement and batch observation, source information identities, stack/copy
frames, contextual collections, simultaneous exile and waiting-source services.
Added source-read integration for linked producers and collection consumers.
`CreatedByFilter`/`Permanent.CreatedBy` cannot distinguish source visits or two
producer declarations, so they cannot implement this contract. Existing callers
and lexical `CreatedTokensBinding`/`PermanentSetBinding` behavior are unchanged.
No global result slot, card-name executor, production fallback, partial registry,
new payment subsystem or target legality rule was added.

The action reads the creator and count, resolves an exact present unphased
subject, captures immutable copiable values, then builds all independent token
cards before the existing simultaneous entry batch. Nil operands and invalid
required links fail definition validation. Missing creators, unavailable subjects
and nonpositive counts create nothing. Unknown provenance returns an error;
builder errors cannot install a partial batch. Counters, ordinary layers, owner,

transfer. Mana costs and previously established copy exceptions do transfer.

source departure. Return cannot replace the maker visit or copied subject visit.

maker visit and use their resolving controller. Clones retain separate token
state. Waiting queries declare source reads without building or creating tokens.

the existing `NumberTokens(value, token)` wrapper and player scopes.

modifiers, unbound references, wrong arity, static/cost/entry operations and
lexical result consumers remain rejected. Inventory descends into the reference
and modification roles without claiming gameplay support.

  controller. A copied damage spell or a later cast cannot inherit the rule.

inventory descendant roles. Native APIs established here:

### Exact contracts, dependencies and boundaries

New native `ControllerControls(filter PermanentFilter) PermanentFilter` delegates
to the existing `PlayerControls` state query. It checks a present subject's
current controller, present unphased membership and current characteristics.
Absent games, subjects and players cannot match. It saves no choices or state.
`PlayerControls(player PlayerRef, filter PermanentFilter) StateCondition` now
accepts `CombatDefendingPlayer()`. Effect and state reads share the same pure
combat-player resolver, which supplies no player outside two-player combat.
Existing `CantAttackIf(This, condition)` performs the check at declaration,
after power/toughness layers. Layer 6 does not cache incomplete power values.

RON supports `ControlledByAPlayer(ControlsA(propertyFilter))` in permanent target
filters, including conjunctions with ordinary target restrictions. Selection and
resolution both read current control. The predicate does not become a resolved
control effect's duration. RON also supports the source-only static shape
`PermanentRuleEffect(ThisPermanent, [CantAttackIfDefendingPlayer(
PlayerPassesFilter(DefendingPlayer, ControlsA(propertyFilter)))])`.
Both contexts reuse the existing reference-free property filter grammar,
including nonempty And/Or and fixed power/toughness comparisons. Bad arity,
references in property filters, chosen colors, dynamic source bounds, wrong
player and host-source declarations reject before execution. The existing
positive land-dependent attack rule remains unchanged.

Reuse includes permanent target visit checks and resolution legality, activation
payment/rollback, source-bound control durations, static printed-rule lifecycle,
state-trigger arming, current layers, phasing, definition validation, copies and
clone isolation. There are no new mutable bindings, global action slots, card
name branches, parallel engine services or partial production registries.
No existing caller was removed. Runtime/Go-definition/DSL removal gates remain
closed. No unused-DSL deletion was attempted without the required caller audit.

### Exact contracts, dependencies and boundaries

Native `RegenerateInsteadOfDestroy() Ability` reads the source's current runtime
abilities when destruction is proposed. Candidate identity is cached on that
action by permanent visit and ability declaration. Source phasing, face-down
status, departure and ability removal stop it. No-regeneration destruction and
current regeneration prohibitions exclude it. Each eligible destruction uses the
same native tap, damage removal and combat removal service as existing shields;
the static rule is not consumed. This is CR 614.8 and 701.19b, not a new shield.

Native `ReplaceNextDestructionThisTurn(subject PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect`
saves one present subject visit. It cancels one destruction and removes damage
and the deathtouch flag without tapping or combat removal. It survives source
exit and ignores regeneration prohibitions. Indestructible blocks destruction
before consumption; sacrifice and zero-toughness moves are not destruction.
Phasing suspends matching; return cannot supply an old visit. Cleanup expires
it. Shared waiting persistent reference queries now expose its saved subject,
including departure facts. Copies and clones keep separate consumption state.

RON accepts exactly `ReplaceWouldDestroy(PermanentWouldBeDestroyed(ThisPermanent),
[RegeneratePermanent(WouldBeDestroyed_ThatPermanent)])` at permanent rule scope,
and resolving `CreateFutureReplaceWouldDestroy(
NextTimePermanentWouldBeDestroyedThisTurn(ref), [CancelDestroy,
RemoveAllDamageFromPermanent(WouldBeDestroyed_ThatPermanent)])` with existing
singular typed references. The event reference is checked locally, not added as
a general resolving reference. Malformed arity, symbols, subjects, operation
lists and unrelated contexts reject before execution. RON spelling stays in ron;
engine mechanics contain no card-name branches or global result slots.

`OnlyOtherPlayersMayActivate(Opponent)` lowers to existing `WithAnyPlayerMay()`
and `WithActivationStateCondition(NotCondition(PlayerIsPermanentController(This)))`.
The current source controller determines permission; the activator pays. Other
filters and duplicate permissions reject. Existing target visits, per-instance
bindings, source resolution, payment rollback, printed definition reconstruction,
replacement choices/rechecks and simultaneous destruction are reused.

Local Oracle data in `data/ARN.json` and `data/LEG.json` confirms both records.
Rules read: CR 701.8, 701.19a–c, 614.8 and 616.1; identity/phasing and target
contracts use existing CR 400.7, 601.2c, 608.2b and 702.26 behavior. No source
defect or environment failure was found. RON hashes remain unchanged, so no
vocabulary snapshot refresh was required. Existing callers remain. No Go-card
or unused-DSL removal gate is open; no functions were deleted without an audit.

### Failing-first evidence and gameplay mapping

Native tests first failed compilation for the two missing APIs, after fixing

failed at unsupported ReplaceWouldDestroy and CreateFutureReplaceWouldDestroy.
Later failures exposed Clergy's missing permission adapter and the missing saved

### Contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

Engine signatures:

- `TargetPowerLessThanOrEqualToSourcePower() PermanentTargetOption`.
- `GainControlWhileSourceTappedAndPowerLE(subject PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect`.
- `GainControlEachWhileSourceControlled(subjects PermanentSet) ResolvingEffect`.

Target legality reads current powers, including equality and negative values.
The existing exact source-information service supplies LKI after departure or
phasing; returned sources cannot replace it. Illegal announcements consume no
payment. Power control requires a present, unphased tapped source and subject
at resolution. It saves the source/subject visits and resolving controller.
Source control changes and ability removal do not end it. Untapping, source
absence, subject absence or a failed power comparison end it permanently.
Subject phasing ends this subject-dependent duration under CR 702.26f.

The native `ControlTargetPowerLESource` condition previously read reset P/T in
Layer 2. Control-layer evaluation now defers that condition until all layers
complete. A failed endpoint expires permanently and repeats the layer pass
before control bookkeeping and state-trigger observations. Each repeat expires
at least one effect. Normal `IsActive` queries retain full condition checks.
This corrects existing native callers without replacing control reconciliation.

Plural control captures distinct present, unphased members at resolution before
installing all effects and reconciling layers once. It saves the exact source,
subject visits and resolving controller. Later entries, combat removal or filter
changes cannot add members. Source loss of control, phasing or departure ends
all captured durations. Target phasing preserves this source-only duration;
return cannot inherit it. Copies and clones retain independent frames/state.
Source phase and untap hooks keep latched endpoints through immediate returns.

RON exact contexts:

- `PowerIs(LessThanOrEqualTo(PowerOfPermanent(ThisPermanent)))` in a
  permanent-source permanent target, directly or in existing conjunctions.
- `GainControlOfPermanentUntil(subject, Or([
  ForAsLongAsPermanentRemainsTapped(ThisPermanent),
  UntilPermanentNoLongerPassesFilter(subject,
  PowerIs(LessThanOrEqualTo(PowerOfPermanent(ThisPermanent))))]))`.
  Endpoint order is free; exactly one of each and the same typed subject are
  required.
- `GainControlOfEachPermanentUntil(collection,
  UntilPermanentChangesControl(You, ThisPermanent))`, using existing contextual
  permanent collections.

Both resolving forms require ordinary permanent-source bodies. Other endpoint
forms, power references, comparisons and plural durations reject. Static, cost,
entry, spell-source and draw-replacement contexts gain no support. RON owns
syntax, scope and diagnostics. Mage owns reusable mechanics. Existing typed
references, targets, source LKI, per-instance factories, control timestamps,
control prohibitions, combat removal, summoning sickness, optional untap/stun,

RON accepts exactly this operation sequence in an ordinary spell resolving body:

```ron
ChooseADamageSource(AnyDamageSource),
CreateFutureReplaceWouldDealDamage(
    NextTimeDamageWouldBeDealtThisTurnBySourceToRecipient(
        TheChosenDamageSource, Player(You)),
    [ContinueDealingDamage,
     SpellDealsDamage(ThisSpell, WouldDealDamage_ThatMuchDamage,
         Player(WouldDealDamage_ControllerOfDamageSource))])
```

The event player uses existing typed player references and the choice uses existing
source-filter forms. The source choice must dominate the consumer. Continuation,
spell, proposed amount and source-controller operands are strict symbols. Operations
must have that exact order and count. Proposed operands cannot escape their event.
Permanent-source, source-zone, entry, delayed and draw-replacement contexts reject.
Other bounded events, operations and destinations reject. Existing selected-source
permanent-to-player redirection remains supported.

RON owns spelling, arity, context, lexical scope, fresh factory bindings and semantic
inventory roles. Mage owns saved exact source/spell information, event expansion,
replacement ordering/rechecks, packet identity, damage execution and cloning. It
reuses selected permanent-spell continuation, current/retained source information,
player choices, CR 609.7a source enumeration, cleanup and shared damage batches.
No card-name branch, Go factory fallback, global result slot or partial registry.

### Supported contract, boundaries and source evidence

RON accepts `ActionForEachPermanent(collection, [actions])` in ordinary resolving
spell, activation, trigger and delayed bodies. `EachablePermanent` is a strict
symbol bound only inside the body. The collection uses the enclosing scope;
nested bodies shadow and restore the member. Malformed forms, missing bindings,
escaped choices, member reads in new ability declarations, entry operations and
draw replacements reject. Existing contextual collection and action grammars
remain responsible for their nested declarations. Each factory gets fresh bindings.

Native API: `ForEachInTurnOrder(PermanentSet, *PermanentBinding, ResolvingEffect)
ResolvingEffect`. Mage captures distinct present, unphased visits once in APNAP
control groups. The resolving controller chooses order within each group before
body execution. Invalid choices use the first remaining member. Sequential body
actions keep their normal payment, replacement and observation contracts; this
is not a simultaneous batch. `ForEach` retains its existing battlefield order.

The shared executor now isolates plural-card, spell, mana-type, damage-source,
plural-damage-result and singular-damage-result maps, in addition to its existing
maps. Deep copies and deferred restoration preserve outer values on success or
error. Later entries do not join; return cannot supply a saved incarnation.
Phasing suspends permanent actions; changed control does not remove a member.
Exact LKI supplies departed-member information. Delayed effects save each member.
Both loop constructors declare source reads in collections and bodies without
running selectors, values, decisions or actions. Copies and clones remain separate.

Reuse: `controlledPermanentGroups`, `PermanentBinding`, `ForEach`, contextual
collections, shared optional-payment transactions/mana abilities, combat-pair
collections, temporary keyword layers, delayed capture and source-read services.
RON owns syntax, scope, inventory roles and lowering; mage owns rules and state.

### Supported shape and reuse boundary

`LifeTotalOfPlayer(playerRef)` takes exactly one typed player reference in an
ordinary resolving spell, activation, trigger or delayed body. It lowers to
`LifeTotalOf(subject PlayerRef) ResolutionValue`. Each instruction reads current
life; negative totals remain available to arithmetic. `HalfRoundedDown` and
`HalfRoundedUp` use the existing integer rounding services.

`LoseLife_ThatPlayer` is a strict symbol available only within the amount of its
own `LoseLife` instruction. A fresh plan and `PlayerBinding` identify that
instruction. When the amount uses the symbol, the factory lowers to:

`Sequence(SnapshotPlayer(explicitSubject, binding),
LoseLifeFor(FromPlayer(binding), amount))`.

Existing exact signatures are `SnapshotPlayer(PlayerRef, *PlayerBinding)
ResolvingEffect`, `FromPlayer(*PlayerBinding) PlayerRef`,
`LoseLifeFor(PlayerRef, ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect` and
`GainLifeFor(PlayerRef, ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect`. No native API was
added or changed. `SnapshotPlayer` selects the subject once and clears absent
subjects. Life actions use shared restrictions, replacements, history and
events. Nonpositive amounts do nothing; this is not damage, life payment, or
setting a life total. Unchanged life instructions retain their original lowering.

The compiler owns RON spelling, arity, ordinary-value context and local scope.
The engine supplies player snapshots, life totals, rounding, source identity,
LKI, phasing and copy/clone frames. Each factory gets separate target and local
subject bindings. Later actions cannot read the life-loss subject. Typed player
references can read enclosing targets and `ActionPlayer` only with their
existing producers. Entry, draw replacement, payment and static contexts reject;
existing event-player life-action restrictions are preserved.

source visits without choosing a player or reading life. The native test checks
absent-subject clearing in the same resolution frame, so a fresh frame cannot

### Exact supported shape and engine boundary

RON accepts `WasTappedToPayForAbilitiesOfPermanent(permanentRef)`, exactly one
typed source/attachment/singular-target/saved-event reference in an ordinary
resolving permanent collection. It composes with existing collection `And` and
`Or` operations. The complete card uses
`And([IsCreatureType(Merfolk), WasTappedToPayForAbilitiesOfPermanent(Trigger_ThatPermanent)])`
in its bound source-death trigger. Arity, reference type, scope and context
checks stay in `ron`. Entry, static, target and payment-filter contexts reject.
No source spelling changed.

New native signature:
`TappedForAbilitiesThisTurn(source PermanentRef) PermanentSet`.
The query reads current-turn activation payment history by exact source and
payer battlefield visits. It returns present, unphased members once each.
Current type restrictions stay in the existing collection intersection.
Source death, return, control changes or ability removal cannot rewrite old
payment facts. Payer return cannot supply the paid visit. Phasing preserves
identity but hides members during the query. Repeated payments do not duplicate
members. Shared cleanup resets history; clones copy its map independently.

The existing payment transaction retains actual tap subjects from tap-symbol,
matching, multiple, attached and exact-subject costs. A successful battlefield
activation publishes them for its exact source. Costs paid during resolution
and ordinary tap actions do not publish activation history. Direct/planned
mana paths retain their source tap as a payment, including zero production.
Preparation and failed total payments do not publish history. Copies do not
pay again. No mutable declaration state or global last-action slot was added.

The source-death event already saves `Trigger_ThatPermanent` in a fresh typed
binding; that adapter was reused. General permanent-information identities keep
saved subjects readable after departure without making them legal action
subjects. Shared collection, destruction, replacement, regeneration, trigger
copy, delayed-source query and clone services supply the rest. Waiting-query
inspection now traverses the new typed set without execution. API and rules
contracts document only this established context.

### Source defect and rules evidence

`cards/mtgish/ATQ.lines.ron:51` used `ThePermanentTappedThisWay` as the subject of

### Supported signature, context and engine boundary

RON accepts exactly:

```ron
CreatePermanentRuleEffectUntil(
    Ref_TargetPermanent,
    [DoesntUntapDuringControllersUntap],
    ForAsLongAsPermanentRemainsTapped(ThisPermanent),
)
```

The subject uses existing typed singular permanent references. The operation
is one strict symbol. The duration has one typed reference to the resolving
battlefield source. This adapter is limited to ordinary permanent-source
resolving bodies. Wrong arity, tuple aliases, mixed operations, unbound or
player references, other duration endpoints, entry, costs and spell-only
source contexts reject. Static untap rules keep their separate existing path.
`ThePermanentTappedThisWay` remains unsupported; it is not a target alias.

Native API: `PreventUntapWhileSourceTapped(subject PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect`.
Resolution requires a present, unphased, tapped source and a present, unphased
subject. It saves both visits and installs `capturedTappedUntapRule` in the
shared effect manager. The shared untap decision service checks this rule
before selecting simultaneous untaps. This is a game rule, not an ability grant
or a characteristic change. Other untap effects can untap the subject.

Existing source untap and phase notifications expire the rule permanently.
Departure removes it; a returned source cannot restart it. A replacement that
keeps the source tapped, such as stun, preserves the duration. Source control
changes and source/subject ability removal do not end it. Subject phasing keeps
the rule; departure/return cannot substitute for the saved visit. A clone copies
the expiration latch. Stack copies install separate restrictions and do not pay
again. Waiting delayed-source queries retain the exact source without execution.
No cost, damage, replacement-order or simultaneous-operation service changed.

subjects and event-local bindings stay unchanged. Tuple aliases, arguments,
duplicate damage-history symbols and missing creature domains reject.

Native API: `WasDealtDamageThisTurn PermanentFilter`. It requires a present,
unphased exact visit and tests `DamageSystem.turnDamageRecipients`, keyed by

and its callers remain unchanged. That ID-only tracker cannot safely supply

also cannot supply spell recipients without a battlefield source incarnation.

The shared final damage executor records positive actual damage to its exact
recipient before damage observations. Prevention, redirection, source facts

simultaneous recipients are recorded before any batch observations. Regeneration,

subject; a phase cycle preserves its visit. Return cannot supply an old visit.
Final turn cleanup clears the history, including phased recipients. Cleanup
priority retains it. Clones copy the map, including independent later writes.

Combat-pair detection reads the opposing visit once. Later damage does not
create a missed trigger. Opponent departure after detection does not cancel a
queued self-boost. Source return cannot receive an old self-boost. Existing
source captures, pending trigger frames, stack copies, layers, ability removal
and cleanup supply these behaviors. There is no new binding, decision, cost,
replacement ordering, APNAP or LKI mechanism. No declaration panic, global

### Implemented contract and reuse boundary

groups. Other target shapes and disjunction need separate adapters.

The option retains an immutable typed declaration reference, not a chosen ID.

### Contract, boundaries and implementation

Supported resolving shape:
`CreatePermanentLayerEffect(permanentRef, [AddAbility([ability, ...]), ...])`,
with only the following abilities in this new branch:

- `If(condition, [PermanentRuleEffect(ThisPermanent,
  [DoesntUntapDuringControllersUntap])])`. The condition uses the existing
  static-condition grammar in a fresh permanent-source scope.
- `TriggerA(AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersUpkeep(SinglePlayer(You)), body)`.
  The body uses the existing action grammar in a fresh permanent-source scope.

The outer recipient uses existing typed enclosing bindings. Each granted body
has its own scope: ThisPermanent is the recipient, You is its controller, and
outer targets and donor attachments cannot leak inward. Entry and draw
replacement bodies reject this branch. Other trigger events, acquired rules,
mixed modifications and durations remain unsupported by this branch. Existing
keyword, activated and Aura-host acquisition adapters are preserved.

Native signatures are unchanged:
`AcquireStaticAbility(PermanentRef, StaticRule) ResolvingEffect` now also accepts
`PreventUntapDuringStep(PermanentRef, StateCondition) StaticRule`.
The nested definition gets the existing fresh binding and battlefield context.
Nil or unbound rule children fail definition validation. Existing continuous
acquisition restrictions remain intact.

### Supported shapes, dependencies and boundaries

targets, X, arithmetic, tuple aliases and mixed operation lists reject here.

New native signature: `LoseLifeAsEnters(amount ResolutionValue) Ability`.
Its definition retains the typed amount and requires a battlefield source.
Nil amounts, nil players and unbound bindings fail definition validation.
Each factory has a fresh ability; each entry has separate replacement identities.
The shared entry candidate cache uses declaration provenance and the loss-rule
index so competing replacements cannot repeat a loss. Copy replacements run
first and can remove the original rule or supply newly acquired loss rules.

RON owns spelling, arity, entry-value restrictions and inventory roles. The
engine owns the typed entry context, live life read, exact entry visit, default
replacement priority, affected-player ordering, rechecks and event processing.
`LifeTotalOf`, `Game.PlayerLoseLife`, battlefield entry preparation, copy
builders, batch registration and game clones are reused. Loss is independent
of damage prevention. Nonpositive amounts do nothing. Earlier cancellation
stops loss; later cancellation keeps it. Distinct loss declarations each apply
once. Batch entry observers see all successful entrants and completed losses.
The entrant's own battlefield loss trigger cannot observe its earlier entry
loss. Return applies loss again; phasing does not. Clones and factory instances
keep separate life and entry state. No new cost, LKI, damage, state-based action,
zone or trigger service was added; source-dependent values beyond the stated
RON grammar are not claimed as new entry adapters.

### Contract, engine reuse and boundaries

RON accepts exactly the top-level permanent rule
`PlayerEffect(You, [DoesntLoseTheGameForHaving0OrLessLife])`. The player and
operation are strict symbols; the list has one operation. Other player scopes,
tuple aliases, mixed lists, EachPlayerEffect and resolving contexts reject.

player_rule_operation; no new inventory grammar is needed.

New native signatures:

- `PreventLifeTotalLossStatic(subject PlayerRef) ContinuousEffect`, installed
  through `WithStaticAbility`.
- `(*Game).PreventsLifeTotalLoss(playerID uuid.UUID) bool`, a pure query over
  current static rules and completed layers.

Definition validation rejects nil/unbound subjects and nonbattlefield sources.
The compiler owns syntax and context restrictions and builds a fresh rule per
factory. The engine owns game-loss decisions and the live typed subject.
Printed static wrappers, source incarnation checks, current runtime abilities,
control layers, phasing, definition plans/copy builders and effect cloning are
reused. The source's current controller supplies You. Departure and ability

a fresh visit. LKI cannot supply a departed rule. Independent sources and copied
cards have their own source bindings. Queries make no choices, apply no layers,
change no loss state and inspect no unrelated effect lifetimes.

A missing engine contract was found: BasePlayer.IsAlive previously returned
`life > 0 && !lost`, so nonpositive life caused immediate apparent death and
made the corresponding state-based SetLost branch unreachable. IsAlive now
reads recorded loss. State-based actions alone record life-total loss at the
priority boundary, unless the live exemption applies. Life restored within one
resolving instruction can avoid loss; life restored after recorded loss cannot
revive a player. Each state-based batch saves player loss decisions before
permanent changes. Simultaneous losses draw. Poison, empty-library draws and
explicit SetLost remain effective at negative life under the exemption.
Clone extraction now retains recorded loss at any life total.

Whole-repository IsAlive and nonpositive-life caller searches found ante and AI
fixtures that used direct SetLife to stand in for finished games. They now make
the state-based check; their original ownership, settlement and terminal-score
assertions remain. AI move execution already checks state-based actions.
The scenario tool's nonpositive-life anomaly check now consults the shared
exemption query. Existing game-over, winner, draw, ante and AI consumers keep
their APIs and read recorded loss. No card definition was changed.

### Exact supported contract and reuse boundary

RON accepts this ordinary resolving-body pair:

```text
MustCost(SacrificeNumberPermanents(value, filter)),
If/Unless(CostWasPaid/CostWasntPaid, [actions])
```

The cost has exactly two arguments, the payment exactly one, and the adjacent
continuation exactly two. Conditions are strict symbols. Bodies must be
nonempty. Values use the existing resolution grammar, including bound
Trigger_AmountOfDamageDealt, integer values, arithmetic and permanent power with
exact source LKI. Filters use the reference-free sacrifice grammar, including
IsNonToken and nonempty And/Or. Unbound values, Other(ThisPermanent), malformed
arities, empty groups, separated or reused result clauses and IfElse reject.
Entry and draw replacement contexts reject. Spells, activated abilities,
ordinary triggers and delayed resolving bodies are supported. Existing optional
and announcement payments retain their current restrictions.

New engine signature:

- `RequiredSacrificeNumberOrElse(player PlayerRef, amount ResolutionValue,
  filter PermanentFilter, paid, unpaid ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.

RON owns spelling, role, scope and continuation validation. Each factory builds
its own bound values and branches. The engine saves the typed payer, reads the
count once, and uses tryResolutionCostPayment with required=true and a fresh
SacrificeNMatchingIncludingSourceCost. No optional offer occurs. Each call
selects its own branch; no result slot or mutable declaration state is shared.
A nonpositive count succeeds without choices. An absent payer does nothing.
Definition validation rejects nil/unbound inputs, a zero filter and no branches.

The existing transaction supplies full affordability, distinct exact visits,
locked choices, control/phasing/identity rechecks and rollback. Insufficient
resources cannot start payment, so no partial sacrifice occurs. A returned
selected visit cannot replace an old choice; a matching current source can pay.
Shared sacrifice handling supplies simultaneous movement, source-departure
snapshots, owner destinations, replacement choices and observations.
Indestructibility and regeneration cannot prevent sacrifice. Exile and
cancellation replacements can change the written actions while payment succeeds.
Waiting delayed queries inspect payer, amount and branches without payment and
retain exact source references. Source LKI, independent factories, queued copies
and game clones use the existing binding and lifecycle services.

### Established contract and reuse boundary

Engine signature: `LoseGameFor(subject PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`.
RON accepts only the zero-argument **symbol** `LoseTheGame` in ordinary resolving
bodies, including spells, activated abilities, triggers, delayed bodies and
payment continuations. `PlayerAction` and `PlayerActions` supply their explicit
player. The default scope supplies `You`, the resolving controller. Tuple aliases,
arguments, unbound player references, entry and replacement operations reject.

RON owns spelling and player scope. The engine resolves the typed player once
and calls the existing `Player.SetLost`. It does not change life, poison or
library state. The existing recorded-loss queries and clone extraction remain
the authority. The life-total exemption cannot stop explicit loss. Positive life
cannot reverse recorded loss. An absent player does nothing; definition
validation rejects nil and unbound players. No general loss-prohibition service
is introduced by this slice.

Queued abilities retain their resolving controller after source control changes,
phasing, departure or return. Copies use their own resolving controller.
Factories build fresh typed bindings. Clones retain independent loss state.
Explicit source operands use existing exact-visit and departure-controller LKI.
Waiting delayed queries retain those reads without executing loss or choices.
No payment, zone, replacement, event, clone or terminal-state subsystem is copied.
The existing sacrifice transaction supplies affordability, simultaneous movement
and rollback; this slice only supplies its loss continuation.

### Contract, dependencies and supported context

New engine signatures:

- `CreatureDeathsInto(binding *PermanentSetBinding) DestroyEachResultOption`.
- `ReturnChosenGraveyardCardsForEachPermanent(subjects *PermanentSetBinding,
  member *PermanentBinding, graveyard PlayerRef, filter CardFilter)
  ResolvingEffect`.

The result option is accepted by `DestroyEach` and
`DestroyEachWithoutRegeneration`. It uses the shared simultaneous destruction
result and existing instance-local permanent-set resolution frames. It saves
exact battlefield visits for creatures that actually reach a graveyard, including
tokens. Regeneration, indestructibility, phasing and replaced destinations exclude
members. Empty results clear previous values; duplicate/nil/unnamed declarations
reject. Clone support uses existing copied result slices.

The return service saves the member list, gives each player query a separate
permanent-binding frame, and restores outer bindings. Typed references can read
block history after departure. The resolving controller makes one required choice
per member, excluding previously chosen cards and tokens. Exact graveyard visits
are saved before movement. The shared graveyard batch-entry implementation was
factored into `enterSavedGraveyardCards`; existing All Hallow's Eve callers keep
the same behavior. APNAP entry preparation, owner control, entry replacements,
Aura checks, fresh X, final legality rechecks and simultaneous observations are
reused. Failed entry does not select again. No new payment or replacement system
was introduced. Waiting source-read detection now includes last-block references.

RON accepts ordinary resolving action sequences with an adjacent
`DestroyEachPermanent(collection)/1` or `DestroyEachPermanentNoRegen(collection)/1`
and `ActionForEachPermanentThatDiedThisWay([return])/1`. The list must contain
exactly one `ReturnACardFromPlayersGraveyardToBattlefield(
IsCardtype(Creature), playerRef, [EntersUnderOwnersControl])/3`. The owner-control
operation is a strict symbol. Other bodies and entry operations reject rather
than acquire sequential semantics. Missing/nonadjacent producers, wrong arities,
unbound references, escaping members, entry contexts and draw replacements reject.

Within this body,
`ControllerOfPermanentTheLastTimeItWasBlockedByPermanentThisTurn(
EachablePermanent, blockerRef)/2` reuses the existing pure
`ControllerWhenLastBlockedThisTurn` engine reference. Its member must be the strict
local symbol and its blocker a bound singular permanent reference. The member is
not supplied by an ordinary permanent loop. Bindings are fresh per factory; plans contain no game state. RON spelling and lexical checks stay in ron; the engine has no card-name
branch, fallback registry or global last-action state.

POSTCOMBAT-CASTING-WINDOW was selected for its one credible complete-card gain

### Contract, ownership and requirements

The exact supported declaration is the strict symbol `IsAfterCombat/0` inside
`CastEffect(CantBeCastUnless(condition))/1` on the existing nonmodal
instant/sorcery path. Nonempty nested `And` lists can combine it with supported
turn conditions. Callable symbols, invalid contexts and conjunctions containing
`IsDuringCombat` reject. The latter require a separate current-combat contract;
this slice does not infer one from first-combat history.

The native signatures are `AfterFirstCombat() StateCondition` and
`TurnReader.CombatHasEnded() bool`, implemented by `(*Game).CombatHasEnded`.
TurnSystem's value-only combat history now retains actual completion separately
from first-window closure. EndCombat completion is recorded after priority;
departure from an actual combat step also records the boundary for direct
SetStep callers, including a skipped end step. A postcombat enum alone cannot
supply completion. A wholly skipped combat supplies none. Empty combat completes
at its end, and a later actual combat can complete after a skipped phase. Once
true, the result stays true through later combats and phases in the same turn.
SetTurn and IncrementTurn clear it. Existing value cloning supplies isolation,
and the existing step-turn identity prevents inheritance from the prior turn.

RON owns spelling, arity, context and lowering. The engine owns history and the
pure query. Existing WithCastingCondition gates supply all casting paths,
pre-choice/pre-payment rejection and no repeat checks for stack copies or
resolution. Existing death-result, historical-controller, target and collective
entry services supply the spell body. No new source binding, LKI, payment,
replacement-ordering or simultaneous-operation contract is introduced.
No fallback, card-name branch, global action slot or partial registry was added.

Both complete local ruling files for Glyph and its Wall of Wood fixture were
read. Glyph has two wotc rulings; Wall has an explicit empty array. The fetchset
checks passed for both names. Glyph's local LEG Oracle text confirms the timing,

snapshot has one IsAfterCombat occurrence, in LEG:104. No source defect was
found. No RON changed, so no vocabulary refresh was needed. The implement-engine
skill supplied the native-contract workflow. Removal and cutover gates remain
closed; no Go card definition, generator or DSL export was removed.

### Contract, boundaries and requirements

Native `AttachedPermanentDies().WithDepartedAuraCard(card *CardBinding)` and
`AttachedCreatureDies().WithDepartedAuraCard(card *CardBinding)` expose the new
capture. The binding must be non-nil, occur once, differ from the host's WithCard
binding and use an attached death pattern. Normal declaration validation rejects
invalid producers and unbound consumers. A non-Aura source supplies no Aura card.

Detection saves exact source and host battlefield visits in an immutable pending
capture. The shared simultaneous zone batch records destination visits before
trigger dispatch and fills captures only for matched Aura/host deaths in that
batch. The orphan-Aura state action can instead fill a pending capture after
host departure. It checks attachment incarnation as well as ID. Source return,
reattachment, an ordinary later destruction, exile and hand movement cannot
supply an eligible visit. The existing saved-card reference rejects later
graveyard visits. Tokens supply no returnable card. There is no new global
last-action slot or persistent departure-history map. Pending clone capture
slices are replaced independently; stack copies retain immutable saved facts.
Existing callers and engine card movement remain in use.

RON accepts strict `ReturnDeadGuestGraveyardCardToHand/0` in an ordinary resolving
Aura `WhenAPermanentDies(SinglePermanent(HostPermanent))` body. The host-death plan
requests one fresh native binding per factory only if the operation is used.
It lowers to `ReturnCardToHand(FromCard(binding))`. Other events, callable symbols,
entry and replacement contexts reject. RON owns spelling/context; mage owns
trigger capture, exact visits, state actions and owner-zone movement. Takklemaggot
can reuse the same native binding for later battlefield-return adapters.

Puppet Master's complete local file has one wotc ruling. Takklemaggot's has four
wotc rulings. Both were read in full. The latter explicitly establishes that the
Aura goes to the graveyard as a state action after its host dies and must still
be in that graveyard at resolution. Wall of Wood's fixture ruling file has an
explicit empty array. `fetchset -check` passed for all three affected/test names.
Local LEG Oracle records confirm both return procedures. Rules read: CR 400.7f,
603.3, 603.10 and 704.5m. Vocabulary has one hand-return symbol (Puppet Master),
one legality symbol and two battlefield-return tuples (Takklemaggot). No source
defect was found. No RON changed; the vocabulary snapshot needs no refresh.
The implement-engine skill supplied the native-contract workflow. No Go card,
generator or DSL API was removed; cutover gates remain closed.

### Failing-first evidence and gameplay mapping

Native tests first failed compilation because WithDepartedAuraCard did not
exist. The corrected RON fixture then failed at the unsupported hand-return
symbol before its adapter was restored. The first RON fixture used a helper
without an Aura subtype and failed too early; that fixture was corrected before
recording the expected unsupported-node failure. A host-return assertion also
failed with the old ID-only Aura state check (`hand=0 want=1`), then passed with
the incarnation check.

| Independent source instances | TestDepartedAuraCardInstances | Two Auras on one host; changing one graveyard visit leaves the other's saved visit intact |
| Declaration validation | TestDepartedAuraCardInvalid | Nil, duplicate, nonattached and conflicting host/Aura card bindings reject |

### Signatures, ownership and dependencies

New native API:

- `EnterAttachedTo(host PermanentRef) BattlefieldEntryOption`.
- `PutExiledCardsOntoBattlefieldUnderOwnersControl(subjects ExiledCardSet,
  options ...BattlefieldEntryOption) ResolvingEffect` extends the existing
  constructor without changing existing call sites.
- `ReturnCardToBattlefield` and `ReturnCardToBattlefieldInto` retain their
  existing signatures and accept this option. One `EnterTapped` can accompany
  one attachment option. Nil, duplicate and unbound declarations reject.

Supported RON shapes, in ordinary resolving bodies only:

- `ReturnDeadGuestGraveyardCardToBattlefield([EntersUnderPlayersControl(playerRef),
  EntersAttachedToPermanent(permanentRef)])` in an Aura host-death body. The
  existing departed-Aura event binding supplies the exact graveyard visit.
- `PutEachExiledCardOntoTheBattlefield(exiledSet, [EntersUnderOwnersControl,
  EntersAttachedToPermanent(permanentRef)])` with existing grouped or linked
  exile sets. The owner-only form remains supported. The list order and arity
  are strict. Other entry operations and incompatible or unbound reads reject.

RON owns syntax, context and per-factory reference lowering. Mage owns card and
host visits, replacement preparation, legality, zone movement and attachment.
The implementation reuses the existing entry pipeline, shared `canAttach`,
protection/enchant restrictions, `Game.Attach`, exact card bindings, exile batch,
entry observation and delayed-frame services. It introduces no card-name branch,
Go fallback, production partial registry or global action-result slot.

The instruction saves its host before entry replacements. A scoped entry query
makes the prepared entrant visible to shared legality checks, then restores the
prior entry context. This is required when entry copying changes color, type or
enchant restrictions. The same query is used by existing choice-based entry and
both batch rechecks. An illegal or undefined host prevents Aura entry; ordinary
permanents, Equipment and Fortification can instead enter unattached under
CR 301.5e, 301.6 and 303.4h–i. Shroud/hexproof do not prohibit entry attachment;
protection and enchant prohibitions do. Card and host return cannot supply saved
visits. A phase cycle retains a host visit; an absent phased host is unavailable.
All successful exile batch members are registered and attached before entry
observations. No new payment, rollback or replacement-order policy is introduced.

All four Takklemaggot wotc rulings, all six Coffin wotc rulings, and Animate
Dead's five wotc rulings were read. Puppet Master's and Vesuvan Doppelganger's

Coffin and Animate Dead before implementation. Rules used: CR 301.5e, 301.6,
303.4c–j, 400.7, 614.12, 701.3a–c, 702.16c–d and 702.26b–d. No source defect
was found or corrected. No RON source changed, so no vocabulary snapshot refresh

typed host reads. The implement-engine skill supplied the native workflow.

### Contract, signatures and reuse boundary

- Native signatures:
  `EnterWithoutSubtype(family SubtypeFamily, subtype string) BattlefieldEntryOption`
  and `EnterAsNonAuraEnchantment() BattlefieldEntryOption`.
  It removes one subtype in layer 4 from one exact entrant visit and preserves
  other subtypes and card types. The second constructor also sets the card type
  to Enchantment. Other card types and their associated subtypes do not remain;
  supertypes stay unchanged. A copied Aura ability can return a physical card
  that is not an enchantment. Invalid family/subtype declarations, empty
  subtypes, duplicate options and existing nil option checks reject before play.
- The shared entry context carries the option into graveyard and exile entry.
  Replacement checks see the removal before entry. Copy replacements can replace
  subtype state, so each later entry check reapplies it. Projected entry queries
  use the same retained layer effect. Successful entry keeps the effect in the
  shared layer service. Cancelled preparation and rejected/stale prepared entries
  remove the unused effect. Existing entry ordering, attachment and batch
  registration services remain in charge of movement and observations.
- The effect saves a `capturedPermanent`, not a bare card ID. Phasing suspends it
  and preserves the visit; a full phase cycle restores it. Departure ends its
  application. A new visit cannot inherit it. Printed cards and copiable values
  retain their subtypes. Later subtype effects use normal timestamp order.
  Game clones keep independent effect objects and later layer changes.
- RON accepts exactly
  `ReturnDeadGuestGraveyardCardToBattlefield([EntersUnderPlayersControl(playerRef), EntersAsNonAuraEnchantment])`
  in ordinary resolving Aura host-death bodies. The second entry is a strict
  symbol, sets Enchantment and removes Aura from the saved departed Aura's new visit. The existing
  explicit attached-entry shape remains supported. Enchant ability removal is
  a later instruction and is not silently included in the entry operation.
- Both departed-Aura return forms can now produce
  `ThePermanentPutOnTheBattlefieldThisWay` for later instructions in the same
  action list. Shared
  `ReturnCardToBattlefieldInto(card CardRef, controller PlayerRef, result *PermanentBinding, options ...BattlefieldEntryOption)`
  clears failed results and saves the exact successful entrant. RON uses a fresh
  per-instance binding and its existing returned-permanent scope plan. Branch
  results cannot escape; nested producers shadow and restore outer scope.
  Delayed bodies, stack copies and clones reuse the existing saved-frame and
  LKI services. There is no global last-entry result.
- Entry and draw replacement contexts, missing Aura host-death scopes,
  malformed entry lists, incorrect arity and escaped results still reject.

### Supported contract and reuse boundary

Mage adds
`TriggeredAbilityForPlayerModification(subject PermanentRef, player PlayerRef, ability *GenericTriggered) ContinuousModification`.
With `Until(Indefinite, ...)`, it saves the player and exact recipient when the
grant resolves. A missing player makes no grant. Definition validation rejects
nil/unbound players and retains existing subject/trigger/body validation. The
captured UUID filter is combined with existing trigger conditions without
changing the prototype. Repeated installations receive independent filters and
identities. Mage reuses layer capture, exact visits, granted trigger installation,
event capture, APNAP stacking, ability removal, phasing, delayed saved frames
and game cloning. Waiting delayed-source inspection now includes the typed
player's source reads; it never installs a grant.

RON accepts ordinary resolving
`CreatePermanentLayerEffect(permanentRef, [AddAbility([TriggerA(AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersUpkeep(SinglePlayer(playerRef)), body)])])`.
Other supported, bound player references read the outer action scope at grant
resolution. The pre-existing strict `You` form retains its recipient-controller
meaning at event time. Every granted body starts with a fresh permanent scope:
ThisPermanent and You use the recipient, and Trigger_ThatPlayer reads the new
upkeep event. Donor bindings cannot escape into the body. Existing lists can
combine these grants with supported conditional untap grants. Static Aura-host
grants keep their existing compiler path. Entry/draw replacements, unsupported
events and mixed enchant-removal/grant lists still reject.

No new cost rollback, replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation policy is
needed: this capability installs a characteristic effect after resolution.

partial registry, name branch, global last-action state or declaration panic
was added. The runtime/removal gates remain closed.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

Mage adds `RemoveCreatureEnchant(subject PermanentRef) ContinuousModification`
and `(*Permanent).HasCreatureEnchantAbility() bool`. The removal applies to the
fixed declaration created by `CreatureEnchantTarget()`, including repeated
instances. It does not infer arbitrary opaque filters. `Until(duration, ...)`
captures the exact recipient and applies removal in layer 6. A missing recipient
or absent fixed declaration has no effect. Nil and unbound subjects fail native
definition validation. Other enchant declarations, unrelated abilities, Aura
subtype, printed card rules and copiable values stay unchanged.

The computed removal is reset before each layer pass and read by the shared
Aura attachment legality service. Expiry restores restrictions. An incompatible
attachment then goes to the graveyard at the next state action. Phasing suspends
the visit and phase-in permits the same removal on the next layer pass. Return
cannot inherit an old visit's effect. Game clones keep separate computed state
and expiry. Existing exact-visit capture, layer duration, copy-on-write state,
source LKI, and waiting delayed-source inspection are reused. Explicit
HostOfPermanent(This) reads retain the departed donor without executing a query.

RON accepts ordinary resolving
`CreatePermanentLayerEffect(permanentRef,
[LosesAbility(Enchant(IsCardtype(Creature)))])`, alone or in a list with the
existing supported AddAbility conditional untap/upkeep grants. Creature is a
strict symbol; malformed arities, other enchant filters and unbound references
reject. Entry and draw replacement contexts reject. Each factory uses its own
bindings; the existing acquired trigger adapter supplies its fresh recipient
scope. No new payment, replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation policy is
needed for this layer operation. Graveyard enchant declarations and replacement
enchant grants still need separate contracts and adapters.

### Supported signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

Native API:

- `WhenLeaves(subject PermanentRef, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.
- `WhenUntaps(subject PermanentRef, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.
- `WhenLeavesOrUntaps(subject PermanentRef, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.

All require a present, unphased exact subject visit at installation. The union
registers one subscription and is consumed at the first matching event. Cleanup
does not expire these one-shot subscriptions. Earlier leave/untap events cannot
replay. A returned incarnation cannot substitute for a saved visit. Control and
characteristic changes preserve it. Phasing sends neither event and preserves
the subscription. Stun replacement sends no untap event. Departure matching uses
the existing former-battlefield observer, including simultaneous departures.

The engine extends delayedPermanentEventEffect and adds a private scalar
alternate event type to DelayedTrigger. Shared matching, captureDelayedBody,
waiting-source queries, APNAP pending placement, stack copying, binding cleanup
and game cloning remain the owners of their behavior. Existing turn-scoped
callers retain their signatures and repeat/expiry semantics. Definition checks
reuse existing typed subject/body and binding-dominance validation. There is no
new mutable result registry, global last-action slot or card-name branch.

RON accepts `CreateFutureTrigger(event, ActionList(actions))`, where event is
`WhenPermanentLeavesTheBattlefield(ThisPermanent)`,
`WhenPermanentBecomesUntapped(ThisPermanent)`, or their exact two-member `Or`
list in either order. Subjects are strict ThisPermanent symbols. Duplicate
members, other subjects, invalid arities, empty bodies and new body targets
reject. Ordinary resolving permanent-source activations, triggers (including
source-entry triggers), and nested delayed bodies are supported. Entry and draw
replacement operations, source-zone rules and spells do not supply this shape.
The event introduces no new event bindings; ControllerOfLeavingPermanent still
rejects and requires a separate capture adapter. Outer lexical bindings remain
available through existing captured frames. The inventory now distinguishes
these events and their permanent-reference operands from delayed step events.

### Contract and reuse boundary

New engine signature:
`PutExiledCardOntoBattlefieldOrElse(card CardRef, result *PermanentBinding,

One exact saved exile visit returns under its current owner's control. Missing,
stale, token and nonpermanent subjects fail. Shared exile entry retains copy,
replacement, counter, tapped-entry, host-choice and attachment behavior. Entry
operation failure retains its existing graveyard destination. Failed entry
clears the result. Successful registration saves the new incarnation before
observations. Actual entry selects success even if an observation removes the
entrant; later result reads still require its exact live visit. Success is a
local return value. Definition validation exposes the result only inside the
success sequence. Nil/unbound inputs, no branches, failure-branch result reads
and escaped new results reject.

RON signature:
`MustCost(PutExiledCardOntoBattlefield(singularGroupedExileReference,
[EntersUnderOwnersControl, ...options]))`, with an immediately adjacent
`If`, `Unless` or `IfElse` using strict `CostWasPaid`/`CostWasntPaid` symbols.
Owner control is required first. Optional EntersTapped and
EntersWithNotedCounters symbols can each occur once. Noted counters require a
lexically preceding snapshot. Only success introduces the new
ThePermanentPutOnTheBattlefieldThisWay reference. Existing outer bindings stay
available. Per-instance returned-permanent plans reuse the existing typed
PermanentBinding and cloned compiler maps. Inventory records card-reference and
entry-operation argument roles for the resolution cost.

private marker distinguishes it from ordinary graveyard spell targets. Existing
unmarked native callers keep their prior behavior. Definition validation requires
one cast target on an Aura enchantment; nil/unbound reference declarations reject.

Aura spells use the shared exact target visit, payment and resolution legality.
A stale target fails rather than choosing another card. Noncast entry makes one
required controller choice among either player's matching graveyard cards, after
copy and entry operations. No legal host keeps an uncast Aura in its original
hand, graveyard or exile zone. Saved host visits are checked again after batch
entry choices. Entry sets attachment before observations. No battlefield-only
shroud/protection is applied to a graveyard card. Fixed graveyard enchant cannot
attach to a battlefield permanent. Shared state-action batching moves illegal
Auras to their owners' graveyards. Phasing preserves visits and suspends checks.

legality. Hand/battlefield return effects expose their source reads to waiting
queries. Existing entry, target, payment, card movement and clone services remain
the execution owners. No card-name branches, Go fallbacks, partial registry,
global result slot or declaration panic was added.

rule on an Aura enchantment. Creature and AnyPlayer are strict symbols. Duplicate

Candidate #1 is not dependency-ready as a grant adapter: it needs a forward
returned-host identity contract first. None of the compared candidates provides

remaining cards. Counter duration provides the smallest complete end-to-end

The selected contract and acceptance cases were stated before edits. Local
rulings for all three candidates were read. Before implementation,
`go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card 'Cyclopean Tomb'` passed. Tomb has three WotC
rulings and no Scryfall notes. Its land effect persists independently of the Tomb,
uses any mire counter on the land, and does not change snow status. CR 122.1,
400.7, 611.2a–d and 702.26e–f establish counter interchangeability, exact visits,
captured subjects and the permanent end of a tracked duration on phase-out.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

Engine API:
`UntilPermanentHasCounter(subject PermanentRef, counter core.CounterType,
modifications ...ContinuousModification) ResolvingEffect`.
The watched visit must be present, unphased and have a positive selected counter
count at resolution. An absent condition starts no effect. Last-counter removal,
departure or phase-out ends the duration permanently. Partial removal, counters
from another origin, controller changes, ability removal and cleanup do not end
it. The source can depart or phase independently. A different affected recipient
can phase without ending the watched condition.

Each permanent records counter-zero and phase epochs. Captured lifetimes save
these values and the incarnation. Remove-and-readd and phase-out-and-in between
layer passes cannot restart the duration. Game clones copy these values and
installed effects independently. The shared instruction/state-trigger boundary
refreshes expired layers before the next instruction. Phase-out refreshes them
immediately. Native counter annihilation, loyalty damage and charge cleanup
resets use RemoveCounter so these operations retain transitions too.

The existing untilEffect/composedLayerEffect services own recipient/value capture,
layer ordering, timestamps, source independence, control changes, subtype-family
changes and grants. Waiting delayed queries include explicit source reads in the
duration without executing it. Speculative payments cannot expire live effects.
No replacement, payment, zone or layer service was duplicated in ron.

RON accepts exactly
`CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil(subject, modifications,
ForAsLongAsPermanentHasACounterOfTypeOnIt(EachablePermanent, counter))`
in ordinary resolving bodies. The duration's first operand is the strict local
symbol EachablePermanent, bound to the singular layer recipient. Counter types
reuse the existing permanent counter grammar. Existing singular references and
temporary modifications apply. This duration also accepts one strict basic-land
`SetLandType(type)` modification through the existing SetSubtypeFamily service.
Static/collection layers, costs, entry/draw replacements, malformed symbols and
other duration subjects reject. Inventory reports the operands as permanent
reference and permanent counter type. The symbol does not leak into other scopes.
No card-name branch, Go fallback, partial registry, global last-action slot or
game-time declaration panic was added.

API. After correcting test fixture method names, RON tests failed at the missing
duration in all five real Tomb activated clauses. The initial implementation
passed these tests. Two additional timing tests then failed: a following life
instruction read the expired power bonus (life 23 instead of 22), and phase-out
left a separate recipient's bonus installed. Shared boundary refresh and immediate
phase expiry fix those failures without weakening the assertions.

shape; their other counter-removal declarations retain rejection. Inventory

scope, action-player selection and construction; mage owns history and execution.

### Implemented contract and ownership

Native signatures:

- `RecordEntryFrom(source PermanentRef) BattlefieldEntryOption`
- `PermanentsEnteredWithSource(source PermanentRef, candidates PermanentSet) PermanentSet`

The option captures an exact information identity before entry choices. Typed
singular graveyard returns, their saved-result form, and owner-controlled exile
entry accept the option. Only successful registered entrants establish a link.
Every exile batch member is registered and linked before entry observations.
The graveyard path with this option reuses attachment entry's ordering: remove
the card, register, record history, attach if specified, then observe entry and
notify graveyard departure. This avoids the legacy unattached path's premature
zone event. Existing callers without the new option retain their current path.
Failed, stale, prohibited and cancelled linked returns record no relation or
entry observation. Copy entry and other entry options still use shared services.

The query is live and pure. It can be constructed/read before the producer,
then read after it, including from a later delayed body. History belongs to the
zone system, keyed by both exact visits. Cleanup, source departure, ability loss
and control changes do not erase it. Phasing suspends recipient selection until
phase-in. Return cannot inherit either identity. Source information uses existing
saved frames and LKI contracts. Clones and speculative payment trials copy the
history map. Query and producer source reads use shared delayed-source inspection.
There is no global last-result slot, card-name branch or declaration-time game.
Nil/unbound/non-information sources, nil candidates and duplicate source options
fail native declaration validation.

RON accepts exactly `PutOntoBattlefieldByPermanent(ThisPermanent)` in resolving
graveyard-Aura contextual collections, including `And`/`Or`, source entry-trigger
bodies and delayed bodies. `enteringSource` identifies the source entry trigger
here; it is not an entry replacement. The adapter therefore permits this
resolving context. Typed graveyard returns in the scope receive
`RecordEntryFrom(This)`. Other source references, non-graveyard-Aura scopes,
costs, static/enchant grants, entry replacement operations and draw replacement
bodies reject. Inventory labels the operand `permanent_reference`.
RON owns spelling, scope and option construction. Mage owns registration,
attachment, entry replacements, source identity, history, queries and cloning.
There is no RON spelling for the native entry option.

CR 400.7 establishes new visits after zone changes; CR 608.2c preserves resolving
instruction order. CR 303.4 and 303.4j require attachment legality against the
actual enchant restriction. All local Animate Dead rulings were read. The WotC
2016-06-08 rulings establish the returned creature as a new object, and prohibit
moving the Aura to another creature unless that Aura puts it onto the battlefield.
These are WotC rulings, not Scryfall notes. The complete RON record also includes
protection/attachment, presence and delayed sacrifice behavior, which is not
claimed by this slice. `go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card "Animate Dead"` passed.
No source defect was found and no RON source changed. No vocabulary snapshot
refresh is needed. API and rules-contract documentation describe this slice.

### Contract, dependencies and exact supported context

Native APIs:

- `GrantPermanentEnchant(subject PermanentRef, hosts PermanentSet) ContinuousModification`
- `RemoveGraveyardCreatureEnchant(subject PermanentRef) ContinuousModification`

`Until` captures each exact recipient visit. The grant retains a live host query,
not its current result. Host queries read the recipient as `This` and its current
controller as `You`, in a separate declaration binding scope. Donor targets and
saved bindings cannot enter that scope. Nil hosts, nil/unbound subjects and
unbound host references fail native validation. A query can be empty when the
grant starts, then find a later linked entrant in the same resolution.

Layer 6 applies the paired removal and grant in declared order. The graveyard
removal preserves the saved exact attachment so a later return instruction can
still read `EnchantedGraveyardCard`. The grant does not change printed cast
targets, copiable rules or source metadata, and makes no targeting operation.
All current enchant restrictions intersect, including printed and acquired
restrictions. The former printed-target loop accepted any matching declaration;
it now requires every enchant ability, as CR 702.5c specifies. Protection,
attachment restrictions, shroud/hexproof handling and state actions reuse the
shared attachment service. Permanent-only grants cannot enchant a graveyard
card. Removal alone preserves that saved host without its fixed creature filter.

Removal of all abilities clears earlier acquired enchant declarations; later
grants restore them in timestamp order. Fixed creature-enchant removal does not
remove acquired enchant abilities. Expiry restores printed restrictions. A
phase cycle preserves the exact grant; a returned recipient cannot inherit it.
Donor departure does not end an ordinary Until effect. Clones keep separate
computed state, expiry and saved graveyard attachments. A failing clone/expiry
test exposed an existing omission in `clonePermanentInto`: it did not copy
`enchantedCard`. That exact attachment and the relevant enchant state are now
copied there. The shared `targetsWithoutCreatureEnchant` helper became unused;
a repository Go-caller search found only its definition, which was removed.
No broad DSL function or Go card definition was removed.

RON accepts exactly:

```ron
CreatePermanentLayerEffect(ThisPermanent, [
    LosesAbility(Enchant(IsCardtype(Creature))),
    AddAbility([EnchantPermanent(And([
        IsCardtype(Creature),
        PutOntoBattlefieldByPermanent(ThisPermanent)
    ]))])
])
```

The recipient must be the source in a resolving graveyard-Aura scope. That scope
identifies the fixed graveyard enchant declaration removed by this paired form.
The entry-trigger `enteringSource` flag does not make its resolving action list
an entry replacement. This adapter permits that resolving context, without
loosening the guards on other lasting ability grants. It requires both clauses
in the listed order, one acquired enchant ability, and the exact two-member
linked-creature filter with strict symbols. The existing contextual collection
compiler supplies the host query and existing graveyard returns supply entry
history. Other filters, recipients, unpaired graveyard removal, extra/mixed layer
parts, costs, entry replacements and draw replacements reject.

RON owns syntax, shape and lexical context. Mage owns live query execution,
layer state, exact visits, clone isolation and attachment legality. There are no
card-name branches, runtime declaration games, global action-result slots or
partial production registries. Counter events, costs, replacement ordering and
simultaneous entry retain their existing services; this pair introduces no new
payment or replacement procedure.

CR 303.4c/j, 400.7, 608.2c, 611.2a/c, 613.1f and 702.5a/c establish the contract.
All local Animate Dead rulings were read; they are WotC rulings, not Scryfall
notes. The 2016-06-08 rulings establish the new creature object, protection and
