### Supported shapes, ownership and contracts

RON accepts:

```ron
PutGraveyardCardOntoBattlefield(EnchantedGraveyardCard,
    [EntersUnderPlayersControl(You)]),
AttachPermanentToPermanent(ThisPermanent,
    ThePermanentPutOnTheBattlefieldThisWay)
```

The producer and reference now support resolving source entry `TriggerA` and
`TriggerI` bodies. Existing ordinary creature-target and departed-Aura return
contexts retain their own constraints. The entrant binding is lexical and
per factory, never a global last-action slot. Wrong arity, tuple references,
wrong types, unbound or forward result reads and unsupported replacement
contexts reject during compilation. No result can escape a branch.

`compileExactAttachment(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` owns syntax and
scope. It lowers two singular references to the new native signature
`AttachToPermanent(attachment, host PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect`. This action
makes no choice and adds no target. It requires present, unphased exact visits;
LKI cannot supply movement. Illegal attachment keeps the current host. A phase
cycle preserves identity. Returned objects cannot replace saved visits.

Mage reuses `ReturnCardToBattlefieldInto`, `PermanentBinding`, `From`,
`RecordEntryFrom`, shared entry processing and `Game.Attach`. Attachment uses
current enchant restrictions and protection. Shroud and hexproof permit a
non-targeting attachment. Shared links, timestamps, layers and attach events
remain authoritative. `refersToSourcePermanent` and definition traversal retain
explicit source reads in waiting queries without execution. Immutable action
plans need no new clone state; resolution and delayed frames keep bindings
separate. Costs, replacement ordering and simultaneous operations have no new
service or scheduling path. Existing entry and attachment tests retain those
contracts. Failed or prohibited entry cannot supply an old entrant result.

CR 303.4c/e/j, 400.7j, 608.2c, 701.3a–c and 704.3 establish the contract.

### Source defect and rules evidence

All six Animate Dead records used:

```ron
PlayerAction(ControllerOfLeavingPermanent,
    SacrificePermanent(ThePermanentPutOnTheBattlefieldThisWay))
```

Local `data/LEA.json` Oracle text says, "that creature's controller sacrifices
it." The WotC ruling dated 2016-06-08 confirms that even failed attachment due
to protection causes Aura state departure and delayed sacrifice of the returned
creature. CR 303.4e separates Aura control from host control; CR 701.21a requires
the sacrificing player to control the permanent. CR 603.7a-e, 400.7 and 608.2
supply delayed timing, exact identities and resolution-time reads. These local
rulings are WotC rulings, not Scryfall notes. No missing rulings were assumed.
`go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card "Animate Dead"` passed before implementation.

The six identical records now use
`ControllerOfPermanent(ThePermanentPutOnTheBattlefieldThisWay)` instead of the
unbound departure-player symbol. This reads the creature's controller when the
body resolves, including changes after the Aura leaves. No other RON record
changed. The vocabulary snapshot was refreshed from a full parser AST walk:
604 tuple signatures, one fewer symbol signature, six added current-controller
reads and saved-entrant reads, updated positions, six hashes and fresh loader
status. Snapshot loader data had lagged prior slices; it now matches this run.

### Exact shape, contract and reuse boundary

Mage adds:

```go
func SacrificeFor(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect
```

The typed player must control the exact present, unphased subject visit at
resolution. Absent, phased, returned or differently controlled subjects cannot
be sacrificed. LKI can supply information, never a live object for movement.
No choice, target or new cost state is added. Owner destinations,
indestructibility, regeneration, sacrifice replacements and events use the
existing `sacrificeEffect`, `prepareSacrifice` and `performSacrifice` path.
`Sacrifice` keeps its existing ability-controller and result-option contract.
Its definition child layout also remains compatible with existing inspectors
and chosen-sacrifice callers. Explicit player operands enter definition and
waiting-source traversal. Queries resolve neither operand and move nothing.

RON adds `PlayerAction(playerRef, SacrificePermanent(permanentRef))` in ordinary
resolving bodies, including source entry and delayed source departure bodies.
The compiler owns spelling, arity, role and binding checks. It lowers through
`compilePlayerEffect`, `compilePlayerRef` and `compilePermanentRef` to the new
native API. `PlayerActions` is not extended. Nonresolving entry operations and
draw replacements reject. `ControllerOfLeavingPermanent` stays unbound; no
incorrect event binding was invented. There are no card-name branches.

Existing `WhenLeaves`, `PermanentBinding`, `From`, `ReturnCardToBattlefieldInto`,
entry history, attachments and `captureDelayedBody` supply all other behavior.

end the unbounded subscription. Source return cannot supply a different visit.
Copies and pending/waiting clones keep separate frames. No clone-owned mutable
state, global action slot, parallel event path or partial registry was added.
No cost or simultaneous-operation service changed; the full shared regression
suite retains rollback, replacement ordering and batch contracts.

Mage adds:

```go
func CopyAddTriggeredAbility(build func() *GenericTriggered) CopyModification
```

The pure builder must return fresh declarations without saved game state.

builds and binding dominance. Nil builders/abilities, panics, unbound reads and
reused abilities or targets reject before gameplay. The existing

Later builds and copies retain it under CR 707.9a. Existing donor rules remain;
repeated additions stay separate. The recipient supplies source and controller.
Ordinary ability removal does not change the copiable snapshot. Default entry
replacements and entry observations see the added rule. Shared simultaneous
entry gives each entrant its own source and declarations.

RON accepts the following operation in CopyEffects for optional entry copying:

```text
AddAbility([TriggerA(
  AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersUpkeep(SinglePlayer(You)), body)])
```

Each AddAbility contains exactly one trigger. Multiple operations can compose
with each other, KeepColor and AddCardtypes. The compiler reuses
`compileRecipientUpkeepAbility` and `compileBoundStepAbility`, with a fresh
permanent scope. The existing resolving-body grammar supplies actions, local
target groups and event bindings. Donor attachments, targets and payment results
cannot enter the new scope. Declaration errors retain source positions.
Inventory traversal now gives the nested AddAbility body the rule role.

Shared entry-copy replacements, definition plans, snapshots, trigger detection,
target legality, pending frames, copies, phasing and clones supply execution.
No parallel copy, event, target or zone subsystem was added. No game-time
production declaration panic, global action result, card-name branch or partial
registry was introduced. Existing factory purity rules still apply. Existing
text-revision context gates remain; no new text-change context is claimed.
Payment rollback and simultaneous movement retain their existing contracts.

Other events/player filters, AddAbilityVariable(ThisAbility), optional resolving
copy actions and live copy layers remain unsupported. All six complete Vesuvan
records now reject at `unsupported optional action (CreatePermanentLayerEffect)`
instead of the outer AddAbility operation. This keeps the whole production
collection rejected atomically. No Go definition or broad DSL function was
removed; cutover and removal gates remain unmet.

### Exact contract, signatures and reuse boundary

Mage adds:

```go
func ControllerRemovesLastCounter(counter core.CounterType, actor *PlayerBinding) EventPattern
```

RON accepts, in a battlefield-source TriggerA:

```text
WhenAPlayerRemovesTheLastCounterOfTypeFromAPermanent(
  SinglePlayer(You), <supported permanent-counter symbol>,
  SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent))
```

The resolving body can read Trigger_ThatPlayer as a local typed player. Factories
build fresh bindings; the compiler owns spelling, validation and lexical scope.
The engine owns attribution, event facts, exact visits, post-removal layers and
pending captures. Invalid arities, tuple symbol spellings, unknown counters,
other player/permanent filters, unbound actor reads and wrong reference types
reject before gameplay. This does not add a text-revision context.

The existing internal removeCountersFrom service now takes an explicit actor.
Resolving removal supplies its saved effect controller; fixed, X and chosen
counter costs supply their payer. Positive successful removals publish the new
core.EvtCountersRemoved with cause and recipient identities, PlayerID,
CounterType, actual Amount and CountersRemaining. The last-counter pattern
requires zero remainder and matches the source's current exact visit and
controller at detection. Source controller and actor are distinct from the
removing effect's source controller. No mutable global action result is used.

Completed layers are required after removal and before event detection. Tests
first showed that an expiring counter-bound control or ability-removal effect
could otherwise suppress the event. The shared service now updates layers at
that boundary. Later counter placement does not cancel a pending event. Source
control changes, departure, return and phasing do not change its saved player.
Returned incarnations cannot supply an old event. Zone departure makes counters
cease to exist and supplies no removal event (CR 122.2).

Shared pending triggers, source LKI, stack copies, game cloning, declaration
validation and cost transactions remain the execution path. Affordability queries
and payment preparation publish no live events; stale fixed, X and chosen
payments fail without publishing removal. Successful payments publish once.
The raw Permanent.RemoveCounter mutation has no player attribution; state-based
removals are not player actions. No counter-moving procedure, simultaneous
counter-removal batch or new removal replacement order is declared. Existing
zone, replacement and simultaneous-action services retain their contracts.

No source-data defect was found or corrected. RON source files and the vocabulary
snapshot are unchanged. No Go card definition, generator or broad DSL function
was removed: complete loading, gameplay and startup gates remain unmet. There
is no partial production registry, fallback, card-name branch or game-time
production declaration panic.

### Exact contract, dependencies and boundaries

`DrawTheGame` is a strict symbol with zero operands in ordinary non-entry
resolving ActionList bodies, including non-entry triggers and nested permanent
loops. RON rejects tuple spellings, costs, explicit-player actions, source-entry
scopes and entry/draw replacement bodies before execution. The action needs no
source, player, target, binding or mutable factory state. Other reference scopes
keep their existing validation. This adds no text-revision declaration context.

`mage.DrawGame() ResolvingEffect` saves Game.drawn when no earlier result exists.
CR 104.1 and 104.4c establish immediate termination. Divine Intervention's three
local 2009-10-01 rulings are WotC rulings, with no Scryfall notes: controller
attribution, immediate draw without a winner/loser, and limited-range multiplayer.
The last does not apply to this two-player engine. fetchset -check for Divine
Intervention passed. No network refresh or source correction was needed.

A private immutable error value carries the stop through nested resolving bodies;
it is not a global action result. ApplyEffect consumes it without an execution
error or log. Shared branches, sequences, pipelines and loops propagate child
errors. The stack stops before subsequent effects, objects and spell cleanup or
permanent entry. Deferred state actions and trigger checks cannot change the
result. Trigger detection/placement, priority, step finalization, end-of-step
mana cleanup and later turns stop. Scratch frames still restore normally.
Pending objects remain for terminal-state inspection. Custom resolving wrappers
must propagate child errors. The compiler owns spelling and context; mage owns
all execution and result state.

IsGameOver and IsDraw return true; Winner returns an empty string. Neither
player's loss flag, life or other resources change. Clone copies draw state by
value and preserves pending frames independently. An earlier win is not replaced.
AnteResult rejects a draw even after a later direct mutation of a player's flag.
The prior simultaneous-loss draw behavior is retained. Existing last-counter
attribution, exact source visits, LKI, pending captures, copies, cost transactions,
entry counters and upkeep services are reused. No new replacement ordering,
simultaneous operation, target legality rule or payment procedure is added.

### Exact signatures, scope and reuse boundary

Engine: `MayAttachPermanentToChoice(player PlayerRef, attachment PermanentRef,
hosts PermanentSet) ResolvingEffect`. The shared attachment move now has an
optional form. It saves the player before ChooseMayAbility. No present attachment,
no player or no legal host means no offer. Decline makes no host choice.
Acceptance uses the shared permanentChoice with the saved player ID, then checks
the attachment visit, chosen host visit, host collection and attachment legality
again. The private applyForPlayer helper prevents a controller change during the
offer from changing the chooser. Internal host bindings remain local to each
factory and resolution frame. Failed movement retains the current attachment.

The optional legal-host query includes a legal current host. Selecting it does
nothing: no attach event, link change or timestamp change (CR 701.3b–c).
Game.attachmentHostIsLegal factors the existing enchant/equip/fortify checks from
canAttach; canAttach still requires an actual move. Required attachment-choice
callers retain their other-host behavior. All moves still use Game.Attach,
existing enchant restrictions, protection, timestamps and layer updates.
Shroud and hexproof do not prevent the nontargeted choice. Return cannot inherit
either visit. Phasing suspends movement. Waiting queries do not offer, select,
move or consume RNG. Pending stack copies, games and factories retain separate
saved contexts. No payment, replacement-order or simultaneous-batch rule changes.

RON: `PlayerMayAction(playerRef,
AttachPermanentToAPermanent(attachmentRef, filter))` in ordinary resolving
ActionLists, including accepted nested sequences, PlayerActions and delayed
bodies. Existing typed reference and contextual collection compilers validate
operands. The compiler adds no result binding for subsequent TheChosenPermanent
reads. Costs, static rules, source-entry and draw replacement bodies reject.
Other PlayerMayAction action families, invalid arities and out-of-scope/wrong-type
references reject at declaration time. Inventory assigns player_reference and
action roles to the wrapper's operands.

RON owns spelling, lexical scope and per-factory lowering. Mage owns optional
choice, legality and exact visits. Existing AttachedBecomesTapped event bindings,
ControllerOfWithLKI, AttachPermanentToChoice, permanentChoice, capture/clone frames,
protection, destruction/regeneration and stack state-action timing are reused.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

RON accepts `CreatePlayerEffectUntil(playerRef,
[MayPayLifeToProduceManaAsManaAbility(Integer(positive), fixedManaType), ...],
UntilEndOfTurn)`. Each operation produces one mana. Fixed mana symbols are
ManaProduceW/U/B/R/G/C. The wrapper can contain separate supported operations.
Ordinary resolving spell, activation, trigger, scoped and delayed bodies use
existing player-reference lowering. Costs, static rules, entry/draw replacements,
wrong roles/kinds/arities, missing references, zero/negative/dynamic life,
color choices and other durations reject during declaration.

Native `PlayerLifeManaThisTurn(player PlayerRef, life int, color core.Color)
ResolvingEffect` validates fixed positive life and saves the player at resolution.
`GetPlayerManaAbilities(player uuid.UUID) []PlayerManaAbilityInfo` reports
current affordable permissions. `ActivatePlayerManaAbility(player, id uuid.UUID)
error` pays and produces immediately, with no stack object. Direct callers must
supply priority; `PriorityActivatePlayerManaAbility` with PlayerManaAbilityID
integrates the priority handler. Shared payment planning supplies legitimate
mana windows while casting, activating or resolving a mana payment. The direct
API rejects arbitrary use during resolution. Player permissions do not tap a
permanent or emit permanent-activation events.

ManaSolverInputs adds AvailableLife. Each mana search state saves life spent,
with one shared budget across permissions; source plans have a distinct
PlayerManaAbilityID instead of a fake permanent identity. Life is minimized
before preservation score and activation count. Affordability, maximum X and
hypothetical mana read the same permissions without mutation. Total-cost trials
and commit preflight use the existing game clone and cost transaction. Commit
checks the complete remaining life budget and permission IDs before mutation,
including additional life costs. Multiple grants cannot duplicate available life.

Shared LifePayCost and life-loss events, mana production/replacements, pool
spending/X restrictions, resolution payment services, definition validation,
source/LKI reads, delayed-source inspection, priority, game cloning and cleanup
are reused. A permission saves no mutable target or result frame: only its
resolved player, source identity, positive cost, fixed color and unique ID.
Source departure, return, phasing or control changes do not revoke it or change
the payer. Clones hold separate permission lists. Cleanup expires each game alone.

### Contract, signatures and reuse

Supported ordinary resolving RON shapes:

- `CreatePermanentLayerEffect(permanentRef, [IsACopyOfPermanent(permanentRef, NoCopyEffects)])`
- The same shape with `CopyEffects([KeepColor])` instead of `NoCopyEffects`.

Both references use existing lexical permanent scopes and per-factory bindings.
There must be exactly one copy modification and one strict KeepColor symbol if
exceptions are present. Mixed lists, unsupported modifications, malformed kinds
or arities, wrong/unbound references, entry and draw replacement contexts reject
during declaration. Costs and static rules do not acquire resolving semantics.
Inventory now reports the subject as permanent_reference and exceptions as
copy_modification, including descendants inside the still-unsupported wrapper.

Native APIs:

- `CopyPermanent(recipient, subject PermanentRef, keepColors bool) ResolvingEffect`
- `(*Game).BecomeCopyOfPermanent(recipient, subject *Permanent, keepColors bool) error`

Mage owns exact current-visit checks, snapshot capture, physical identity,
complete rule replacement, static registration replacement, face-down status,
continued text, clone state and departure. RON owns syntax and scope validation.
There is no LKI fallback for missing operands. Waiting queries retain source
reads without resolving operands. KeepColor reads the recipient's copiable
colors, not ordinary color layers. Self-copy captures before replacement.
Pending triggers keep their old instructions; future triggers use fresh rules.
No entry event, entry replacement, zone move or counter event is introduced.
Damage, counters, control, attachments and status stay with the recipient.

Reuse: CaptureCopiableValues, CopyRetainColors, BuildEntryCopyWithText,
CardDefinitionPlan validation, physical departure restoration, existing target
legality, phase/visit identities, printed static wrappers, layer application,
ability-context isolation, pending frames, game COW cloning and delayed-source
inspection. The legacy partial P/T/keyword copy helper is not used or changed.
Unknown copy provenance remains an error.

The copied permanent holds an immutable replacement state with its snapshot,
continued intrinsic words and prepared current/post-cleanup definitions. Text
services preflight both outcomes before adding another word effect. This avoids
runtime declaration panics during cleanup. Old word effects keep their order and
lifetime across form changes, including an intermediate form with no matching
word. Paired object instructions continue once, rather than once per old rule.
New text on a copied visit uses the same preparation. Text expiry preserves the
static registration position. Donor text and ordinary layers remain outside copy
values. Current supported text durations are indefinite and end of turn.

### Contract, exact shapes and reuse boundary

New native API:

`MayCopyPermanent(player PlayerRef, recipient, subject PermanentRef,
keepColors bool) ResolvingEffect`

The existing resolvingCopyEffect now supports an optional typed player. Both
exact operands must resolve to present, unphased visits before a choice is
offered. Missing operands make no choice; LKI cannot make an impossible copy
available. The selected player decides at resolution. You uses the saved
ability controller, even if source control has changed. Direct native callers
can supply another typed player. Decline changes nothing and permits subsequent
instructions. Accept calls the existing BecomeCopyOfPermanent operation.
There is no mutable decision state in the declaration or factory.

RON accepts only:

- `MayAction(CreatePermanentLayerEffect(permanentRef,
  [IsACopyOfPermanent(permanentRef, NoCopyEffects)]))`
- The same form with `CopyEffects([KeepColor])`.

These are ordinary resolving action bodies, including targeted activations and
acquired upkeep triggers. Existing lexical reference rules apply. No player
scope, copy exception or replacement context was broadened. Entry/draw
replacement bodies, malformed arities/kinds, unbound/wrong references, mixed
modifications and AddAbilityVariable(ThisAbility) reject. Diagnostics now name
the unsupported copy modification instead of stopping at MayAction.

RON owns spelling, syntax, context and instance reference lowering. Mage owns
operand legality, the decision and snapshot/rule replacement. Reuse includes
CopyPermanent's exact visits, CaptureCopiableValues, retained copiable colors,
validated definitions, text continuation, layer/static replacement, source LKI
inspection, stack copying and game cloning. Existing mandatory-copy callers
keep their behavior. No cost, replacement-order or simultaneous-operation
contract changes. No Go-card fallback, partial registry or card-name branch was
introduced. No Go definitions, generators or broad DSL functions were removed;
their removal gates remain unmet.

### Contract, supported context and reuse boundary

Native APIs:

- `BindTriggeredAbility(build func(*TriggeredAbilityBinding) *GenericTriggered)
  *GenericTriggered` supplies one typed lexical self-reference. Its pure builder
  creates fresh abilities, targets and bindings. No game state is captured.
- `RetainCopyAbility(binding *TriggeredAbilityBinding) ResolvingCopyOption`
  adds that invoking declaration to the resulting copiable values.
- `CopyPermanent(recipient, subject PermanentRef, keepColors bool,
  options ...ResolvingCopyOption) ResolvingEffect` and
  `MayCopyPermanent(player PlayerRef, recipient, subject PermanentRef,
  keepColors bool, options ...ResolvingCopyOption) ResolvingEffect` preserve
  all existing calls. `Game.BecomeCopyOfPermanent` keeps its existing signature.

RON supports `AddAbilityVariable(ThisAbility)` alone or with one `KeepColor`
inside resolving `CopyEffects`, in either order. Both mandatory
`CreatePermanentLayerEffect` copying and its `MayAction` wrapper work. The lexical
producer is the acquired controller-upkeep `TriggerA` built by the existing
`AddAbility` adapter, including entry-copy additions and existing upkeep grants.
Donor bindings and attachments do not enter that scope. Unbound/wrong references,
duplicate operations, malformed arities, unsupported modifications and
entry/draw replacement contexts remain declaration errors.

The engine declares the typed reference before the trigger's event and body.
Inspection follows a finite declaration edge, not the recursive builder. Reads
must have a lexical producer; nil, zero-value, escaped and duplicate retention
options reject before gameplay. Definition plans include the new binding in
independent-build checks. A nonzero-size compiler marker keeps lexical plan
addresses distinct. No global last-action state or runtime ability-index lookup
is used.

At resolution, exact-visit and optional decision checks run first. The shared
copy operation adds `CopyAddTriggeredAbility(binding.build)` through
`WithModifications`. Pending bodies keep their original declaration even after
another resolution replaces the permanent's rules. Self-copy adds one instance
to the donor snapshot; copying another Doppelganger copies its instances and
adds one. Later copies see the gained instances as copiable values. Every build
has fresh targets and references. Stack copies and game clones keep independent
choices and object transitions.

Reuse includes `CaptureCopiableValues`, retained colors, validated definition
plans, entry-copy construction, text continuation, layer/static replacement,
source identity, target legality, event capture, stack copying, game cloning and
printed-card restoration. No cost, replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation
contract changed. No Go-card fallback, partial registry or card-name branch was
added. Go definitions, generators and broad DSL services remain in place because
the cutover/removal gates are not met.

### Signatures, boundaries and rules evidence

- Native API: `ControllerPlaysLand(player *PlayerBinding, land *PermanentBinding,
  ordinal *NumberBinding) landPlayPattern`, with `.AfterFirst()` and the existing
  `WhenEvent` service. All bindings are required and definition-validated. The
  base native pattern includes first plays; `AfterFirst` requires `Amount > 1`.
- `playLandCore` keeps the existing successful-play tracker and event path, and
  now includes `SourceIncarnation` from its actual entrant. Each event captures
  player, exact land visit and ordinal through shared event capture effects.
  No new history tracker, global last-action slot or mutable factory state exists.
- Exact RON shape on a permanent:
  `TriggerI(WhenAPlayerPlaysALand(SinglePlayer(You), IsCardtype(Land)),
  PermanentPassesFilter(Trigger_ThatLand,
  Not(IsFirstLandPlayedByPlayerThisTurn)), ActionList([...]))`.
  Only this negative historical predicate is supported. Other filters, scopes,
  predicates, malformed arities and tuple symbols reject. `Not` is not a general
  negation adapter. Body-local `Trigger_ThatLand` and `Trigger_ThatPlayer` lower
  to fresh typed bindings for each factory instance.
- The condition describes a fixed past event, not current battlefield state.
  Lowering uses the event ordinal filter rather than a mutable state condition:
  a later play, source departure, land departure, control change or turn-history
  reset cannot change which ordinal this play had. Thus the CR 603.4 predicate
  remains true at resolution without requiring the land to remain present.
- RON owns spelling, shape, lexical scope, inventory roles and lowering. Mage
  owns matching, typed snapshots and exact visit resolution. Existing event,
  trigger placement, clone, source LKI, damage and prevention services execute
  the rule. Land timing and failed-play state use the existing shared service.
  No payment, replacement-order or simultaneous-operation contract was changed.
- CR 305.1–4 distinguishes legal land plays, allowance history and direct entry.
  CR 603.1–4 establishes detection, saved trigger control and historical
  intervening conditions. CR 113.7a preserves pending source damage through
  departure. Existing exact-visit services preserve CR 400.7 identity.
- Fresh `go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card Fastbond` passed before changes.
  The two local Fastbond rulings are WotC rulings: all regular/additional plays
  count, and direct entry does not. No Scryfall note was used as a WotC ruling.

Source correction: all six Fastbond records formerly used the positive
`IsFirstLandPlayedByPlayerThisTurn`. `data/LEA.json` Oracle text states:

### Contract, exact shapes and engine reuse

- Native API: `func (p spellCastPattern) AfterFirstInstant() spellCastPattern`.
  Compose with `SpellCast()`, `ByOpponent`, existing contextual filters and
  `WithCaster`/`WithSpell`. Duplicate ordinal modifiers fail definition validation.
- `core.GameEvent.CastInstantOrdinal int` is the successful caster's current
  instant count, including this cast. Other spell types publish zero. The sole
  production spell-cast publisher, `pushCastSpellObject`, updates the existing
  `TurnTrackers` history before saving this event fact. No new tracker, global
  last-action slot, mutable factory state or parallel cast pipeline exists.
- Native matching requires `EvtSpellCast` and saved ordinal greater than one.
  It does not query mutable current history. Stack copies use the existing copy
  path and neither publish a cast event nor update the count. Failed casts do
  neither. Real casts of copied cards still use the ordinary cast path.
- Exact RON permanent rule:
  `TriggerA(WhenAPlayerCastsTheirNthSpellInATurn(Opponent,
  NotEqualTo(Integer(1)), IsCardtype(Instant)), actions)`.
  Only this player/filter/comparison/count shape is supported. Other filters,
  comparisons, integer values, symbols used as tuples, malformed arities,
  TriggerI and nonpermanent rule contexts reject through strict compilation.
  No general numeric or filtered-spell ordinal adapter is claimed.
- Factored the existing ordinary spell-cast lowering into
  `compileSpellCastTrigger`; both event forms build the same fresh per-instance
  typed spell/caster captures and action scope. Existing callers retain their
  behavior and text-layer declaration marker. The ordinal adapter adds only
  `AfterFirstInstant`; it does not extend body actions. Event-player life gain
  remains outside the existing RON body contract.
- `Trigger_ThatPlayer` saves the caster and `Trigger_ThatSpell` saves the exact
  stack identity. Neither adds a target. Separate pending events, source
  instances, spell/trigger copies and game clones keep their own captures.
  Source departure/return, phasing and control changes do not cancel pending
  damage. Normal event detection still excludes phased or abilityless sources.
- Existing turn tracking/reset, cast payment, trigger placement, typed captures,
  source LKI, damage, prevention, copying and cloning services execute the rule.
  No cost, replacement-order or simultaneous-operation contract changed.
- Inventory assigns `cast_ordinal_comparison` and `cast_ordinal_value` roles to
  the nested comparison/value, and existing player/spell-filter roles to the
  event operands. Strict collection loading remains atomic.
- CR 601.2/601.2i establishes a cast after successful payment; CR 603.2/603.3a
  establishes detection and saved trigger control. CR 707.10 excludes stack
  copies from casting. CR 113.7a/608.2h supplies pending source damage and LKI.
  Read these local sections and relevant API/rules-contract documentation.
- `go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card "Ichneumon Druid"` passed before editing.
  Read its complete local ruling file. Its one WotC ruling requires a separate
  instant count for each player. Candidate ruling files were also read; WotC
  rulings were not conflated with Scryfall notes.

### Exact contracts, dependencies and reuse

- Native API:
  `ExileEachWithControllerCounts(subjects PermanentSet,
  result *PlayerNumbersBinding) ResolvingEffect` and
  `DrawEachPlayerNumber(result *PlayerNumbersBinding) ResolvingEffect`.
- The producer selects exact present, unphased visits, deduplicates subjects and
  saves their controllers before replacement choices or movement. It resets both
  player counts on each execution. Tokens count although they do not persist in
  the engine's exile storage. Ownership does not select the drawing player.
- Factored `Game.ExilePermanents` through private `exilePermanents`, which returns
  actual departure facts. It now sends exile-destination `permanentGraveyardAction`
  proposals through the existing replacement pipeline in APNAP order, before
  any departure. Shared `performPermanentGraveyardAction` performs the moves.
  Cancellation, redirection away from exile and stale visits add no count.
  All existing batch callers keep their signature. Singular and linked exile
  paths are unchanged and are not claimed as new replacement adapters.
- The shared zone-change batch supplies simultaneous trigger observations and
  LKI. Indestructibility, regeneration and target protection do not prevent
  exile. Saved counts remain historical after zone/control changes.
- Reused `PlayerNumbersBinding`, `PlayerNumber`, number-frame copying/cloning,
  definition binding dominance, `EachPlayer` order and ordinary draw actions.
  Both draw amounts are read before any draw replacement runs. No global slot,
  new resolution map, alternate zone system or card-name branch was added.
- Exact RON producer: `Exile([EachPermanent(collection)], [])` in an ordinary
  resolving action sequence. The collection must conjunctively guarantee
  `IsCardtype(Creature)` for the supported consumer.
- Exact RON consumer: `EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer,
  DrawNumberCards(NumPermanentsOfTypeExiledThisWay(And([IsCardtype(Creature),
  ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(ActionPlayer))]))))`.
  ActionPlayer denotes the member whose saved count supplies that draw. It is
  not a general player reference introduced into the surrounding sequence.
- A private plan and fresh per-factory player-number binding connect producer
  and continuation. Later producers bind separate results. Results cannot be
  read before production or escape a branch. Other filters, count consumers,
  delayed reads, modifiers and entry/draw replacement contexts reject.
- Inventory assigns `permanent_filter` to the count filter and preserves its
  nested player-filter/reference roles. Atomic collection publication is intact.
- `go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card "Martyr's Cry"` passed before edits. Its
  complete local ruling file has one WotC ruling (battlefield creatures only),
  with no Scryfall notes. Local DRK Oracle text requires one draw per creature
  actually exiled for its former controller. CR 400.6–7, 406.2, 608.2c/e/f/i,
  614.5, 616.1, 111.7 and 702.26b establish the engine contract.

Contract before edits: a specified player must choose one current hand card at
resolution, if one exists, and put that exact visit on its owner's library top.
RON owns spelling and scope; mage owns required choice, identity and movement.
Acceptance includes empty hands, invalid choices, returned visits, owners,
post-move events, source sacrifice/phasing/LKI, copied abilities, pending clones,
replacement-modified draws, draw-trigger timing and payment rollback.

### Implemented contract and reuse

- Added `mage.PutChosenHandCardOnLibrary(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`.
  Nil and unbound declarations fail definition validation. An absent runtime
  player or empty hand makes no choice and moves nothing.
- The shared `ChooseCardFromHand` interface receives current hand candidates.
  Original visits are saved before the choice. A selected ID resolves to its
  canonical current card. Nil, foreign and stale choices use a valid original
  candidate in hand order. If none remains, no card moves. A returned visit
  cannot replace an original one, and a forged card cannot supply its data.
- Reused `handOperationPlayer`, shared hand visits and departure information,
  `RemoveFromHand`, `SetLibrary`, definition edges and source-read inspection.
  The canonical card moves to the owner's library top. Existing retained
  library order/visits remain intact under the shared visibility rules.
- One hand-to-library `EvtZoneChange` fires after movement. This instruction
  does not discard, reveal, draw, search or shuffle. Discard/draw replacements
  do not apply to it. Earlier draws still use shared draw replacements.
- No new global result, binding family, payment mechanism or zone subsystem.
  Saved resolving controllers, source LKI, copied abilities, delayed bodies
  and independent game clones use existing services.
- Exact RON shape: strict symbol `PutACardFromHandOnTopOfLibrary`, in ordinary
  resolving spell, activated, triggered (including source entry) and delayed
  action bodies. Default player is You. `PlayerAction` and nested
  `PlayerActions` retain their typed player scope. Arguments, costs, layers,
  entry replacement bodies and draw replacement bodies reject.
- `EachPlayerAction` remains unsupported for this symbol. A simultaneous
  multi-player choice batch requires a separate contract; this slice supplies
  one player's choice only.
- `go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card "Conch Horn"` passed before edits.
  Read its complete local ruling file: one WotC ruling dated 2004-10-04, no
  Scryfall notes. Local FEM Oracle text requires two draws, then a card from
  hand on top. CR 400.2–3, 400.7, 401.2, 608.2c–d, 113.7a, 117.2e and 603.3
  establish identity, destination, timing and source independence.

  use their existing scopes and instance bindings.

  one history predicate and at most one symbol `AnyPlayer` or `Opponent`.
  The permanent form accepts the history predicate alone, or one `And`
  containing one history predicate and supported characteristic filters.
  These source operands are independent across the two sets.

  The existing type filter reads the current permanent type.

  Nested history unions and duplicate player filters reject. History requires
  an ordinary resolving body; costs, static declarations, entry operations and
  draw replacement bodies do not gain this grammar. Singular damage recipient
  collections retain their existing grammar.

  PlayerSet) PlayerSet`, `PermanentsDealtDamageBy(DamageSourceRef, PermanentSet)

### Supported shape, boundary and engine reuse

Supported declaration:

`ref` is `ThisPermanent`, or `HostPermanent` on an Aura. Host modes can read
`Trigger_ThatPermanent`. Source modes retain source-tap context. Unsupported
modal event contexts, nested modal actions, invalid lists/arity, incompatible
references and cross-mode target reads still reject at declaration time.

`compileTapTriggerBody(Node, scope)` returns a per-instance builder with type
`func(mage.EventPattern, instanceBindings) *mage.GenericTriggered`.
It reuses `compileChooseOneModes` and `buildChooseOneModes`, with fresh target
namespaces and host bindings for each factory call. The nonmodal path keeps its
existing sequence and target construction. RON owns syntax and scope only.

Native execution uses `BecomesTapped`, `AttachedBecomesTapped`,
`WhenEvent`, `GenericTriggered.WithModes`, the legal-mode menu, trigger stack
placement, typed target groups, shared damage/prevention, LKI, stack copying
and game cloning. No new engine API or parallel execution path was necessary.
CR 603.3c–d and 700.2b–c require mode and target selection at placement;
CR 700.2f–g retains the chosen mode in copies. Resolution does not prompt again.
Pending triggers retain controller and source information after source departure,
control change or phasing. Resolution checks exact target visits and current
legality. Reattachment cannot change the captured host.

No mana payment, replacement ordering, simultaneous batch or zone lifecycle
contract changed. Aura casts use the existing transaction: unpaid and illegal
casts preserve hand and mana. Damage prevention uses the shared shield service.

### Supported shape, boundary and engine reuse

continuation. Each choice becomes an immutable concrete-keyword branch using

the enclosing targets. No mutable chosen-ability result is introduced.
`buildResolutionChoiceFor` preserves the explicit player scope. The existing
ChooseAnAbility grant adapter retains its former shape and tests.

RON owns spelling, arity, scope, diagnostics and branch lowering. Engine mechanics
reuse `ChooseAtResolution`, `ResolutionOption`, `Until`, `RemoveKeyword`, exact
permanent references, activation transactions, target legality, stack copying,
game cloning, native combat and cleanup. No new engine executor, API, state slot
or duplicated life cycle was needed. Inventory now reports choice operands as
keywords and the removal's TheChosenAbility operand as an ability reference.

CR 608.2b/d places target rechecks before the resolution choice. Both keyword
options remain available even if the creature lacks them, as Urborg's rulings
require. Copies choose separately; invalid chooser responses retain the existing
engine fallback to the first option. Pending abilities retain their controller
and source information after departure, return, phasing, control changes or
ability removal. Returned targets cannot supply old visits. Layer 6 removal
uses CR 611.2a/c and 613.1f and lasts through cleanup. Removing first strike does
not remove double strike. CR 510.4 and 702.7c retain strike history after first
strike damage. CR 509.1 and 702.14c make swampwalk removal useful before blockers
are declared; it does not insert blockers after declaration.

### Contract, signatures and ownership

Supported top-level permanent declaration:

```ron
ReplaceWouldDealDamage(
    AnAmountOfDamageWouldBeDealtByASourceToRecipient(
        GreaterThanOrEqualTo(Integer(threshold)),
        Or([IsCardtype(Instant), IsCardtype(Sorcery)]),
        Player(You)
    ),
    [DealDamageInstead(Integer(amount))]
)
```

The source filter can instead be one `IsCardtype`. An `Or` requires at least two
distinct valid types. The threshold is positive; the fixed replacement amount
is nonnegative and smaller than the threshold. Other comparisons, players,
recipient kinds, dynamic amounts, duplicate types, extra operations, resolving
bodies and entry/draw replacement bodies reject before factory publication.
There is no runtime declaration panic, card-name branch or Go-card fallback.

New compiler helpers:
`compileStaticDamageCap(n Node) (optionFactory, error)`,
`compileDamageCapSourceTypes(n Node) ([]core.CardType, error)` and
`fixedDamageCapAmount(n Node) (int, error)`.
RON owns spelling, arity, context and immutable lowering. Inventory reports the
amount event/comparison/operation, source filters, card types and player reads
with their separate roles.

New engine API:
`LimitPlayerDamageFromTypes(subject PlayerRef, threshold, amount int,
kinds ...core.CardType) StaticRule`. Definition validation checks the player,
threshold, amount and copied type list. The rule supplies a live static effect
and a per-cycle replacement. Current controller and exact source incarnation
are checked for each event. Source exit, phasing and ability removal suspend
it. Return installs a new rule; cleanup retains a live printed rule.

Reuse: `Static`, `funcContinuousEffect`, printed ability identity, cycle
replacements, `damageSourceHasCardType`, current/retained source information,
`DamageSource.SameObject`, `PlayerRef`, damage assignments/outcomes, affected
player replacement priority and APNAP choice, prevention, damage event bindings,
lifelink, state actions, activation/cast payments, stack copying and game cloning.
No parallel damage executor or replacement manager was introduced.

The shared replacement pipeline now accepts an internal
`damageBatchReplacement` with `matchesDamageBatch` and `replaceDamageBatch`.
`replacementCandidatesMatching` retains ordinary candidates and priorities
while allowing a grouped matcher. Simultaneous packets from one exact source
to the player share a threshold and replacement amount. Other sources, visits,
players and permanent recipients stay separate. Threshold accumulation saturates
at the threshold to avoid overflow. Applied records remain per packet, so later
redirection cannot cause a second use. No global last-event state is used.

CR 614.1a, 614.4–6 and 616.1 establish live replacement, one application and
rechecks after the affected player's choice. CR 609.7c supplies source-type
matching. CR 611.3a–b and 702.26b/d establish current control, static lifetime
and phasing. CR 120.3f/120.4b establish replaced damage amounts for lifelink
and damage events. The local Forethought Amulet WotC ruling confirms that
amounts one and two remain unchanged. No Scryfall note was substituted for a
WotC ruling. `go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card 'Forethought Amulet'` passed.

Ali from Cairo was checked as a possible reuse boundary: its complete RON record
and local WotC rulings require replacing the life-loss result while the full
damage is still dealt. It is not a damage-amount replacement. This slice does
not reuse or change the legacy minimum-life damage cap and does not claim Ali
as a new unlock.

case failed with life 17/23 instead of 18/22 for packets 1+2. Added the grouped
matcher through the existing batch pipeline, then confirmed that case passes.
No expected gameplay result was weakened.

### Supported contract, dependencies and reuse

Exact RON shape, on a permanent as a static rule:

`PlayerEffect(You, [DamageThatWouldReduceLifeTotalToLessThanNumberReducesItToThatNumberInstead(Integer(positive))])`.

The list must have exactly one operation. The player must be the strict `You`
symbol. Zero/negative/dynamic amounts, wrong arity, additional operations,
incompatible players and resolving-body use reject during compilation.
`compileDamageLifeFloor(Node) (optionFactory, error)` owns lowering and syntax.
The existing player-rule dispatcher supplies strict player and operation checks.
Inventory assigns the operand its numeric value role.

Native API: `LimitDamageLifeLoss(player PlayerRef, floor int) StaticRule`.
Definition validation requires a player and a positive floor. A fresh static
rule installs an exact-source cycle replacement through the existing static
ability lifecycle. Current control supplies You. Departure, phasing and ability
removal suspend it; return, phase-in and ability restoration reinstate current
rules. Cleanup retains printed rules. Clones have separate sources and life.

The internal `damageLifeLossAction` supplies player, loss amount and the proposed
life total before that loss. A local damage batch saves life-loss and life-gain
results when a result-floor rule is present. Actual gains from lifelink and
prevention pass through `prepareLifeGain`, including modifiers and replacements.
Their values enter the loss test. Aggregate damage life loss then passes through
the existing replacement pipeline, including affected-player choice, priority,
once-per-event application and rechecks. Both players choose in APNAP order. Life mutations finish before life and
damage events dispatch. Existing damage packets, source information, amounts,
outcomes, history, lifelink and source notifications remain shared. Nested batch
execution restores the prior frame. No global last-result slot was added.

Damage without the new result rule keeps its existing single-event and
prevention additional-effect order. Legacy minimum-life APIs and Go callers
remain unchanged. Direct life loss is unaffected. A player below the floor does
not gain life from this rule. Simultaneous lethal damage to the source keeps its
protection until state actions remove it.

Rules: CR 120.3a/f and 120.4b–d distinguish damage, its life-loss result and
simultaneous gains. The CR 120.4 example with Worship and Awe Strike requires
including actual simultaneous gains. CR 611.3a–b supplies live static behavior;
CR 614.4–6 and 616.1 supply replacement timing and rechecks. All three local Ali
rulings are WotC rulings: direct life loss is excluded, full damage still triggers,
and simultaneous lethal source damage retains protection. No Scryfall note was
used as a WotC ruling. `go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card 'Ali from Cairo'` passed.

### Contract, signatures and reuse boundary

RON now accepts this static rule on a permanent:

`EachPermanentStickyLayerEffect(And([IsNonCardtype(Creature), IsCardtype(Artifact)]), [LosesAllAbilities, AddCardtype(Artifact), AddCardtype(Creature), SetPowerAndToughnessBoth(ManaValueOfPermanent(EachablePermanent))], UntilEndOfTurn)`.

`compileStickyAnimation(Node) (optionFactory, error)` validates exactly two
conjuncts and four distinct modifications. Each list may be reordered. Missing,
duplicate or incompatible operations, a different subject/value, non-symbol
removal or duration, other durations, wrong arity and resolving-body use reject.
Inventory assigns permanent-filter, static-modification, static-value,
permanent-reference and duration roles to the operands.

Native API: `AnimateArtifactsUntilCleanupAfterExit() StaticRule`.
It has no mutable input or result binding. Each registered animation layer gets
its exact source incarnation through `bindCharacteristicEffect`. The per-pass
membership key includes the declaration, physical source and source incarnation.
Shared animation selection saves exact subject visits at layer 4. Layer 6 removes
all abilities; layer 7b uses each member's current mana value. Existing type
additions, dependency probes, ability-removal service, P/T reset/setters, modifiers,
counters, combat permissions, LKI and state actions remain the execution path.

`EffectManager.continueEffectsAfterSourceExit(*Game, *Permanent)` runs before
ordinary source-effect removal. A typed continuation interface replaces a
registered part in place only when its complete effect started in layer 4.
This retains its timestamp and all layer parts even if layer 6 removed the
source's ability. The independent effect expires at cleanup and continues to
select current noncreature artifacts, including new entrants after departure.
A present source keeps its static rule across cleanup. Source phasing suspends
the live rule without starting the departure duration. Returning sources have
new incarnation keys. Old continuations, new rules, separate physical copies
and game clones cannot overwrite each other's lifetime or member selections.
Changing a source's copiable rules is not departure and does not start the
continuation. An earlier visit's continuation remains independent.

Read both complete source records, the complete local WotC ruling, and local
ATQ Oracle data. `go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card "Titania's Song"` passed.
The WotC ruling preserves continuous-control restrictions for attacking and tap
abilities after animation. There are no local Scryfall notes for this card.
CR 205.1b, 302.6, 611.3a–c, 613.1d/f/g, 613.4b, 613.6–8, 514.2 and 702.26
supply the shared type, layer, cleanup and phasing contracts. The explicit
Oracle sentence supplies continuation after source departure. This is the
same static effect; it is not a newly resolving effect with frozen membership.

### Supported shape and engine boundary

RON accepts `ExchangeLifeTotalWithPlayer(playerRef)` in ordinary resolving
spell, activation, trigger and delayed bodies. Bare actions use `You`;
`PlayerAction` and `PlayerActions` supply one explicit action player. Existing
typed player references and per-instance bindings select both participants.
Costs, entry operations, draw replacement bodies, wrong arity, incompatible
references and unbound targets/events reject before gameplay. Inventory marks
the operand `player_reference`. RON owns syntax, scope and lowering only.

Native API: `ExchangeLifeTotals(first, second PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`.
It resolves both participants once and saves their totals before any ordinary
life mutation. Missing/same participants and equal totals do nothing. Negative
life totals remain valid. Unrepresentable differences return an error before
changing state. Shared replacement services prepare gain/loss in APNAP order.
Both ordinary mutations finish before life events. Replacement-modified or
replaced gains/losses retain the other leg's committed amount; actual amounts
supply events. Damage prevention and damage-only life floors do not redefine
this direct life exchange.

The missing eligibility prerequisite is included in this operation's contract:
`Game.CanGainLife(uuid.UUID) bool`, `Game.CanLoseLife(uuid.UUID) bool`,
`GameRules.AddCantGainLife(uuid.UUID)` and `AddCantLoseLife(uuid.UUID)`.
The last two register current layer-cycle flags. Reset clears them; clones
copy their maps. Layer recalculation handles continuous-source control,
phasing, ability removal and departure. The lifecycle tests explicitly apply
layers after raw phase operations, as required for cycle-based rule state.
Ordinary gains, direct losses, damage life loss, life costs, life-paid mana
queries/planning and resolution gain payments use the same eligibility checks.
Positive life costs recheck before resource mutation; zero payment remains legal.
`NewLifeLossAction(source, player uuid.UUID, amount int) *LifeLossAction` sends
direct loss through the existing affected-player replacement manager. Damage
retains its distinct damage/life-result pipeline and uses loss eligibility.
No new card-specific replacement, payment, event or source-identity system exists.

Existing typed references, captured source incarnations, LKI, delayed frames,
stack copies, clone isolation, payment transactions, upkeep conditions, target
legality, gain modifiers, draw replacements and event dispatch remain in use.
No Go-card fallback, production registry exception, card-name branch or global
action-result slot was added. No DSL API or Go card definition was removed;
their design removal gates remain unmet.

### Supported declaration, native boundary and dependencies

RON supports exactly:

```ron
ReplaceWouldDiscard(
    AnEffectWouldCausePlayerToDiscardACard(You),
    [MayAction(DiscardItToTopOfLibraryInstead)]
)
```

The declaration must be a battlefield permanent rule. Wrong event/player,
arity, operations, required destination, extra operations, other source zones,
spell statics, ordinary resolving actions and entry bodies reject.
`compileDiscardReplacement(Node, scope) (optionFactory, error)` validates this
shape and creates a fresh `WithStaticAbility(DiscardToLibraryReplacement())`
for each factory instance. Inventory assigns discard-event, optional-operation,
destination and typed-player roles without inventing general action bindings.

`DiscardToLibraryReplacement() ContinuousEffect` retains its public signature.
Its existing typed native rule supplies exact source incarnation, live ability,
phasing, current controller and effect-versus-cost cause checks. The private
optional prompt now identifies the selected card, including random discards.
It does not call a reveal service. Each card has an independent decision.

The shared discard batch now calls
`(*Game).orderDiscardDestinations([]*DiscardAction, core.Zone)` for graveyard
and library destinations. Library ordering uses the existing
`orderCardsByChoice` snapshots and invalid-answer fallback. Players order their
library cards in APNAP order before movement. The first selected card ends on
top; successive top insertions execute in reverse order. Old library cards stay
below new cards. All destination moves precede discard events. Native graveyard
ordering, replacement rechecks and cost transactions stay in their shared
services. No RON-specific zone executor or second replacement manager was added.

No public DSL API or Go card definition was removed. The runtime/definition/DSL
removal gates are still unmet. There is no Go-card fallback, card-name branch,
partial production registry, global action-result slot or game-time declaration
panic. The new API/rules documentation covers only this established contract.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

New public engine signature:
`RedirectNextDamageToPermanentFromSelectedSource(source DamageSourceRef,
player PlayerRef, destination PermanentRef, filter DamageSourceFilter)
ResolvingEffect`.

RON lowers exactly
`CreateFutureReplaceWouldDealDamage(NextTimeDamageWouldBeDealtThisTurnBySourceToRecipient(TheChosenDamageSource, Player(playerRef)), [DealToCreatureOrPlaneswalkerInstead(permanentRef)])`.
`compileSelectedSourceRedirect(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` dispatches
the new direction to `compileSelectedPermanentRedirect(Node, scope)
(effectFactory, error)`. Ordinary resolving bodies require a prior lexical
source-choice plan and valid typed references. Entry and draw replacement
bodies, malformed arities, extra operations and unbound reads reject.

The native installation and replacement retain the existing signatures for
reverse-direction callers. One direction flag changes the action recipient;
source information, exact source/destination visits, current filter checks,
selected permanent-spell continuation, waiting reference declarations, shared
batch replacement order, clone state and cleanup remain in their existing
services. All matching simultaneous packets redirect before the rule is used
up. Nonpositive damage, wrong sources/players and invalid destinations leave the
rule unused. Phasing suspends a destination; a phase cycle restores it. Return
cannot restore an old visit. Later target restrictions do not apply. Source
attribution, combat status, lifelink and damage events remain shared behavior.
No new payment service is added; existing activation transactions handle failed
payment without tap or stack publication.

No Go definitions, DSL APIs or production registry paths are removed. Complete
loading, runtime cutover and removal gates remain unmet. There is no Go-card
fallback, card-name branch, global result slot or game-time declaration panic.

### Baseline, candidate comparison and selection

A reusable native instruction completes the remaining activation prerequisite. | One run; high native interaction and RON test effort |

and the complete comparison records, including their nested operations.

dependencies were ready, and the other apparent multi-card family needs
distinct contracts. No smaller ready shared slice credibly completes both
prevention cards. Estimated gain was one unique name and six records.

### Contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

Native `ActivateManaAbilityOfEach(player PlayerRef, filter PermanentFilter)
ResolvingEffect` selects matching present visits controlled by the resolved
player. That player chooses order, ability, colors and variable output.
Each visit supplies at most one successful activation. Remaining options are
reevaluated after each success. Exact visit, ability identity and control are
checked after choices. Phasing suspends a source; return cannot replace it.
Zero output remains a mana ability. Failed payments publish no partial costs
or stack object and do not block other options. X belongs to each activation;
the enclosing X is restored. An unaffordable chosen X falls back to zero after
the ordinary transaction rejects it. Working state is local to Apply.

`IsActivatedManaAbility`, ordinary `CanActivate`, mana cost planning with a
reserved tap source and `ActivateAbilityByIndex` supply the existing rules.
Shared payment transactions handle mana, life, counter and sacrifice costs,
rollback, immediate resolution, replacements, bonuses and mana events.
There is no second payment solver or RON execution logic in the engine.

RON accepts `PlayerAction(playerRef,
ActivateAManaAbilityOfEachPermanentAndLoseUnspentMana(And([IsCardtype(Land),
ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(ActionPlayer))])))` in ordinary resolving
bodies. The two clauses can be reversed. Other filters, extra clauses,
malformed arguments, unbound players, entry and draw replacement bodies reject.
`compileForcedManaPlayer(Node, scope) (playerReferencePlan, error)` validates
that shape; `compileForcedMana(Node, scope) ([]effectFactory, error)` lowers
instructions without a consumer. The saved-mana producer also recognizes it.
Each factory snapshots one typed player for both activation and loss, then
uses existing `LostManaBinding`, `LoseUnspentManaInto` and `AddLostManaFor`.
`TheManaLostThisWay` retains lexical dominance and local PlayerActions scope.

### Contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

Native `PreventDamageByThisTurn(source PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect` saves
one exact source visit at resolution through `permanentInformationReference`.
Definition checks reject nil, unbound and non-information references. A saved
source from a pending or delayed body can install the rule after departure.
Both combat and noncombat damage from that visit are prevented until cleanup.
Return creates a different visit. Control changes and phase cycles keep identity.
The rule does not require the source to keep its former abilities or types.

The existing `combatSourcePreventionReplacement` gains `allDamage bool`.
Existing callers keep their combat-only default. The new operation enables
all damage and reuses exact source matching, the shared prevention marker,
replacement choices, unpreventable damage handling, damage batches, outcomes,
lifelink, cloning and end-of-turn expiry. No second damage pipeline is added.
Existing `waitingPreventionPermanents` supplies the installed source reference.
The new instruction declares direct source reads to waiting delayed queries.
Queries do not install rules, make choices or substitute returned sources.

RON `compileSourceDamagePrevention(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` accepts:
`CreatePreventDamageUntil(DamageWouldBeDealtByPermanent(permanentRef),
[PreventThatDamage], UntilEndOfTurn)` in ordinary resolving bodies, including
delayed bodies. `compileCombatPrevention` validates outer arity before dispatch.
The source uses `compilePermanentRef` and per-factory `instanceBindings`.
Missing/extra operands, unbound or incompatible references, other operations,
other durations, nonresolving, entry and draw replacement contexts reject.
Inventory gives the event operand the `permanent_reference` role.

RON spelling, roles and lexical scopes remain in `ron`; damage mechanics remain
in `mage`. The complete LEG Kry Shield record uses this instruction with the
existing target, payment and temporary-value services. No Go definition, broad
DSL API or production registry path was removed. Cutover gates remain unmet.

panic or partial production registry. RON source bytes remain unchanged, so no

implement the remaining self-death or ownership/exile capabilities.

### Exact supported contract and reuse boundary

Native API:

```go
RedirectNextDamageToPlayer(subject PermanentRef, player PlayerRef,
    amount ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect
```

Resolution saves an exact permanent visit, a player and a positive finite budget.
Nonpositive native amounts install nothing. The rule lasts until exhaustion or
cleanup. It redirects from a present creature or planeswalker; phased, absent,
returned and wrong-incarnation subjects cannot supply damage. Control changes
keep the saved subject and destination. Separate installations, copied abilities
and clones keep separate budgets. The subject's current controller allocates
across simultaneous packets through bounded number choices and legal fallback.

RON ordinary resolving bodies accept precisely:

```text
CreateFutureReplaceWouldDealDamage(
  NextAmountOfDamageThatWouldBeDealtThisTurnToRecipient(
    Integer(positiveAmount), Permanent(permanentRef)),
  [DealToPlayerInstead(playerRef)])
```

Existing typed source, target, saved-event/member and attachment plans supply
permanent references. Existing typed player plans supply the destination.
Malformed, unbound and wrong-role operands reject at compilation. Dynamic RON
amounts, nonpositive amounts, other recipients/operations and entry/draw
replacement contexts reject. Delayed ordinary bodies use their saved context.
The dispatcher checks the event before selected-source redirection lowering.
RON spelling and lexical scopes remain in `ron`; reusable mechanics remain in
`mage`. Inventory already assigns the amount and recipient their correct roles.

The existing affected-player replacement pipeline selects the rule, rechecks
both portions and retains prior replacement uses. Original and redirected
portions preserve source identity, LKI, combat classification and targeting
cause. Both execute in one simultaneous damage batch through existing life,
lifelink, history and event services. The prevention/redirection prohibition
keeps the budget. Prevention before redirection spends only remaining proposed
damage; prevention after redirection does not restore the budget.

Per-action packet ancestry preserves all positive redirected outcomes for the
original instruction. Portions of that input which converge on the same
recipient from the same source combine after replacements. This keeps one
source damage event instead of duplicate events from multiple shields. Existing Eye for an Eye expansion marks its added spell
damage as a separate instruction, so it remains excluded from the original
results. Scalar amounts sum the original instruction's portions. Plural results
retain separate recipients and source snapshots. A multi-recipient result does
not invent a singular player/permanent binding. Existing singular clamped-result
reads retain their one-outcome requirement. Result snapshots clone separately.
The obsolete internal expanded-action count was replaced by ancestry; no broad
DSL function was removed. Instruction-local prevention now spends one amount
across descendants instead of renewing prevention for each split portion.

The waiting redirection service includes active finite rules' exact subjects,

existing `PermanentTarget.opponentOwned` behavior through typed declarations and
definition inspection; it adds no second targeting pipeline. Ownership is read

inside `And`. The existing `SinglePlayer(You)` shape remains supported.

`Or` forms reject. Collection and ante-card filters keep their separate scopes.

transactions, saved ability controllers, stack copies and clone services do the

### Contract, exact shapes and reuse boundary

In ordinary resolving action lists, the adjacent forms
`MayCost(PayLife(Integer(n)))` or
`PlayerMayCost(playerRef, PayLife(Integer(n)))` and
`IfElse(condition, [true_actions], [false_actions])` lower as one operation.
`n` is a fixed nonnegative integer. The bare condition is `CostWasPaid` or
`CostWasntPaid`; the latter reverses the branches. Both action lists must be
nonempty. Nested and adjacent pairs keep their own results. Existing typed
player scopes supply the payer. Results cannot escape their pair.

`ron.compilePaymentBranches` reuses `compileCosts` and fresh `LifePayCost(n)`
declarations. The existing native signature is
`PayOrElse(player PlayerRef, costs CostGroup, paid, unpaid ResolvingEffect)
ResolvingEffect`. No new engine API or payment-result slot is needed. Shared
`tryResolutionCostPaymentFor`, total-cost transactions and life services handle
affordability, choices, permission, rollback, replacements and events. Exact
life is payable. Positive life costs cannot be paid with insufficient life or
a life-loss prohibition. Zero life requires acceptance even at nonpositive
life. Missing payers execute neither branch. Payment replacement cancellation
keeps the accepted paid result; damage prevention cannot prevent life payment.
CR 118.3, 118.5, 118.10–12, 119.4 and 119.8 establish the payment contract.
CR 113.7a, 400.7, 608.2b/h and 702.26b supply existing source, LKI, legality and
phasing behavior. No replacement-order or simultaneous-operation rule changes.

Dynamic life, `Or` alternatives, mandatory payments, malformed values, empty
branches and unbound players remain declaration errors in this shape. Existing
fixed-mana two-branch callers retain their behavior. Go definitions, registry
cutover and broad DSL removal gates are not reached.

### Exact shapes, signatures and reuse boundary

`DefendingPlayerOf(attacker PermanentRef) PlayerRef` is a reusable engine query.
It resolves the exact present attacker and checks `IsAttackingIncarnation` before
using the existing two-player `combatDefendingPlayerID` service. There is no
fallback from a missing, phased or returned attacker to another object or player.
An attacked planeswalker leaving does not change the two-player defender.
After combat, phasing or control-change removal, no current attacker is supplied.
The query intentionally has no LKI semantics. It changes no existing player
reference and adds no target-controller or state-condition declaration shape.

RON accepts `ControlledByPlayer(PlayerOrControllerOfPlaneswalkerCreatureIsAttacking(ThisPermanent))`
in `TheNumberOfPermanentsOnTheBattlefield` inside live static P/T values. It can
stand alone or appear in nonempty nested `And` filters with existing static count
operands. The attacker must be a symbolic source permanent. Host, target, player,
event and callable references reject. Resolving, entry and draw-replacement
contexts reject. Other static count support is retained, including entry-count
validation; this slice does not broaden those entry operations.

`compileStaticAttackerController(Node, scope) (mage.PlayerRef, error)` owns this
RON declaration. `compileStaticCountCollection(Node, scope) (permanentSetFactory, error)`
combines validated controller and existing characteristic sets. Existing
`PermanentsControlledBy`, `IntersectPermanents`, `CountPermanents`, `Static`,
`While` and `SetBasePowerToughness` perform execution. There is no new layer or
combat state. `playerRefReadsSourcePermanent` retains the new reference's explicit
source read for waiting delayed bodies without resolving it. Inventory traversal
reports its child as `permanent_reference` under `player_reference`.
No public DSL API was removed; the runtime cutover and removal gates remain unmet.

### Contract and reuse boundary

RON accepts these exact shapes in ordinary resolving sequences, including
conditional and delayed bodies:

- `PutCardFromHandIntoPlayersHand(TheCardRevealedFromHandThisWay, playerRef)`
  after a dominating lexical reveal producer.
- `PutCardFromAnywhereIntoPlayersGraveyard(ThisCard, playerRef)` for a permanent
  source. `ThisCard` is a symbol reserved here for the physical source.

Wrong arity, callable symbols, wrong-kind and unbound references, branch escape,
and cost/static/entry/draw-replacement use reject during definition compilation.
RON owns spelling, context and binding checks. Inventory reports the operands as
`card_reference` and `player_reference`.

Native APIs are `PutHandCardInHandFor(card CardRef, player PlayerRef)
ResolvingEffect` and `PutSourceCardInGraveyardFromAnywhere(player PlayerRef)
ResolvingEffect`. The former checks the saved exact hand visit. The latter
uses the effect's physical source ID across later zone visits. It does not
extend ordinary `CardRef` lifetimes or search for a card by name.
Both validate the selected player. The owner's corresponding destination takes
precedence under CR 400.3. Being in the same destination already makes no move.
An ownership change can leave a card in another player's graveyard; moving it
to the owner's graveyard gives it a new visit and a departure event.

Nonbattlefield movement uses `CardZoneMoveAction` through the shared replacement
pipeline. The current visit is retained and checked again after replacements.
The affected player is the owner; `WithExile` retains subject identity.
Existing hand/library/graveyard/ante/exile/command storage and stack removal
services supply movement and history. A physical zone query excludes ability
objects on the stack: a pending ability does not move its source to the stack.
Battlefield movement reuses `PutPermanentIntoGraveyard` for exact identity,
phasing, replacement, LKI, creature-death history and departure events.
Phased sources cannot move. Events follow placement. Hand transport is not
discard; direct graveyard transport is not sacrifice. The two instructions
are sequential, not a new simultaneous batch contract.

Instance factories, pending abilities, copied abilities, delayed frames and
clones use existing source/controller and card-binding storage. Waiting queries
retain explicit source/player reads without running movement or reveal effects.
No global result slot, card-name branch, Go-card fallback or production registry
change was added. No DSL API was deleted; the removal gates remain unmet.

### Exact supported contracts and reuse boundary

RON accepts the symbol `XCantBeZero` in `ActivatedWithModifiers` with an X mana
payment. It lowers to `mage.WithActivationMinimumX(1) mage.ActionOption`.
Duplicate, callable, non-X and invalid-context declarations reject. Native
validation requires one positive minimum on an activated action with an X mana
cost. The activation entry point rejects announced X below the minimum before
target choices or costs. Availability queries test minimum affordability without
changing X, tapping, paying mana or creating a stack object. A defined X below
the minimum makes the action unavailable. Existing callers retain their behavior.
Text-context comparison retains the scalar minimum; unsupported spell-text
reconstruction paths reject the new activation restriction.

RON accepts the exact operation list:

`LookAtTheTopNumberCardsOfLibrary(value,
[PutAGenericCardOnTopOfLibrary,
PutTheRemainingCardsOnTheBottomOfLibraryInARandomOrder])`.

The current typed player scope supplies viewer and library. Resolving bodies,
future draw replacements and delayed bodies are supported. Entry bodies,
incorrect operation lists, arities, callable symbols and unbound values reject.
Inventory records value and library-operation roles separately.

`mage.SelectLibraryTopAndBottomRestRandomly(viewer, library PlayerRef,
count ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect` reads count once and uses shared private
inspection, `ChooseCardFromLibrary`, library visits and random-bottom placement.
The chooser receives copies. A nil or foreign choice uses the first eligible
card. The chosen card remains on top; other inspected cards go below the
untouched tail. There is no draw, public reveal, full-library shuffle or zone
change in this effect. Empty libraries and nonpositive computed counts do
nothing. Fixed negative counts and missing operands reject at definition time.
The effect checks every saved visit before placement; departure and return
cannot supply an old selection. The chosen card and untouched tail retain
their visits; only the bottomed group is removed before random placement. Waiting source queries declare typed operands
without reading counts, inspecting libraries, choosing cards or consuming RNG.

The existing future draw replacement saves X and the resolution frame, consumes
each rule before running its body, restores the outer frame and lets another
replacement modify the generated draw. Source departure, return, control change
and phasing do not cancel the installed effect. Cleanup expires it. Copies,
separate factories, players and game clones keep independent use and X. No
replacement pipeline, global result slot, card-name branch, Go-card fallback or
partial production registry was added. No DSL function or Go definition was
removed; the removal gates remain unmet.

### Contract, signatures and boundaries

- `PlayerOrControllerOfDamageTarget(target *DamageTargetBinding) PlayerRef`
  reads the declared player or the exact permanent visit's current controller.
  Departure and phasing use saved information. Return cannot substitute a new
  visit. Unbound reads supply no player. The projection retains the original
  target declaration for validation; it does not create a second target.
- `CopySpellFor(player PlayerRef, spell StackObjectRef) ResolvingEffect`
  copies a present spell under the explicit player's control with optional new
  targets. `MayCopySpellFor` has the same signature and adds a separate copy
  choice. Neither copies abilities, absent spells or spells that left the stack.
  Both use `Game.CopyStackObjectDirect`; `ThisSpell` supplies the exact resolving
  spell, including a resolving copy. No parallel copy or event pipeline was added.
- RON accepts `PlayerOrControllerOfPermanent(recipientRef)` for a declared
  singular damage target. `CopySpellAndMayChooseNewTargets(ThisSpell)` and
  `MayAction(CopySpellAndMayChooseNewTargets(ThisSpell))` work in ordinary spell
  bodies and explicit `PlayerAction`. Permanent-source, activated, delayed,
  entry and draw replacement contexts reject self-copy declarations.
- `PlayerActions` accepts `PlayerMayCost` and its adjacent continuation through
  the shared action-sequence compiler. Its existing `SnapshotPlayer` saves the
  player before costs. `ActionPlayer` supplies payment, optional copy and control
  without reading a changed target controller after payment.
- Factories retain separate target declarations and player bindings. Existing
  resolution frames and game cloning keep state separate. Existing copy services
  preserve X, modes, source facts, copiable text, targets and target visits.
  New targets use shared legality checks. Copies are not cast and can be answered
  before they resolve. Copy resolution/countering does not add a graveyard card.

RON owns names, shapes, scope, diagnostics and inventory roles. Native code owns
information and copying. Shared damage, prevention, payment rollback, LKI,
player snapshots, stack priority and copy services are reused. There are no
Go-card fallbacks, name branches or partial registries. No Go card definitions
or DSL functions were removed; cutover and removal gates remain unmet.
