### Contract and reuse boundary

- `CombatOpponentsWithLKI(subject PermanentRef) PermanentSet` reads the exact
  current or saved combat visit through `readPermanentInformation` and
  `snapshotCombatOpponents`. Existing immutable LKI retains the relation after
  source departure. Only present, unphased creatures of the saved opponent
  visits are selected. The source or opponent returning cannot replace a visit.
  Later combat removal or control change does not erase a departure relation.
  Phase cycles retain identity; an opponent phased at resolution is excluded.
- The engine primitive validates information-compatible typed references.
  Nil and undeclared bindings reject through ordinary definition validation.
  Waiting delayed-source analysis recognizes explicit source reads without
  evaluating the collection. Existing clone and resolution state services apply.
- RON accepts `Or([BlockedDeadAttacker, WasBlockingDeadDefender])`, in either
  order, as a permanent collection in a permanent-source death resolving body.
  Both distinct symbols are required, once each. Ordinary `And` intersects it
  with a creature filter. Individual symbols, wrong shapes, extra operands and
  unrelated event contexts reject before factories are published.
- The existing `compileSourceDeathCardTrigger` supplies a fresh permanent
  binding per factory and captures the exact dying incarnation. No global
  last-action state, target substitution or runtime declaration panic was added.
- `DestroyEachWithoutRegeneration` supplies one simultaneous destruction group
  through shared replacements. Shroud does not apply; indestructibility and
  destination replacements retain their behavior. Regeneration cannot save an
  affected creature. The old live-only `BlockingOrBlockedBy` and all callers
  remain unchanged.

RON owns spelling, shape, scope and semantic inventory roles. Mage owns the
information projection. Existing combat, departure/LKI, death events, phasing,
copying, cloning and destruction supply execution. No new parallel mechanics,
Go-card fallback, card-name branch or partial production registry was added.
No Go definitions, generators or DSL functions were removed: the design's
cutover/removal gates remain unmet.

### Contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

- `CastingRequirement(condition StateCondition) *ActionDefinition` is an engine
  declaration for an `ActionSpell` with `WithCastingCondition` and no resolving
  instruction. This reuses the existing casting gate, definition validation,
  castability queries, payment transactions, card copying and stack resolution.
  There is no second legality or payment implementation. It grants no casting
  permission. Cast copies check the requirement; stack copies and resolution do
  not. Typed nil, unbound and battlefield-source conditions reject validation.
- RON accepts exactly one top-level
  `CastEffect(CantBeCastUnless(NoPermanentsPassFilter(filter, OnTheBattlefield)))`

### Contract, boundaries and evidence

Engine API:
`PayChosenExileOrElse(player PlayerRef, subjects PermanentSet, result *NumberBinding, paid, unpaid ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.
It offers one optional exile payment, including zero. A payer can choose other
players' permanents when they belong to the declared set. The complete selected
subset is checked for exact visits, presence, phasing and membership before any
move. An invalid selection takes the unpaid branch without a partial payment.
This contract covers one exile payment, not a compound total cost.

Reuse `choosePermanentSubset`, `TokensCreatedWith`, exact source/LKI references,
`Game.exilePermanents`, shared replacement ordering and zone batches. All
replacement choices precede departures; events see the simultaneous batch.
Replacement-modified or canceled moves still pay the cost (CR 118.11–12), but
the result counts actual exile moves, including tokens. The binding is written
only in the paid branch and restored afterward. Definition validation rejects
unpaid and subsequent reads. Nested payments, ability copies, game clones and
delayed bodies retain independent state. Source-read metadata preserves waiting
and departed producer references without executing payments early.

RON accepts exactly
`MayCost(Exile([AnyNumberOfPermanents(TheCreatedTokens)], []))`
and an adjacent nonempty `If` or `Unless` continuation with a strict
`CostWasPaid` or `CostWasntPaid` symbol. `NumPermanentsExiledThisWay` is a strict
symbol available only on that payment's paid path. Context: ordinary
permanent-source resolving bodies, including delayed bodies. Entry and draw
replacement bodies reject. Other payments, selections and modifiers remain
unsupported. One unambiguous source token producer is required by the existing
link validator. Each factory builds its own count binding; no global action
slot, card-name branch, fallback or partial registry was added.

The semantic inventory distinguishes resolution exile selection, its linked
permanent collection reference and its numeric result. RON source and vocabulary
snapshot are unchanged. No source defect was found. The full Tetravus Oracle

commands passed. Tetravus's four WotC rulings establish counter provenance
independence, orphan token survival, exact producer links and separate upkeep
triggers. Season's two and Nafs Asp's four WotC rulings establish their deferred
prerequisites. No Scryfall note was used as a WotC ruling.

### Supported shapes, dependencies and engine boundary

RON owns the `resolutionTokensPlan`, lexical producer dominance, spelling,
context checks and fresh instance bindings. In an ordinary resolving action
sequence, `CreateTokens([TokenWithPT(...)], [])` or the named prototype form,
including `NumberTokens`, can supply later `TheTokensCreatedThisWay` collection
reads. `compileTokenCreationWithResult` lowers the producer to the existing
`CreateTokenCopiesInto`; reads use existing `FromCreatedTokens`. A later
producer has a different plan. Optional and conditional branch scope does not
leak a producer to the outer continuation. Each factory builds fresh bindings.
Token-copy result producers, draw replacement bodies and combinations with
persistent `TheCreatedTokens` producer links remain explicit rejections.

`CreateFutureTrigger(WhenAPermanentLeavesTheBattlefield(TheTokensCreatedThisWay),
ActionList(body))` lowers to the new engine service:

`WhenAnyLeaves(subjects PermanentSet, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.

It saves the set's present, unphased visits and installs one shared delayed
subscription. An empty set installs nothing. The first exact departure consumes
the whole subscription, including simultaneous member departures. The event
introduces no member, player or amount binding. Shared departure snapshots,
trigger queueing, APNAP, replacement processing and captured delayed frames
retain rules ownership. Saved member slices are copied in game clones and
included in waiting delayed-source queries without executing the body.

### Contract and reuse boundary

`compileContextualCollection(Node, scope) (permanentSetFactory, error)` now
accepts `ExceptFor(collection)` with exactly one supported permanent collection
in ordinary resolving bodies, including delayed bodies. It builds:

`mage.WithoutPermanents(mage.MatchingPermanents(mage.AnyPermanent), excluded)`.

The existing engine signature is
`WithoutPermanents(subjects, excluded PermanentSet) PermanentSet`.
`And`/`Or`, nonempty nested combinations, nested exclusions, singular typed
references and player-scoped collections compose without a new reference role.
Each factory uses its existing `instanceBindings`; no execution state is stored
in the AST or a global action result. New forms reject in entry, draw replacement
and nonresolving contexts. The original exact
`ExceptFor(NotControlledSinceBeginningOfTurn)` form keeps its prior contexts.
Singular target filters keep their existing supported forms.

The engine compares permanent IDs and incarnations. Collections read live,
unphased membership when the instruction resolves. A return cannot inherit an
excluded saved visit. Control change preserves identity; phasing excludes action
subjects and a phase cycle preserves the visit. Delays and copies retain saved
source/target frames and copied controllers. `permanentSetReadsSourcePermanent`
already traverses both difference operands, so waiting queries retain excluded
source facts without executing actions. Existing tap/destruction services own
batch timing, replacements and regeneration. Exclusion pays no cost, makes no
choice and creates no persistent state. No rollback or replacement ordering
algorithm changed.

### Contract, engine boundary and source evidence

New engine signatures:

- `CardPaymentFact{Filter CardFilter, Result *NumberBinding}`.
- `DiscardCardCostWithFacts(facts ...CardPaymentFact) Cost`.

This is a one-card discard cost, with one independently bound 0/1 result per
predicate. The shared discard pipeline chooses replacements first, reads the
chosen card immediately before its move and retains results only for completed
discards. Graveyard and face-up exile destinations retain matches. An unrevealed
hidden destination supplies zero for every predicate, including negative ones,
because characteristics are undefined (CR 701.9c). The cost has no type/color
restriction; it remains payable with any hand card. Existing filtered costs keep
their separate requirement for known payment characteristics.

Payment preparation, hand-visit locking, replacement order, events and movement
remain in shared engine services. Results publish through the existing
transaction `paidNumbers` and saved-number frames, not a global last discard.
They survive later movement, return, source departure and phase cycles. Copies,
clones, interleaved transactions and delayed frames remain independent. Direct
activation and spell additional costs support this engine API. Nil/duplicate
bindings, missing producers, zero filters, optional/alternative wrappers and
resolution-payment use reject at definition validation.

The rollback test found a concrete shared-engine gap: installing a discard

### Contract, boundaries and source evidence

New engine signatures:

- `DamageSourceHasName(name string) DamageSourceFilter`.
- `DamageReceivedThisTurnFromOtherSources(subject PermanentRef,
  from DamageSourceFilter) ResolutionValue`.

The engine stores positive final damage amounts, exact recipient visits and
source snapshots through `DamageSystem.ExecuteDamageToCreature`. Prevention,
redirection and other replacements have already selected the actual recipient
and amount. Simultaneous packets all enter history before damage events fire.
Both permanent and spell sources can contribute. Self-damage excludes the exact
recipient visit, rather than every later object with that card ID. Player damage
cannot contribute. Historical source properties come from damage time under
CR 608.2i; later changes, departure or return cannot change the recorded name.
This is separate from the source LKI used when the dead creature deals new damage
under CR 608.2h. No global last-damage result or card-name execution branch exists.

History remains through phasing, damage removal and cleanup priority. Final turn
cleanup clears it. Game clones deep-copy entries and source snapshots; later
writes and cleanup remain independent. Saved permanent references read departed
visits without acting on them. `resolutionValueReadsSourcePermanent` declares
source reads for waiting delayed queries. Queries cannot apply the delayed body.
Invalid/unbound subjects and empty name filters fail definition validation.

RON supports exactly:

- `TheAmountOfDamageDealtToPermanentThisTurnBySources(subject,
  And([Other(subject), IsNamed(NamedCard(name))]))` in ordinary resolving bodies.
  The two terms may appear in either order. Both subjects must identify the same
  typed compiler binding. Other source-filter compositions remain rejected.
- `DeadPermanentDealsDamage(amount, recipient)` inside a source permanent death
  event, including its saved resolving context. The event supplies
  `Trigger_ThatPermanent` through the existing per-factory permanent binding.
  Existing `DamageSourceOf`, `DealDamageFrom`, arithmetic and recipient services
  supply source LKI, legal targets, protection, replacements and damage events.

RON retains syntax and scope ownership; mage retains damage, identity, history,
cloning and cleanup. Entry and draw replacement contexts, unrelated trigger
sources, malformed arities, mismatched exclusion references, missing/duplicate
filter terms and empty names reject before gameplay. No Go-card fallback,
production partial registry, broad DSL export or existing caller was removed.
No removal gate has been reached.

### Supported contract, rules and reuse boundary

RON accepts `MayAction(ChooseAnAttackingCreatureForBlockerToBlock(filter, ref))`
in ordinary resolving spell, activation and trigger bodies. The outer arity is
one; the inner arity is two. The filter uses supported contextual permanent
collections. The ref uses typed permanent bindings from its own factory/scope.
The current typed action player makes the optional choice at resolution.
Unbound refs, malformed shapes/filters, a bare required choice, entry operations
and draw replacement bodies reject before gameplay. Inventory identifies the
first operand as a permanent collection and the second as a permanent reference.

New mage API:
`MayHavePermanentBlockAttacker(PlayerRef, PermanentRef, PermanentSet) ResolvingEffect`.
The engine intersects candidates with current attackers of the blocker's defending
player. It saves exact visits before the choice and rechecks them before commit.
The choice does not target the attacker. Declining does not undo prior removal.
No LKI object can block; absent, returned and phased visits are excluded. A phase
cycle before spell resolution keeps the target visit but has removed its old
combat membership, so it cannot unblock its former attacker through removal.

The internal reusable signature is
`(*Game).addEffectBlockers([]effectBlockAssignment) bool`; each assignment holds
`blocker, attacker capturedPermanent` values. It validates every visit before
committing any member. A stale member rejects the complete batch. Band expansion,
combat membership and block history are complete before any new event is emitted.
It reuses `Combat.AddBlockerIncarnation`, `recordBlockHistory`, and the existing
new-blocker, pair, group and becomes-blocked event services. Existing blocked
attackers do not become blocked again. The action does not rerun declaration,
change declaration-only alone snapshots, tap creatures, make an attack, produce
whole-step/unblocked events, or pay a cost. Existing callers are unchanged.

Declaration restrictions (including tapped status, evasion, protection, menace,
block capacity and declaration limits) do not gate this direct blocking effect.
This follows CR 509.1a–f's declaration boundary and 509.3a–f's effect transitions;
there is no `could block` condition in False Orders. Sorrow's Path explicitly has
that condition and still needs its separate feasibility contract. CR 506.4,
509.1g/h, 509.3a–g, 509.4, 510.1 and 702.26 establish combat membership,
transitions, damage and phasing. Source/target exact identity follows CR 400.7
and 608.2b/c. Read the local rules sections using the rules index.

Read all five complete False Orders records, complete Sorrow's Path, Season of
the Witch and Nafs Asp records, their complete local ruling files, and the local
Oracle text for False Orders and the ranked candidates. All four
`go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card "<name>"` checks passed. Their local rulings
are WotC rulings; no Scryfall notes were conflated with those rulings. False
Orders' ruling preserves already-triggered block abilities. Sorrow's Path's
rulings establish the separate could-block and swap contracts; that card is not
claimed as executable. No source-data defect was found in the selected records.
RON sources and the vocabulary snapshot were not changed by this slice.

The immutable effect keeps no global result slot or per-factory chosen state.
Copies, clones and delayed frames retain separate bindings and combat state.
Waiting source queries keep explicit reads in player, blocker and collection
operands without making choices or altering combat. Existing target, payment,
zone, replacement and damage services supply their established behavior. No new
payment or damage replacement order is introduced. No Go fallback, partial
production registry, Go-card deletion or DSL API removal occurs. Removal gates
remain unmet.

### Contract, exact signatures and reuse boundary

RON now accepts the sole target group
`NumberTargetGroupPermanents(Integer(2), filter, ControlledByTheSamePlayer)`
when the supported conjunctive filter requires opponent control. In this
explicitly two-player engine, both opponents are the same player. Other counts,
unknown group restrictions and unrestricted same-controller groups reject.
One fresh `mage.DeclarePermanentTargets(name, 2, 2, filter, options...)` declaration
retains target legality, distinctness, phasing, returned visits and copy frames.
The typed `pairedTargets *permanentTargetsPlan` scope must match the current
collection binding. No global choice slot or mutable per-factory state is used.

`TrySwappingBlockAssignmentsOfTwoBlockingCreatures(Ref_TargetPermanents_0,
Ref_TargetPermanents_1)` accepts these two distinct members, in either order,
in an ordinary resolving body. It lowers the symmetric pair operation to
`mage.TrySwapBlockingAssignments(subjects PermanentSet) ResolvingEffect`.
Fewer than two legal members supplies no swap. Unbound, duplicate, malformed
and incompatible operands, entry bodies and draw replacement bodies reject.
Spell, activation and trigger scopes have definition-validation evidence.

The engine checks exactly two present blocking creature visits with the same
controller. It reads their current attacking sets, checks both incoming sets,
then removes both blockers and commits the complete swapped batch. Checks use
shared `CanBlock`, `HasLandwalkEvasion`, `blockCapacity`, live attacker identity
and continuous restriction services. Tapping, evasion, protection, blocking
restrictions, minimum blockers and additional/unlimited capacity apply. A band
uses one slot and one legal member supplies its block under CR 702.22h.
Costs, requirements and declaration-only limits are not repeated. Empty sets
pass, including after all their attackers leave combat. Failed checks leave
both assignments unchanged; no removal is allowed before both checks pass.

The existing `addEffectBlockers` service installs all assignments and history
before events. Blockers become blockers again, even for a shared old attacker.
New block/pair/group events fire; attackers remain blocked, so becomes-blocked
events do not fire again. Existing pending triggers and declaration-only history
remain. Combat damage reads the swapped assignments. No LKI object becomes a
blocker. Source departure cannot cancel a pending activation. Copies, separate
factories, repeated activations and clones keep independent target frames.
Waiting delayed-source queries retain explicit source reads without executing.

The complete card's tap trigger uses one singular player in `MultipleRecipients`.
`mage.OnePlayer(player PlayerRef) PlayerSet` supplies the typed singleton to
`mage.DamageRecipients` and the existing damage batch. The permanent side reuses
`compileContextualCollection` when no damage-history predicate is present.
Both sides remain simultaneous and retain normal prevention and source/controller
snapshots. Missing/unbound singleton players supply an empty set; invalid
bindings fail definition validation. Source-query inspection follows the typed
player. No payment, zone, replacement-order or declaration service is replaced.

### Contract, signatures and engine boundary

RON lowers exactly
`CreateFutureTrigger_UnlessPlayerPaysManaBefore(AtTheBeginningOfPlayersNextDrawStep(player),
ActionList(nonemptyActions), player, fixedManaList)` in ordinary resolving
bodies. Deadline and payer must use the same declaration. X mana, malformed
arity, empty/wrong bodies, unknown events, unbound players, entry contexts and
draw-replacement contexts reject during compilation. Inventory labels the
nested deadline event, player reference, action body and mana cost separately.

The reusable engine API is
`UnlessManaPaidBeforeNextDraw(player PlayerRef, mana core.ManaCost,
unpaid ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`. It reads the payer once and creates
one permission plus one delayed ability with a shared per-instance ID. Fixed
nonnegative ordinary mana and valid typed operands are checked by definition
validation. Existing `GetPlayerPayments`, `TakePlayerPayment` and
`PriorityTakePlayerPayment` expose and pay the permission. The shared cost
transaction owns affordability, mana activation and rollback. A successful
special action cancels only its corresponding delay and cannot repeat.

The payer's next actual draw-step event expires payment before priority and
uses the shared delayed-trigger queue, stack placement, saved controller,
source incarnation and typed resolution bindings for the unpaid body. Cleanup
retains these permissions while retaining expiry for existing turn permissions.
Skipped draw steps emit no deadline event. Installation after an event waits
for the next occurrence. Source departure, return, control changes and phasing
cannot cancel an installed obligation. Clones copy permission storage and
shared delayed capture supplies independent frames. Existing source-reference
inspection retains explicit waiting source reads without executing effects.

RON owns syntax, lexical player scope and diagnostics. The engine owns state,
payment and timing. No card-name branch, fallback registry, parallel payment,
damage or delayed-trigger subsystem was added. Existing repeatable player
payments keep their behavior. API and rules documentation describe only this
new contract. No Go card or DSL service was removed; cutover gates remain unmet.

Ordinary instant and sorcery bodies now accept exactly two target groups:
`TargetPlayer(existingSupportedFilter)` followed by
`AnyNumberOfTargetGraveyardCards(And([IsCardtype(type),
InAPlayersGraveyard(SinglePlayer(Ref_TargetPlayer)))]))`.
The two filter operands can appear in either order. There must be exactly one
card type and one reference to the earlier player. The associated resolving
action is `ReturnGraveyardCardsToTopOfLibraryInAnyOrder(Ref_TargetGraveyardCards)`.
Zero cards is legal. Malformed declarations, external/wrong references, repeated
filters, nested targets and unsupported contexts reject before publication.
Activation, permanent, entry, static, draw-replacement and delayed contexts reject.

RON owns spelling, lexical scope and lowering. Its new collection plan joins the
existing per-factory instance binding maps. It builds the player declaration
before the dependent card declaration. Inventory labels the target's card filter
and the action's card-collection reference separately; compilation evidence
remains distinct from behavior evidence.

- `DeclareGraveyardCardTargets(name string, player *PlayerTargetBinding,
  filters ...CardFilter) *GraveyardCardTargetsBinding`
- `ReturnGraveyardCardsToLibraryTop(cards CardSet, chooser PlayerRef)
  ResolvingEffect`

The supported dependency list is one singular player target followed by its
optional card collection. Definition validation rejects missing, external and
forward dependencies. Existing target query frames, announcement validation,
stack target visits, partial resolution, copy group counts and cloning retain
ownership of target choices and identity. Zero cards does not prevent choosing a
player with an empty graveyard. The collection has no arbitrary 100-card limit.
Copies can change the player and the cards while retaining the original count.

The return action saves all exact visits before any replacement. It uses the
existing `CardZoneMoveAction` replacement pipeline in APNAP order, then the
existing `LibraryTopOrderChooser` or `ChooseScryPlacement` choice service.
The explicit chooser is the spell controller for the RON action. Invalid orders
retain collection order. Shared movement now supports library-top placement and
can defer its events. Existing immediate-move callers keep their event timing.
All moves finish before zone events and aggregate graveyard departure events.
Rechecks after replacements and ordering exclude returned visits. Owner zones
apply. The engine accepts typed card sets and a typed chooser; it has no RON
spelling or card-name policy. No separate replacement, target, clone or zone
subsystem was added.

### Supported shape, mechanics and reuse boundary

- `CouldntAttackThisTurn` is a strict bare symbol handled by
  `compileContextualCollection(Node, scope) (permanentSetFactory, error)`.
  It is available in ordinary resolving permanent collections, including
  nonempty nested `And`, `Or`, `ExceptFor` and delayed resolving bodies.
  Tuples, arguments, generic target filters, entry and draw replacements reject.
- Lowering uses `mage.MatchingPermanents(mage.CouldntAttackThisTurn)`.
  `CouldntAttackThisTurn mage.PermanentFilter` is a pure exact-visit read.
  Normal collection services still exclude absent and phased recipients.
  This form has no new binding or source reference to share between factories.
- `(*Game).recordAttackOpportunities(player uuid.UUID)` observes the battlefield
  after layers apply in both `doDeclareAttackers` and `ExecuteAttackers`.
  Only the declaring player's creatures qualify. Existing attack legality
  supplies tapping, sickness, haste, attack permissions, defender, matching
  restrictions, player protection and Sanctuary. Optional attack costs do not
  force payment. A successful paid declared attack also disproves inability.
- `(*Game).attackRequirementWeight(*Permanent) int` extracts the unchanged
  requirement weight calculation from the existing capped attack service.
  A limit's last-slot weight determines all legal alternative participants;
  tied alternatives qualify, while an optional creature cannot displace a
  required one. This is the existing two-player combat model.
- `TurnTrackers.attackOpportunities map[capturedPermanent]bool` retains all
  eligible visits across extra combats. Skipped declarations add none. Later
  haste, untapping, animation or control changes cannot add earlier facts.
  Observation does not depend on Season being present. Control and phasing
  keep history; return does not. Tracker cloning and final cleanup handle the
  map with the existing turn lifecycle. Payment trials inherit separate maps.
- Semantic inventory preserves the collection role through `ExceptFor` and
  classifies the new symbol as a permanent collection rather than advertising
  generic filter support. Collection support remains distinct from gameplay.

### Signatures, contexts and engine contract

New native API:

owner, controller *PlayerBinding, card *CardBinding, body ResolvingEffect)

separate frames. Cleanup after detection does not remove a pending body.

RON keeps its existing spelling:
`CreateTriggerUntil(WhenAPermanentDies(SinglePermanent(ref)), ActionList(actions),
UntilEndOfTurn)`. In that body, singular `Exile([Permanent(ref)], [])` uses the
death card when `ref` is the watched declaration. The event spelling
`Permanent(Trigger_ThatPermanent)` uses the same saved card. Other references
keep battlefield semantics. `CardInGraveyards(Trigger_ThatGraveyardCard)` supplies
an explicit typed card operand in that lexical body. Spell, activation, trigger
and supported nested resolving bodies retain their normal scope rules. Static,
entry replacement and draw replacement declarations reject. A source entry
trigger is a resolving trigger, not an entry replacement. Leaves-only events do
not produce a death card; siblings cannot read the delayed body's local binding.
Grouped dead-object exile, modifiers and malformed references reject.

`ExileGraveyardCard` now uses the existing `CardZoneMoveAction` replacement and
movement services. The owner chooses competing replacements; movement rechecks
the saved visit after choices. Canceled movement sends no departure event.
Zone events observe the actual destination after movement. Tokens supply no
retained graveyard card. Later graveyard or battlefield visits cannot replace
the saved visit. Ownership, exile source, LKI, phasing and clone services are reused.

`EachPermanentRuleEffect(staticPermanentFilter,
[CantAttackAPlayer(ExceptFor(test))])` on a static permanent. `test` is
`CastASpellDuringTheirLastTurn(AnySpell)`,
`PutAPermanentOnBattleDuringTheirLastTurn(IsNonToken)`, or a nonempty recursive
`Or([...])` of those tests. The player is the two-player combat defending
player. Other cast/entry filters, malformed symbol/tuple shapes, unresolved
references and spell contexts reject at compilation. Inventory child roles
identify the player activity, spell filter and permanent filter separately.

`TurnTrackers` archives only the active player's completed actions at final
cleanup. Cleanup priority keeps the prior archive. Empty/extra turns replace

### Contract, signatures and reuse

Engine API: `ThisCardDiscardedByOpponentEffect(cause *PlayerBinding) EventPattern`.
Use `WhenEvent`, a fresh `BindPlayer`, and `FromPlayer` for the body. Definition
validation rejects a nil binding or a read outside its event scope.

RON supports exactly this wrapper and event operand shape:

```ron
FromAnyZone(TriggerA(
  WhenASpellOrAbilityCausesAPlayerToDiscardACard(
    ControlledByAPlayer(Opponent),
    SinglePlayer(You),
    SingleCardInHand(ThisCardInHand)),
  ActionList([PlayerAction(
    Trigger_ControllerOfThatSpellOrAbility, LoseLife(Integer(5)))])))
```

The ordinary action-list compiler lowers the body with a new lexical typed
player binding. The wrapper rejects other event kinds, operands, arities,
intervening conditions and target declarations. The body supplies no permanent
or source-spell binding. Self damage, resolving spell copies and continued spell
damage reject in this event context. Sibling rules cannot read the event player.
Inventory roles retain the wrapper, event, cause filter, hand subject and player
reference. Every factory builds independent bindings.

Single and batch discard services capture the hand visit, effect-versus-cost
status, cause identity and controller before replacements. Resolving objects
supply their saved stack ID and controller; a source that has left, returned,
changed control or phased cannot replace them. Direct effect callers with a
present unphased permanent source retain their existing controller-based use.
Missing causes cannot match. Replacement proposals keep the original facts and
selected visit. An unspecified proposal now saves its hand visit before
replacements. Cancellation and returned visits produce no completed discard.

Public graveyard and face-up exile source discovery reuses
`detectCardZoneTriggers`; no all-zone polling service or parallel event system
was added. The shared mover now respects an exile discard destination. A hidden
library destination supplies no self-card ability. All batch moves finish before
discard events. Shared pending-trigger/APNAP, event capture, stack copy, clone,
replacement ordering and payment-transaction services remain in use. No mutable
last-action slot or card-name branch was added. LKI does not replace saved cause
facts. Card source departure after detection cannot cancel the pending trigger.

trigger placement and discard boundaries. No RON source defect was corrected.

### Contract and implementation

New API: `mage.PhaseOutUntilSourceLeaves(subject PermanentRef,
tapOnReturn bool) ResolvingEffect`. RON accepts precisely
`PhaseOutPermanentUntilWithEffects(subject,
UntilPermanentLeavesBattlefield(ThisPermanent), TapAsPhasesIn)` in resolving
battlefield-source bodies, including entry triggers. Typed permanent references
retain their factory-specific declarations. Unbound/wrong references, malformed
arities, other durations, other phase-in operations and payment contexts reject
at declaration time. Inventory roles distinguish the subject, duration and
phase-in operation. RON spelling and scope checks remain in `ron`.

Engine waits live in ZoneSystem, with exact source and subject visits, the
subject's phase epoch and the optional return status. ZoneSystem.Clone copies
the waits; permanent copy-on-write cloning now also preserves the phase epoch.
The native external-cycle test exposed the missing epoch copy: an old wait could
otherwise release a later phase cycle after a clone caused copy-on-write.

Source departure before resolution prevents the initial phase-out. A phased
source remains the same battlefield visit and can start or retain the wait.
Control changes, ability removal and cleanup do not end it. A returned source
cannot replace the saved visit. Normal untap phase-in skips held subjects.
External phase-in cancels the return; a later phase cycle or returned subject
cannot inherit the old wait. This is a one-shot return, without a delayed trigger
or priority pass. Replaced destruction with regeneration retains the source and
the wait. Actual exile, bounce and other shared battlefield departures end it.

Shared PhaseOut/PhaseIn now track indirect parent visits recursively for Auras,
Equipment and Fortifications. Opponent-controlled and nested attachments follow
the same group. Directly phased attachments cannot join an unrelated group.
Indirect attachments cannot phase in alone. Counters, attachment relationships,
choices, identity and untapped attachment status remain in place. Only the
subject's phase-in status changes when tapOnReturn is true; no tap, entry,
zone-change or attachment event is emitted by phasing.

All simultaneous source moves finish before the return group becomes present.
Shared withZoneChangeBatch flushes waits before its continuous-effect pass and
leave-event dispatch. Single removals flush at the shared removal boundary.
Shared replacements, target legality, pending-trigger placement, stack copies,
LKI services and copy-on-write state remain in use. No new parallel event system,
card-name branch, mutable last-action slot, game-time declaration panic or
production partial registry was added. LKI cannot replace a saved source visit.

### Supported contracts and engine reuse

RON accepts `EachPermanentRuleEffect(filter, operations)` inside the existing
static `If`, `Unless` and `IfElse` bodies. It uses `compileStaticPermanentFilter`
and the existing static condition grammar. The nonempty operation list accepts
`CantBeEnchantedAndDoesntRemove(IsEnchantmentType(Aura))` and the bare symbol
`CantBeGainedControlOf`, individually or together, once each. Other subtype
predicates, unknown/mixed operations, duplicates, malformed arities and unbound
references reject at compilation. Unconditional and resolving declarations
remain outside this adapter. Conditional layer rules can share the body.

New reusable APIs:

- `PreventNewAuraAttachmentsIf(subjects PermanentSet, condition StateCondition) StaticRule`
- `PreventControlGainsIf(subjects PermanentSet, condition StateCondition) StaticRule`

Both validate the typed subject set and condition. They read each source visit,
its current controller and the current subject set. Printed-ability suppression,
source departure and source phasing disable them. Source return supplies its own
new effect instances. Queries do not use LKI to replace an absent source.

The Aura rule uses the shared attachment/target/entry/state-action query. An Aura
already on the exact current subject visit remains legal under this rule. Other
attachment restrictions still apply. A former Aura cannot attach again while
protection holds. Returned visits do not inherit an exception. Re-enabling the
condition permits Auras already attached at that time. No allowlist is saved.

Control uses the shared Layer 2 service, exchanges and later-layer evaluation.
It tests proposed gains against the subject's prior controller after completed
layers establish types and abilities. Rejected gains cause a new layer pass with
the permitted controller held through Layer 2, so the later indestructible layer
uses correct membership. Holds are local to that evaluation. Established control
remains; later condition changes can permit a pending continuous control effect.
An ended control effect can restore default or underlying control. Effect
identities and per-visit application provenance distinguish ending an effect
from a new gain. Ordinary control effects, attached control and composed control
modifications record that provenance. Clones retain effect identity and copy
per-visit state. Phased objects retain their visit and do not enter present-object
mutation paths. Exchanges reject before either half changes if one is protected.

This reuses static declarations, typed sets/conditions, printed-ability wrappers,
copy-on-write permanents, control dependency reconciliation, continuous layers,
attachment legality, spell targeting and destruction/sacrifice services. No new
card-name branches, production partial registry, action-result global, runtime
declaration panic or alternative rules pipeline was added.

110.2, 303.4a–j, 611.2a, 611.3 and 613.11 establish the rule boundary and the

### Supported signatures, timing and boundaries

- `XIs(Twice(ManaValueOfSpell(Ref_TargetSpell)))` with one `TargetSpell` and
  `PayManaX([ManaCostX], ValueX)` on an ordinary nonmodal activation. The target
  and resolving body cannot read this defined `ValueX`. Missing, wrong-type,
  duplicate, cyclic and unbound declarations reject before game execution.
- `If(SpellPassesFilter(spellRef, TargetsPlayer(playerRef)), [actions])` and
  `ChangeTheTargetsOfSpellToAPlayer(spellRef, AnyPlayer)` in ordinary resolving
  activation bodies. Entry, draw replacement, delayed and spell-body contexts
  remain rejected by these adapters. Spelling and scope remain in `ron`.
- `WithActivationManaXFromSpell(*SpellTargetBinding, int) ActionOption` requires
  a positive multiplier, the sole X-independent spell target and an X cost.
  Queries enumerate legal candidates without choices or ambient-X changes.
  Announcement uses the submitted exact stack ID and includes the spell's X
  in mana value. Shared payment locks the cost and supplies rollback. Pending
  abilities and copies retain payment X through source changes.
- `IfSpellTargetsPlayer(StackObjectRef, PlayerRef, ResolvingEffect)
  ResolvingEffect` checks a present spell's current targets without departure
  LKI. `ChangeSingleSpellTargetToPlayer(StackObjectRef) ResolvingEffect` checks
  the spell's own controller, target declarations, X and source restrictions.
  It requires one target occurrence and another legal player. Missing spells,
  abilities, no legal player, cancellation and invalid choices change nothing.
  Success keeps controller, mode and X, moves retained allocations by target
  position, updates modal targets and uses shared target events. Copies and
  clones keep separate lists and maps.

CR 115.7a–b, 115.7e–f, 115.8–9, 202.3e and 601.2b–f/602.2b establish these
contracts. Definition inspection declares the target before reading it for X.

### Supported shapes, boundaries and rules

Before editing, the stated acceptance contract required resolution-time
sacrifice; saved mana value before departure; optional failure to find; no
payment offer for cheaper/equal finds; exact positive difference payment;
owner's graveyard for an unpaid find; and movement before one shuffle. Tests
also cover invalid declarations, unavailable/phased offerings, failed casting,
countering, lost offerings, library return visits, replacements, entry failure,
mana sources, spell copies and pending clones.

New native signatures:

- `IfSacrificeWithManaValue(PlayerRef, PermanentFilter, *NumberBinding,
  ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` selects one required matching sacrifice
  through the shared payment transaction. Its source can pay. The transaction
  saves the selected visit's mana value before departure. Only the paid body
  receives that result; nested executions restore prior values. The definition
  graph has a private result producer and rejects unbound and missing operands.
- `SearchLibraryWithManaDifference(PlayerRef, CardFilter, ResolutionValue)
  ResolvingEffect` snapshots allowance once, clamped to zero. It can find no
  matching card. It saves exact library visits before selection, fixes a positive
  difference before shared optional mana payment and checks the selected visit
  again after payment and entry choices. Paid entry uses shared entry
  replacements; failed entry preserves its destination. Unpaid movement uses
  `CardZoneMoveAction` and the normal replacement service. Entry/movement
  precedes a shuffle even when no card is found. No extra reveal is added.

RON accepts `MustCost(SacrificeAPermanent(filter))` with an adjacent
`If(CostWasPaid, actions)` that reads `ManaValueOfTheSacrificedPermanent` in
ordinary resolving bodies. Per-factory bindings remain separate from activation
and additional-cost sacrifice bindings. The supported `SearchLibrary` body has
three steps: artifact `FindACardOfType`, the conditional continuation and
`Shuffle`. `ACardOfTypeWasFoundThisWay(ManaValueIs(LessThanOrEqualTo(
ManaValueOfTheSacrificedPermanent)))` selects normal entry. The greater-value
branch offers `MayCost(PayManaX([ManaCostX], Minus(ManaValueOfTheFoundCard,
ManaValueOfTheSacrificedPermanent)))`, followed by an adjacent
`IfElse(CostWasPaid, [normal entry], [PutFoundCardsIntoGraveyard])`.
Every nested constructor, symbol, arity and operation list is validated. Other
entry operations, wrong predicates/payments/destinations and unbound values
remain errors. Entry and draw-replacement contexts remain rejected.

RON owns syntax, shape validation, lexical dominance and instance bindings.
The engine owns sacrifice selection, saved results, mana payment, zone visits,
replacement proposals and entry. There are no card-name dispatches, Go-card
fallbacks or partial production registries. The declaration/result scopes add
no global last-action slot. The existing sacrifice and mana transaction
contracts retain replacement ordering, visit checks and rollback.

CR 118.11–12, 400.7, 608.2g–h, 701.21 and 701.23–24 establish this contract.
The first synthetic omitted-sacrifice replacement assertion expected no
continuation. CR 118.11–12 instead requires the continuation when mandatory
payment has started, regardless of the replaced event. The corrected test
asserts that the artifact stays while the saved-value search still resolves.
This does not change the shared payment service. Simultaneous multiple moves
are not introduced by this single-card search or sacrifice shape.

### Exact supported declaration and engine contract

The complete supported context is a source permanent's entry rule:

```ron
AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent, [
  MustCost(Exile([NumberCardsInGraveyards(ValueX,
    And([cardFilter, InAPlayersGraveyard(SinglePlayer(You))]))], [])),
  IfElse(CostWasPaid,
    [EntersWithNumberCombinationCountersOfChoice(
      NumberOfCardsOfTypeExiledThisWay(cardFilter), [counterTypes...])],
    [PutIntoGraveyardInstead])
])
```

The same supported card filter must supply payment and count. Counter choices
must be nonempty, valid and distinct. Other players, amounts, branch shapes,
modifications, result contexts and entry instructions reject at compilation.
The result stays inside this entry declaration; there is no ambient last-action
slot, escape into another ability, retained game binding or game-time panic.

New API:
`ExileGraveyardAsEntersWithCounterChoice(amount EntryCounterValue,
filter CardFilter, counters ...core.CounterType) Ability`.
It reuses `AnnouncedXForEnteringPermanent`,
`ExileMatchingCardsFromSingleGraveyardCost` selection and validation,
`OnePlayer(You)`, `CardZoneMoveAction`, `performCardZoneMoveEvents`,
`withZoneChangeBatch`, the entry replacement candidate lifecycle and shared
entry counter replacement processing. Definition validation checks permanent
context, amount/filter/choices and duplicate payment declarations.

The full amount is selected and all exact graveyard visits are rechecked before
any payment move. Insufficient resources or changed visits prevent entry without
partial payment. Invalid chooser answers fall back to legal candidates; a player
cannot decline mandatory entry payment. Existing cost callers keep their
choice-error behavior.
Once valid payment starts, changed or omitted moves do not unpay it; only actual
exile moves count. All moves finish before zone observations, followed by one
graveyard-leave event for the batch. Each exiled card supplies one counter choice.
Counter totals combine by kind before shared counter replacements and entry
observations. Copy priority supplies acquired rules before payment. Noncast
entry uses X=0. Return, spell copies and game clones have separate results.
Phasing keeps counters and introduces no new entry payment.

Failed permanent spell entry now proposes owner-graveyard movement through the
shared card-zone replacement service. The service recognizes the exact resolving
stack visit, marks completed departures and sends the actual zone event.
Existing stack exile rules still apply. Failed spell copies do not become
battlefield tokens. No change to the general casting-payment transaction is
needed: this is a single mandatory entry payment with complete prevalidation.

Rules evidence: CR 107.3m, 118.3, 118.11, 122.1a, 122.2, 122.6, 400.7,
614.1c, 614.5 and 616.1. The sole local Monster ruling is from WotC and permits
X above the available graveyard count. There are no Scryfall notes.
`go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card "Frankenstein's Monster"` passes.

### Contract, boundaries and source evidence

Engine signatures:

- `SnapshotPermanentSet(subjects PermanentSet, result *PermanentSetBinding) ResolvingEffect`.
- `ChangeEachController(subjects PermanentSet, controller PlayerRef) ContinuousModification`.

The producer saves each present, unphased exact battlefield visit once.
Empty membership clears a prior result. `FromPermanentSet` reads survivors
without repeating the producer's filter. Phasing preserves visits; return does
not. Existing resolution-frame clone and delayed-capture services retain
independent results. There is no global last-action result.

Plural control uses `Until(Indefinite, ChangeEachController(...))` through the
existing layer modification service. It captures every subject before applying
control. It retains timestamps, control restrictions, combat reconciliation,
summoning sickness, source independence and later-layer behavior. The same
shared service preserves installed control through subject phasing and ignores
returned visits. No new control subsystem or card-name dispatch was added.

RON supports `CreatePermanentsList(collection)` in ordinary resolving action
lists and the lexical symbol `ThePermanentsList` in subsequent collection
consumers. A nested producer has a separate typed binding. Payment branches and
modes cannot export their declarations. `GainControlOfEachPermanent(collection)`
uses the action player, including `PlayerAction(TheChosenPlayer, ...)`.
Named collections use the existing `IsNamed(NamedCard(nonemptyString))` filter.
Entry/replacement contexts, unbound reads and malformed shapes still reject.
The compiler owns spelling, declaration checks and lexical scope; the engine
owns snapshots, decisions, tap batches, payments and control layers.

Source defect corrected: the sole Rohgahh LEG record used `If(CostWasPaid, ...)`
for losing control. `data/LEG.json` Oracle text says “If you don't”; both local
WotC rulings dated 2009-10-01 confirm all named creatures across controllers
are tapped, already tapped creatures are also transferred, and the opponent is
chosen during resolution without targeting. The source now uses
`If(CostWasntPaid, ...)`. There is one record, so no reprint remains inconsistent.
There are no Scryfall notes for Rohgahh. The complete Kobolds of Kher Keep record
and its WotC color-indicator ruling were also read for the gameplay fixture.
`go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card "Rohgahh of Kher Keep"` and the same command
for `"Kobolds of Kher Keep"` pass. Rules: CR 400.7, 608.2c–h, 611.2a/c,
613.1b and 702.26b/d. Sylvan Library's separate source defect remains deferred.

### Supported signatures, reuse and boundaries

- `StaticAbilityPayment(PermanentRef, StaticRule, core.Duration)` extends
  `ResolutionActionPayment`. Shared `PayActionOrElse` prepares the exact visit,
  offers a choice, rechecks availability and selects one local branch.
- `AcquireStaticAbilityUntil(PermanentRef, StaticRule, core.Duration)` extends
  the acquired static service. It accepts EndOfCombat, EndOfTurn or Indefinite.
  The old `AcquireStaticAbility` caller remains indefinite. The grant and its
  registered rule effects expire together. CantAttack rules are supported
  acquired statics. Recipient context, layer timestamps, later ability removal,
  phasing, independent ability identities and clone state use existing services.
- `AttacksWithoutTappingUntil(PlayerRef, PermanentFilter, StateCondition,
  core.Duration)` saves the player and source visit until EndOfCombat or
  EndOfTurn. Both attack paths query the live filter and condition. The game
  rule can affect later creatures and survives ability removal; it does not
  grant vigilance or bypass attack legality and costs. Source control changes
  retain the saved player. Departure/return cannot replace the source; phasing
  suspends the condition and phase-in can restore it.
- RON supports the exact single `AddAbility([PermanentRuleEffect(ThisPermanent,
  [CantAttack])])` modification in `CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil` for
  ThisPermanent and UntilEndOfCombat, as an ordinary action or a MayCost /
  PlayerMayCost payment. Payment continuations reuse If, Unless and IfElse.
- RON supports `CreatePlayerEffectUntil(playerRef,
  [AttackingDoesntCauseCreaturesToTapIf(permanentFilter,
  PermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent,IsUntapped))],UntilEndOfCombat)`.
  Multiple such operations can share the list. Ordinary battlefield-source
  resolving bodies support these shapes. Entry/draw replacement contexts,
  other source conditions, subjects and durations reject at declaration.
- `ron` owns shape validation, references and lowering. `mage` owns the rule,
  exact source capture, acquired ability lifecycle and optional payment.
  Waiting delayed source discovery includes the static payment's source read.
  No Go-card fallback, production subset registry or card-name dispatch exists.

### Contract, contexts and reuse boundary

- `mage.MayDrawCardsThen(player PlayerRef, count int, body ResolvingEffect)
  ResolvingEffect` asks once, runs each draw through existing replacement
  services and runs the body on acceptance even if no actual draw occurs.
- `mage.PayLifeOrReturnDrawnCards(player PlayerRef, count, life int)
  ResolvingEffect` chooses all required eligible hand visits before a life
  decision. Fewer available cards means choosing all available cards. For each
  choice, the shared transactional LifePayCost payment or CardZoneMoveAction
  library return applies. The choice order supplies the per-card order and
  therefore the resulting library order. Exact life can be paid. Prohibited or
  unaffordable life payments cannot be chosen. There is no discard or reveal.
- TurnTrackers records `(player, physical card, exact hand visit)` from completed
  EvtCardDrawn events. It retains earlier draws this turn, rejects added and
  returned visits, includes actual replacement-generated draws, clears on final
  cleanup and clones its map independently. Failed/replaced draws add no visit.
- RON accepts `MayCost(DrawNumberCards(Integer(n)))` with the immediately adjacent
  `If(CostWasPaid, actions)` in ordinary resolving action lists. Its payer is You,
  consistent with existing MayCost. Only fixed nonnegative n is supported.
  Other payment kinds/conditions, IfElse and draw replacement contexts reject.
  The payment result does not escape the continuation.
- RON accepts `PayLifeOrPutCardsDrawnThisTurnOnTopOfLibrary(Integer(count),
  Integer(life))` in ordinary resolving player actions and typed single-player
  scopes. Both arguments are fixed nonnegative integers. Malformed declarations,
  dynamic values, unbound references, costs, static/entry declarations and draw
  replacement bodies reject. The inventory walks all three Integer operands as
  values, including the resolution draw cost.
- RON owns spelling, shape checks and lowering. Mage owns draw history, exact
  visits, decisions, payments and moves. Shared draw/zone replacements, life
  costs, trigger timing, source LKI, clone services and definition validation
  remain in use. No card-name dispatch, fallback or production subset registry
  is added. Existing production callers and Go definitions remain.

cards, then DiscardNumberCardsDrawnThisTurn. Oracle in `data/LEG.json` requires
choosing two cards drawn this turn, then paying life or putting each on the
library. Local WotC rulings require earlier draws to be eligible, accepted
replaced draws to retain the continuation, and no actions between drawing and
choosing. Replace that pair with the explicit choose-before-payment action.

its occurrence delta is exactly the removed pair/payment/result symbol and the

### Signatures, contexts and engine reuse

- `ChooseSpellCastThisTurn(player, caster PlayerRef, filter DamageSourceFilter,
  binding *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect`: saves a required non-targeted
  historical choice. The central successful cast path saves immutable source
  facts and caster before cast events. Unresolved and countered casts qualify.
  Failed casting and uncast copies do not. The existing damage-source chooser
  supplies defensive copies, exact identities and required-choice fallback.
- `DamageDealtThisTurnBySource(source DamageSourceRef) ResolutionValue`: reads
  actual damage from the exact spell stack identity. Nonspell or missing results
  supply zero. Shared damage execution records final positive amounts across
  player and permanent recipients after replacements, prevention and redirection.
  Simultaneous packets update totals before notifications. No life-loss substitute
  or separate damage pipeline is introduced.
- Cast entries live in TurnTrackers; totals live in DamageSystem. Cleanup clears
  both; clones copy them. Results use the existing per-resolution damage-source
  binding maps, including copied and saved frames. Historical cast entries do
  not expand general CR 609.7 legal damage-source categories.
- RON accepts `ChooseASpellCastThisTurn(And([IsCardtype(Sorcery),
  CastByPlayer(playerRef)]))` in ordinary resolving action lists. The clauses can
  occur in either order and must each occur once. Its lexical continuation can
  read `DamageDealtBySpellThisTurn(TheSpellCastChosenThisWay)` as a resolution
  value, including existing HalfRoundedDown arithmetic. Each factory creates a
  fresh binding. Unbound, malformed, duplicate, incompatible and branch-escaped
  forms reject. Entry/replacement contexts and other cast filters remain errors.
- Existing player choice, explicit player references, player cast counters,
  rounding, resolving spell damage, paid casting and definition validation remain
  the dependency boundary. No broad DSL export or Go definition is removed.

### Contract, supported shape and dependencies

Native API: `ReturnToHandInsteadOfDyingWithPlayLock() Ability`.
Visibility query: `(*Game).IsHandCardRevealed(player, card uuid.UUID) bool`.

RON supports the complete battlefield rule:

```ron
ReplaceWouldPutIntoGraveyard(
  APermanentWouldDie(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent)),
  [PutItInOwnersHandInstead,
   CreatePlayerEffectUntil(OwnerOfTheCardReturnedToHandThisWay,
     [PlaysWithCardInHandRevealed(TheCardReturnedToHandThisWay),
      CantPlayCardInHand(TheCardReturnedToHandThisWay)],
     UntilPlayersNextTurn(OwnerOfTheCardReturnedToHandThisWay))])
```

The two hand restrictions may occur in either order, exactly once each. Other
subjects, event forms, continuations, result references, durations and nonbattlefield
contexts reject before execution. Compiler spelling and result scope stay in ron;
reusable movement, replacement, identity, visibility and play rules stay in mage.

Current source incarnation and runtime ability identity supply the replacement.
Shared affected-controller choices and replacement rechecks run before movement.
A hand destination is proposed rather than moved during replacement selection.
The same declaration cannot repeat if another replacement changes it again.
Destruction, sacrifice and direct graveyard moves share the service. Simultaneous
batches complete all choices before any departure. Phasing suspends applicability;
a phase cycle preserves it. Ability removal stops the source's static rule.

Only an actual nontoken hand return installs the retained rule. It captures owner,
card ID, exact new hand visit and installation turn. Returned and cloned objects
cannot share mutable results. A later hand visit cannot inherit restrictions.
Sacrifice remains a paid sacrifice and sends its event, but a hand return creates
no death or graveyard visit. Failed payment and replaced hand destinations create
no lock. Direct battlefield entry remains possible. Shared next-turn expiry
handles extra turns, skipped whole turns and skipped untap. Per-card snapshots
and hand damage-source information expose the returned card without exposing the
rest of the hand; public departure facts survive in clones.

### Contract, signatures and boundaries

Engine: `SpendAnyManaForOneSpellThisTurn(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`.
Each resolution saves one player and fresh permission ID through cleanup. Source
departure, phasing, ability removal and control changes do not affect it. Clones
copy the permission slice. No shared last-action slot or source-name branch exists.

RON accepts ordinary resolving `CreatePlayerEffectUntil(player,
[MayActionOnce(CastASpellAndMaySpendManaAsThoughAnyTypeToPayManaCost(AnySpell))],
UntilEndOfTurn)`, with existing typed player refs. Spell, activation and triggered
resolving bodies reuse the ordinary compiler path. Entry/draw-replacement contexts,
escaped operations, other filters, unknown operations and malformed arities reject.
Factories keep their existing per-instance bindings. Syntax stays in ron.

Casting chooses an available permission through ChooseMayAbility, then saves its
ID in the transaction. Shared total-cost preparation applies taxes/reductions
before changing the printed-cost payment demand. Added colored/hybrid costs and
taxes retain their requirements. Generic reductions cannot remove printed colored
symbols. Printed X can use the permission; generic reductions remove additional
restricted X before printed X that can use the permission. Actual mana types, restrictions and announced X remain.
Alternative costs and ability costs cannot use this printed-cost permission.
Commit checks the saved permission before resource changes and consumes it only
after total payment succeeds. Copies do not pay again. Cleanup clears unused IDs.

`Game.CanPaySpellManaCost(player uuid.UUID, card Card, x int) bool` reads the
printed cost and available permissions without choices or mutation. It does not
claim to include added costs or cost modifiers. GetCastableSpells uses X=0 and
retains its existing added-cost limits; Game.CanAfford keeps its supplied-cost API.
No runtime cutover, Go definitions or DSL functions are removed before their gates.

events, clone/copy isolation, delayed reads, source departure/phasing, repeated
producers, invalid declarations and strict atomic loading.

### Signatures, contexts and dependencies

RON supports `EachPlayerMayCost(AnyPlayer, AnteTopCardOfLibrary)` in ordinary
resolving action sequences. It produces the local collection `PaidCost`.
`EachPlayerAction(PaidCost, SetLifeTotal(Integer(total)))` reads the most recent
preceding producer. Integer totals may be negative. Branch results cannot
escape; malformed arities, tuple symbols, unbound reads, other filters/costs,
other paid-player actions, and entry/static/cost/draw-replacement contexts reject.
Spell, activated, trigger and delayed resolving sequences share this adapter.

Engine APIs:

- `BindPlayerSet(name string) *PlayerSetBinding`
- `FromPlayerSet(binding *PlayerSetBinding) PlayerSet`
- `MayAnteTopEach(players PlayerSet, paid *PlayerSetBinding) ResolvingEffect`
- `SetLifeTotalEach(players PlayerSet, total ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect`

PlayerSetBinding uses existing PlayerNumbersBinding seats and shared number
frames. No new Game field or global last-payment state exists. The producer
clears old membership each invocation; factories receive fresh declarations.
Shared frames retain results for copies, clones and delayed continuations.
The saved set does not depend on the source's continued presence or abilities.

Reuse locked AnteTopCost legality checks and Game.AnteLibraryTops. All optional
choices precede rechecks and one simultaneous movement batch. Earlier decisions
are included in later prompts. Empty, token, foreign-owned, disabled and settled
payments cannot contribute. A changed top cannot substitute for the proposed
card; one invalid candidate does not cancel another. Results exist before zone
events. This bounded single-resource batch has no partially spent mana or costs
to roll back; broader heterogeneous plural payments remain unsupported.

No existing life-total-setting effect was found. Its required consumer captures
deltas, then uses prepareLifeGain/prepareLifeLoss in APNAP order. Ordinary life
changes finish before gain/loss events. Permissions and replacement outcomes
retain normal behavior; setting a total does not bypass life-gain replacements.
Equal totals do nothing. Overflow errors precede replacements and changes.

### Exact supported shape and engine boundary

`TriggerA(WhenAnyNumberOfCreaturesAttack(filter), actions)` accepts exactly
`IsCardtype(Creature)` or a two-member `And` containing that type and
`ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))`, in either order. Other filters fail
compilation rather than being approximated. The event body can use
`EachPlayerAction(Trigger_ThoseDefendingPlayers, action)` through the existing
scoped player-action compiler. The symbol is legal only in this event body;
it does not become a singular player reference or leak into other abilities.

`controlledAttackBatchPattern.WithDefendingPlayer(*PlayerBinding)` extends both
`OneOrMoreCreaturesAttack()` and `OneOrMoreCreaturesYouControlAttack()`. Definition
validation rejects nil and repeated capture declarations. It composes with
`WithCount(*NumberBinding)`. In this two-player engine the event's declaring
player has exactly one defending opponent. Detection saves that player's ID,
including for attacks on a planeswalker or battle; resolution does not query
current combat, current source control or the current active player.

The engine owns the capture, validation metadata and ordinary execution frames.
RON owns the syntax, exact filter shape, lexical collection scope and lowering.
A private `scope.attackGroup` plan and the existing per-instance defender-binding
map connect the producer and consumers. Each factory allocates a fresh binding.
Reuse declaration events from both `doDeclareAttackers` and `ExecuteAttackers`,
APNAP trigger placement, pending trigger snapshots, source identity, effect
sequencing and copied/cloned resolution frames. No new event type, history store,
last-action slot, speculative execution or production registry is introduced.

Read CR 508.1–508.5 and 603.1–603.3. Nonempty declaration groups trigger once;
entering attacking does not count (508.4). Event facts and ability control are
captured at detection (603.2, 603.3a). Phasing and ability removal before the event
suspend observation; after detection they cannot erase pending facts. No cost,
replacement, damage or simultaneous zone-operation contract changes in this slice.

### Established signatures and contracts

Engine API:

- `NamedPermanentPile{Name string, Result *PermanentSetBinding}`.
- `SeparatePermanentsIntoNamedPiles(player PlayerRef, subjects PermanentSet,
  piles ...NamedPermanentPile) ResolvingEffect`.
- Existing `BindPermanentSet` and `FromPermanentSet` declare and read each output.

The action snapshots distinct present, unphased battlefield visits. Input sets
are read before old output values are cleared, including when a previous pile
is partitioned again. The specified player assigns each visit to exactly one
pile with a required `ChooseMode` decision. Later decisions display earlier
public assignments. An invalid decision index uses the first pile. Piles can
be empty; objects stay on the battlefield. At least two distinct nonempty names
and distinct non-nil output bindings are required at definition validation.
Shared resolution frames preserve results through repeated resolutions, delays
and clones. Returned visits and new members cannot replace saved visits; phase
cycles preserve membership but phased members cannot be selected. No LKI is
used to supply absent members.

RON shape, only in an ordinary resolving attack-group defender action:

`EachPlayerAction(Trigger_ThoseDefendingPlayers,
SeparatePermanentsIntoNamedPiles(filter, ["Left", "Right"]))`.

Additional distinct names use the same shape. Existing contextual permanent
collections lower `filter`. `EachablePlayer` is a typed player reference only
inside this filter and selects the saved event defender. It cannot escape into
a subsequent action. Each effect factory creates fresh pile bindings. The
adapter currently exports no RON pile reader or selected-pile result. This
producer executes fully, while dependent pile-choice declarations remain
rejected. A subsequent slice must connect those scoped producer/consumer plans.

### Supported signatures and rules boundary

Engine: `RetainBlockerEligibility(duration core.Duration, subject PermanentRef,
eligible PermanentSet, allowed RetainedBlockerFilter) ResolvingEffect`.
Durations are `EndOfCombat` and `EndOfTurn`. `CurrentBlockers(PermanentFilter)`
checks current properties; `SavedBlockers(PermanentSet)` captures exact unphased
visits. `AllRetainedBlockers(...RetainedBlockerFilter)` and
`AnyRetainedBlockers(...RetainedBlockerFilter)` compose nonempty conditions.
Zero conditions, absent references/sets, unsupported durations, undominated
set reads and undeclared targets fail definition validation.

The action captures eligible visits and saved predicate leaves, then installs
`Until(duration, CantBeBlockedExceptBy(subject, filter))`. It adds no combat
storage, zone service, frame lifetime or replacement pipeline. Immutable saved
membership cannot follow returned objects or later binding writes. Current
properties read the querying game. Source departure, source phasing and ability
removal do not erase the installed rule. A subject phase cycle retains it;
returned subjects cannot inherit it. End-combat priority retains the rule;
native phase completion removes it. Clones expire separately.

RON: ordinary resolving
`CreatePermanentRuleEffectUntil(EachablePermanent,
[CantBeBlockedExceptByDefenders(filter)], UntilEndOfCombat)` after a preceding
partition and named choice for this same loop member. Filter leaves use existing
ordinary permanent filters or the scoped
`InThePileChosenForPermanent(EachablePermanent)` reader; nonempty `And`/`Or`
compose them. Reject malformed operations, mixed lists, wrong references,
missing producers, branch leaks, nested-loop substitution and other durations.
Saved delayed frames retain these lexical results and exact subjects.

The adapter captures all present creature visits, including flyers. It does
not freeze control or flying: normal declaration legality supplies defending
control, and the predicate reads current flying. This refines the earlier
candidate's shorthand “defending creature visits” without adding a historical
controller restriction absent from Oracle. The two WotC rulings require that
new entrants and newly animated permanents cannot block already affected
attackers, even with flying; later attacking entrants receive no installed rule.

### Supported signatures and rules boundary

Engine: `MaySkipYourTurnToUntap(subject PermanentRef, condition StateCondition)
StaticRule`, installed with `Static`. Subject is `This` or `AttachedPermanent`;
conditions and references must pass definition validation. No unbound targets,
absent conditions or invalid subjects. Runtime source presence, visit, abilities,
condition and controller govern each offer. Phasing and ability removal stop
new offers. A source phase cycle retains its visit.

`Game.TryBeginTurn() bool` proposes a turn through the shared replacement
pipeline. Existing scheduled skips become local candidates in that pipeline;
the affected player chooses their order with optional rules. Each candidate
can apply once. A decline leaves other candidates available. An accepted skip
ends the proposed event and does not consume other scheduled skips. Repeated
start requests keep the attempted turn/player result. `BeginActiveTurn` marks
an accepted turn so a later request cannot replace an already started turn.

An optional paid skip saves the subject's exact battlefield visit in
`TurnSystem.pendingTurnUntaps`. Intermediate skipped turns keep it. The next
turn that survives replacements performs normal start lifecycle/history work,
then untaps saved subjects in its first actual step before step actions.
The step runner checks step skips and sets the current step before these
untaps. Skipped steps retain them, and events cannot observe a stale step. This is CR 614.10b, rather
than an immediate untap between turns. The shared untap service handles stun
counters and events. Source departure, ability removal and controller changes
after acceptance cannot cancel the continuation. Returned objects cannot
inherit it. A phased-out subject cannot untap, while a completed phase cycle
retains its identity. Clones copy both pending visits and attempted-turn state.
No second scheduler, cost transaction, zone system or replacement pipeline.

RON: conditional static bodies support exactly
`ReplaceWouldBeginATurn(PlayerWouldBeginTheirTurn(You), [MayCost(SkipThisTurn),
If(CostWasPaid, [UntapPermanent(ThisPermanent)])])`. The outer static condition
uses its existing compiler. Cost and result are bare symbols, and this result
does not escape into resolution scopes. Other event players, subjects, actions,
operation counts and malformed arities reject with positioned errors. The
inventory assigns separate event, cost, payment-result and continuation roles.

Native `RunTurn`, gametest, single- and multiplayer interactive loops, and
`cmd/gametest`/`cmd/scenariotest` use the shared turn-start boundary. The
whole-repository caller audit finds no remaining production driver consuming
scheduled skips separately. Direct step and AI search runners retain their
existing role inside an accepted turn. Keep public schedule callers compatible.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

RON accepts exactly
`CreateGameEffect(UntilEndOfTurn, DefendingPlayersChooseCreaturesToDefendAttackersAtRandom)`
in an ordinary resolving body. Both operands must be symbols. Entry and draw
replacement contexts, other durations, unknown operations and wrong arity reject
at compilation. Inventory roles are `duration` and `temporary_game_operation`.
The compiler produces `mage.RandomizeBlockingPilesThisTurn() ResolvingEffect`.
It owns spelling and declaration validation; all decisions and execution stay
in the engine.

The effect saves a source-independent turn flag in TurnSystem. Clones copy it;
turn changes and cleanup clear it; later combats in the same turn retain it.
Copies install the same procedure without multiplying choices. At the blocker
boundary, current attacking visits determine pile count, including attacks on
the defender's permanents. Present controlled creatures may enter optional
piles. Additional blocking capacity permits distinct additional pile membership.
ChooseMode supplies existing UI and search-player decisions, with public prior
pile contents. Invalid optional answers decline the remaining choices.

After all pile choices, Fisher-Yates uses shared game RNG to assign every pile
to a distinct attacker. Empty piles are valid; zero or one attacker consumes no
random result. Captured visits protect both sides against leave-and-return.
The existing blocking planner validates the proposed random pairs for current
status, controller, evasion, protection, landwalk, capacity, bands and minimum
blocker counts. Its preferred-legal path cannot add a creature or redirect a
random assignment to satisfy a requirement. The card's optional creature/pile
procedure replaces the ordinary declaration choice (CR 101.1).

Both doDeclareBlockers and ExecuteBlockers enter the shared commit path. The
native path does not request an ordinary DeclareBlockers answer. An explicit
AI assignment cannot bypass the random procedure. Pure feasibility queries make
no choices and consume no RNG. Existing combat commit, histories, grouped/pair
and blocked/unblocked events observe the completed batch. No separate combat,
cost, replacement, target or zone system is added. Casting and rollback reuse
the existing spell payment and timing services.

### Supported contract and reuse boundary

Engine APIs:

- `(*Game).SetOutsideGameCards(uuid.UUID, []Card) error` atomically supplies a
  permitted pool of owned traditional cards. Reject nil/token/foreign/duplicate
  cards, unknown players and cards already in any game zone, including phased
  permanents. Input cards are copied; each pool membership gets a new identity.
- `(*Game).OutsideGameCards(uuid.UUID) []Card` returns separate snapshots.
  Outside the game is not a zone. The pool is not exposed through GameReader.
- `PutOutsideGameCardInHand(PlayerRef, CardFilter) ResolvingEffect` makes one
  required choice at resolution. A zero filter means any eligible card. Empty
  pools do nothing. Invalid answers use the first candidate. Answers select
  identity only; they cannot supply new characteristics or ownership.
- `Player.ChooseCardFromOutsideGame([]Card, string, GameReader) Card` has native
  human, AI, search and default implementations. Human/TUI/pylib choices have
  a distinct kind. AI and search reuse existing hand-benefit selection.
- `OutsideGameEntryAction` exposes `ActionSource`, `PlayerID` and `CardID` to
  shared replacement ordering. Cancellation leaves membership untouched.

Recheck exact membership, absence from game zones, ownership, filter and ante
restriction after choices and replacements. A returned pool membership cannot
replace a saved one. On success, remove membership and add to the owner's hand
before the shared entry notification. EvtZoneChange uses ZoneAny only for the
absent origin, never as storage. Entry is not a draw, reveal, target or random
operation. Clone cards and membership independently. No new zone, last-action
slot, card-name branch or registry fallback is introduced.

RON owns `PutACardFromOutsideGameInHand(AnyCard)` spelling, arity and context.
Accept resolving bodies, explicit PlayerAction, and future draw replacement
bodies; read the lexical typed player. Reject other filters, callable AnyCard,
wrong arity and entry/static/cost contexts. Inventory marks the argument as
`card_filter`. No new result binding escapes the operation.

Use CR 108.2b, 108.3/3b, 108.5, 400.11, 407.3 and 614.5/6/11. Existing payment,
source LKI, future draw capture, affected-player ordering, hand visits, event
notification and clone services retain their contracts. Applications supply the
pool allowed by their match or casual-game policy; no registry catalog is used
as an implicit sideboard. Runtime registry cutover remains separate work.

### Established shape and API

RON accepts `MayCost(ChooseACardInHand(filter))` and
`PlayerMayCost(playerRef, ChooseACardInHand(filter))` in ordinary resolving
spell and ability sequences. The adjacent `If`, `Unless` or `IfElse` must test
the symbol `CostWasPaid` or `CostWasntPaid`; each provided branch is nonempty.
`AnyCard` is a standalone symbol filter. Existing hand predicates support card
type, non-type, color, non-color and nonempty And/Or lists. The engine exposes:

`ChooseHandCardOrElse(PlayerRef, CardFilter, *CardBinding, ResolvingEffect, ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`

The operation saves a private exact hand visit, makes no move or reveal, and
runs one branch. Empty candidate sets skip decisions. Declined, nil, foreign,
newly added, departed or returned selections use the unpaid branch. Candidate
copies cannot change canonical cards. Current membership and filters are checked
after the response. The chooser supplies an ID, never authoritative card facts.
Source departure, control change and phasing do not cancel pending instructions.

RON owns syntax, filter validation and lexical scope. The engine owns selection,
current hand membership, visit identity and local runtime frames. Each factory
allocates fresh result bindings. `TheCardInHandChosenThisWay` is a symbol usable
as a private card reference in the existing `ExchangeOwnershipOfTwoCards`
adapter, only on the successful path. The existing ownership service retains its
ante gate. Other zone-role adapters cannot mistake this for a graveyard,
revealed-hand or permanent reference. Face-down casting is still unsupported.

Declaration validation rejects nil players/results, absent branches, unpaid or
later reads, and nested reuse of an already assigned result binding. Nested
calls restore outer results. FromCard rejects departed visits without hand LKI.
Shared stack copy, resolution capture and clone services supply isolation. No new
payment transaction, zone move, simultaneous batch or replacement ordering rule
is introduced. No Go-card fallback, declaration panic or global result slot is
added. The removal gates remain unmet; no Go definitions or DSL exports change.
