### Exact supported signatures, dependencies and reuse

Engine API:

- `BindActivationMana(name string) *ActivationManaBinding`.
- `WithActivationManaReceipt(binding *ActivationManaBinding) ActionOption` saves
  the total actual payment on one nonmodal nonmana activated ability.
- `WithActivationManaXReceipt(binding *ActivationManaBinding) ActionOption`
  saves the X component of one pure `{X}` cost on that same ability context.
- `ChooseHandCardWithActivationManaOrElse(player PlayerRef, filter CardFilter,
  receipt *ActivationManaBinding, result *CardBinding, chosen, notChosen
  ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.

RON supports symbol-form `ManaCostIsSubsetOfManaPaidForThisAbility` alone or
within nested `And` conjunctions of supported static hand filters, as the filter
of `ChooseACardInHand` in `MayCost` or `PlayerMayCost`. The immediate activation
must be nonmodal and nonmana, with the exact declaration
`PayManaX([ManaCostX], ValueX)`. The existing paid-path If/Unless/IfElse rules
remain in force. Fixed/composite costs, Or containing this predicate, tuple
predicates, spell/entry/delayed contexts and unbound results reject. This is one
complete supported declaration context, not a claim for every hand-filter form.

Extend the shared pool payment allocator with an internal receipt return.
The shared transaction retains actual amounts and types, excludes tax-assigned
mana from X, respects reductions, and publishes captures only after successful
payment. Fixed requirements receive mana first; remaining paid generic mana up
to announced X belongs to X. The receipt tracks actual types even under spending
permissions. Eligibility uses a fresh local pool and the shared allocator without
live spending permissions or cost modifiers. Hand X is zero; absent costs
reject and printed zero costs can match an empty receipt. No private card is
moved or revealed by the choice.

Reuse captured `NumberBinding` maps for immutable receipt amounts, preserving
existing clone and stack-copy services. Each factory creates a fresh typed
receipt declaration; each activation saves distinct values. Source identity,
phasing, control and LKI do not replace payment facts. Hand identity, canonical
answer validation, scope restoration and private candidates reuse the existing
optional-hand service. No game-time declaration panic, global last-action slot,
Go-card fallback or partial registry is introduced. Preserve existing callers;
no deletion gate is met and no DSL function is removed.

in an ordinary resolving body with a successful optional hand-choice binding.
It rejects other references, unbound reads, malformed arities, nonliteral or
nonstandard P/T, entry bodies and draw-replacement bodies. The current action
player supplies the caster. No spell-result binding or permanent-result reader
is fabricated. The full records reject at `CreateReplaceWouldMaskUntil`.

Engine API:
`CastHandCardFaceDownWithoutPaying(player PlayerRef, card CardRef) ResolvingEffect`;
`(*StackObject).IsFaceDown() bool`;
`(*Game).InspectFaceDownObject(viewer, id uuid.UUID) Card`.

The cast uses an object-local face-down definition with retained private printed
identity. Restrictions, external taxes, shared transactional mana payment,
spell insertion, cast event/history, entry replacements, battlefield layers,
copying, phasing and zone movement use existing services. The printed face-up
mana cost, targets, additional costs and entry rules cannot apply. The spell is
nameless, colorless, textless, 2/2 and has no mana cost; its X and mana value are
zero. It stays on the stack for responses and countering. Entry status precedes
entry rules/events. Exact selected hand visits cannot follow returns.

Inspection uses the exact spell ID or permanent ID and the current controller;
phased permanents retain permission. Public reveal history records departure
and reads remaining face-down cards when the game ends, without state mutation.
Spell copies keep public copiable values without status or private identity;
permanent copies keep status, later face-up values and physical departure
identity. New face-down values use ordinary continuous grants and summoning
sickness. Legacy callers keep their existing representation. Current owner and
ID override stale retained departure definitions without changing those shared
definitions. Copies, source departure and game clones keep separate state.

RON owns syntax, contexts and the existing typed hand-card reference. Mage owns
all casting, status, private identity, reveal and physical-card movement. No
card-name branch, Go-card fallback, last-action slot, game-time declaration panic
or partial registry is added. No deletion gate is met; no DSL function or Go
card is removed. RON source is unchanged, so no vocabulary hash refresh is needed.

Supported syntax, in an ordinary resolving sequence after its local saved cast:

```text
CreateReplaceWouldMaskUntil(
  PermanentWouldAssignDamageDealDamageBeDealDamageOrBecomeTapped(ThePermanentSpellResolvedThisWay),
  [TurnItFaceUpInstead],
  UntilPermanentIsTurnedFaceUp(ThePermanentSpellResolvedThisWay))
```

Both operands must bind the same saved cast result. The operation is one symbol;
malformed arguments, different references, unbound/premature/escaped results and
entry/draw replacement contexts reject. There is no partial operation list.
RON owns spelling, context and lexical binding. The engine API is
`TurnResolvedPermanentFaceUpBeforeAction(DamageSourceRef) ResolvingEffect`.
It saves exact card and stack identities, including a pending spell, and
installs a persistent, source-independent replacement. Countered spells,
spell copies and returned objects do not supply its permanent. Control changes
keep it; phasing suspends it. Turning face up ends it permanently. A per-visit history field also prevents
late installation from restarting it after a face-up/face-down cycle. The explicit
permanent clone retains this history; it is not a copiable characteristic.

The engine adds exact tap and combat-assignment proposals to the existing
replacement pipeline. Its face-up operation restores characteristics, abilities
and layers before the original event continues. Damage batches refresh every
packet from the exact revealed source before replacement rechecks. Protection
therefore reads revealed colors; lifelink uses the revealed source. Group taps
still complete transitions before events. Strike eligibility is captured for the assignment operation before face-up
changes; the prior scope is restored on return and clones isolate its map.
Zero damage, zero power, suppressed
assignment, absent combat recipients, ineligible strike steps and already-tapped
subjects cannot cause this replacement. Standard face-down cards no longer use unconditional post-damage face-up
code. The old status-only representation retains its existing post-damage
behavior until Go callers migrate. This compatibility branch checks representation,
not a card name, and cannot supply a RON fallback.

Payment trials, clone replacement copies, continuous layers, event delivery,
source identity, stack resolution and simultaneous damage retain shared engine
ownership. No card-name engine branch, Go-card fallback, global action slot,
partial registry or new priority window is introduced. No Go definitions or DSL
exports are removed before the runtime cutover gates.

### Exact contract and ownership

Engine signature:

```go
func InspectDirectDestruction(ResolvingEffect) ([]DirectDestructionInstruction, bool)
```

`DirectDestructionInstruction` has `Subject PermanentRef`,
`Subjects PermanentSet`, and `CannotRegenerate bool`. Exactly one subject field
is set. Supported leaves are `Destroy`, `DestroyWithoutRegeneration`,
`DestroyEach` and `DestroyEachWithoutRegeneration` without result options.
Nested `Sequence` and `CompositeEffects` preserve declaration order. Empty
sequences succeed with no instructions. A simultaneous set remains one group.
Each call returns a fresh slice of descriptor values, retaining the exact typed
operand declarations. There is no stored or global game state.

Nil effects and operands, result options, conditions, choices and opaque effects
are unsupported. One unsupported child returns `nil, false` for the entire
tree, including when a known destruction precedes it. Inspection calls no
execution, reference, filter, text, AI-property, choice or RNG callback. It
needs no game and makes no claim about target legality, selected objects,
replacement results, destruction or binding validity. It is not a definition
validator or a boolean preview of a spell's outcome.

RON's `compileDirectDestruction` owns the four exact one-argument action forms:
`DestroyPermanent(ref)`, `DestroyPermanentNoRegen(ref)`,
`DestroyEachPermanent(collection)`, `DestroyEachPermanentNoRegen(collection)`.
It retains existing typed reference, contextual collection, arity and lexical
scope validation. The action switch routes those forms to this one adapter.
Factories still allocate private target declarations. No RON spelling moves
into the engine. Existing result-producing destruction adapters remain intact.

The descriptor inspects existing typed engine actions, rather than display text,
AI hints, card names or Go-card constructors. Native target checks, resolution
frames, incarnation identity, phasing, cloning, destruction batches,
regeneration and replacement ordering remain owned by existing services.
CR 608.2b/c/f, 701.8, 614.6–8 and 702.12 establish the execution boundaries.
Pure legality, replacement and sequential outcome analysis remain subsequent
work. This slice introduces no speculation against live game state.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

```go
func HasCardTypeFilter(core.CardType) PermanentFilter
func InspectPermanentCardTypeFilter(PermanentFilter) (PermanentCardTypePredicate, bool)
func (PermanentCardTypePredicate) Matches(...core.CardType) bool
```

The predicate is immutable and has no object, binding, game or chosen state.
It supports typed card-type leaves, native IsCreature/IsArtifact/IsEnchantment/
IsLand/IsPlaneswalker, AnyPermanent, the zero filter, and complete Not/And/Or
trees. Empty conjunctions match; empty disjunctions do not. Any opaque child
rejects the entire query even below a short-circuited branch. Display labels
never establish support. A failed query must be distinguished using its success
flag. The zero predicate matches every supplied set.

`Matches` reads only the supplied type slice and does not retain it. Inspection
and evaluation call no runtime filter callback, game query, effect, choice or
RNG service. The caller supplies current types after layers. Native runtime
matching still calls `Permanent.HasType`; labels and zero-filter behavior stay
compatible. Boolean constructors now copy their variadic input slices so caller
mutation cannot make native behavior disagree with the immutable plan.

RON owns `IsCardtype(type)`, `IsNonCardtype(type)`, `AnyPermanent`,
`And([filters])` and `Or([filters])` and their arity/type validation in existing
`compileFilter` contexts. `ron.IsCardtype` delegates to the typed engine leaf.
No RON spelling or card policy enters the engine. Other valid runtime filters
retain execution support but reject this narrower pure query.

Dependencies: existing current type/attribute and layer services, normal target
bindings, declaration inspection and clone services. CR 205.1, 205.2b and
613.1d define type sets and layer timing. CR 608.2b/c/f continues to own target
legality, instruction order and simultaneous operations. This API establishes
no target selection, phasing presence, incarnation identity, LKI, destruction
replacement, payment rollback or prospective outcome. It cannot consume a shield,
change a resolution frame or execute a game. These are explicit later contracts.

### Engine, compiler and reuse boundary

- `InspectPermanentCollection(PermanentSet) (PermanentCollectionPredicate, bool)`
  accepts type-only `matchingPermanentSet` and complete nonempty union or
  intersection trees. It reuses `InspectPermanentCardTypeFilter` and immutable
  typed Boolean nodes. Nil, opaque, controlled and empty compositions reject;
  unknown children reject even under an otherwise decisive branch.
- `PermanentCollectionPredicate.Select(*Game) []PermanentVisit` returns separate
  ordered value snapshots. `PermanentVisit` has `ID` and `Incarnation` UUIDs.
  It reads `Permanent.HasType` and current battlefield presence. It does not
  resolve collection references, call filter callbacks, update layers, use LKI,
  make choices, consume RNG or write resolution bindings. Callers supply current
  layers. A zero/failed plan or nil game supplies no members.
- `compileDestructionCollection(Node, scope) (permanentSetFactory, error)` first
  validates the full existing contextual collection. Complete type-only `And`
  and `Or` predicates then lower to one typed matching declaration. Contextual
  collections retain their original runtime lowering. Nested empty collections
  still reject. The four direct destruction forms retain existing contexts,
  regeneration flags and simultaneous operation services.

RON owns syntax and validation. The engine owns current membership, identity and
pure plans. No card-name branch, fallback registry, new global state, payment
mechanic or replacement system was added. Targets, scope-bound controllers,
protection and destruction certainty are outside this supported shape. Engine
inspection reports unknown rather than assuming an empty collection. A selected
indestructible or regenerating member is still selected.

### Contract, implementation and boundaries

Engine signatures:

- `PermanentTargetPredicate.Select(*Game, *StackObject) ([]PermanentVisit, bool)`.

Inspection requires a singular `PermanentTargetBinding` with complete type-only
filters and no additional target restrictions. It captures the exact declaration,
not a name or choices. RON's `compileInspectableTargetFilter(Node)` lowers
`AnyPermanent`, `IsCardtype(type)`, `IsNonCardtype(type)` and nonempty Boolean
type-only target trees. It is called from `compilePermanentTargetFilter`.

and lexical scope validation stay in RON.

Selection reads the aligned announced target slot, saved zone and exact
incarnation. Missing or ambiguous declarations and missing announcement evidence
return unknown. Illegal visits return a known empty selection. Phasing removes
presence; phasing in restores the same visit. Leave-and-return does not.
Current types, including layers and face-down state, use the shared type service.
Current layers are a caller precondition. Queries do not run effects, apply
layers, write bindings, choose objects, consume RNG or predict destruction.

The engine reuses `resolutionTargetSource` for spell colors and current,
phased or departed ability source information. Native `CanBeTargetedBy` and
the query share `canBeTargetedByCharacteristics`, preserving shroud, hexproof,
color protection and fixed attribute restrictions. Native resolution retains
its complete global restriction service. The pure query reports unknown for
Aura sources, noncolor protection and global target restrictions of the
applicable spell/ability kind. It does not call their filter, subject, activity
or condition callbacks, even when a source appears inactive or unrelated.
No parallel targeting rule implementation, game simulation, global action slot,
card-name branch or partial production registry was added.

### Contract, compiler context and reuse

`InspectReplacementActionDomains(ReplacementEffect) (ReplacementActionDomains,
bool)` reads complete coarse categories from a closed native type set.
`ReplacementDamageActions` covers damage-to-player and damage-to-permanent
proposals. `ReplacementDestructionActions` covers destruction proposals.
A known category bounds possible matches; it proves neither activity nor an
individual match. Unknown does not mean an empty set.

The supported set has 25 damage-only types and three destruction-only types.
Native damage shields, combat prevention, filtered/static/counter prevention,
instruction prevention, expansion and redirection are damage-only. Regeneration,
static regeneration and next-destruction cancellation are destruction-only.
Nil, typed-nil, opaque, derived, unclassified and mixed-domain rules are unknown.
Death exile, death return and face-up action replacements are explicitly not
misclassified. Damage-history predicates do not change a replacement's domain.

`Game.InspectDestructionProposal` now ignores proven damage-only replacements in
both persistent and cycle lists, retaining its exact-visit, indestructibility,
regeneration, prohibition, cancellation and conservative unknown contracts.
Local candidates, live damage-history regeneration restrictions and unclassified
rules retain their prior treatment. No rule `IsActive`, `Matches` or `Replace`,
operand callback, filter, choice, effect or RNG runs. No shield, counter, damage,
tap state, combat state, stack or zone changes. Native replacement execution,
ordering, rechecks, batching and payment rollback services remain unchanged.

one-argument destruction forms into `directDestructionPlan` before factory
execution. `build(instanceBindings)` constructs `DirectDestructionInstruction`
with fresh scoped singular references or simultaneous collections and the exact
cannot-regenerate flag. `compileDirectDestruction` lowers that plan to the native
execution descriptor. Scope and source/target/event identity use the existing
shared reference compiler; no new spelling, callback proof or fallback is added.

### Contract, lowering and reuse boundary

`(*Game).InspectDestructionDestinations(PermanentVisit, bool)
(DestructionDestinations, bool)` establishes the complete supported singular
proposal context. The bool input forbids regeneration; the bool result is known.
`DestructionNoMove`, `DestructionToGraveyard`, `DestructionToExile` and
`DestructionToHand` form a set of possible terminal moves. Tokens report their
proposed move before they cease to exist, not a surviving card. Owner destinations remain
native. Callers first select targets/subjects and make layers current.

Supported rules are native regeneration shields, current static regeneration,
saved next-destruction cancellation, exact saved singular death-exile rules,
current death-return-with-play-lock declarations and proven damage-only domains.
Both persistent and cycle lists are read. Current local declarations account
for their corresponding registered replacement objects. Each supported
candidate ends destruction or changes the graveyard destination, after which
other supported candidates cannot match. All possible first choices therefore
supply the exact destination set without executing replacement choices.

Missing/incomplete visits are distinguished from absent, returned, phased or
indestructible objects. Cannot-regenerate and current prohibitions suppress
regeneration only. Face-down and removed local abilities do not apply. Source
departure does not end saved exile. Phasing preserves the visit; return does not.
Cleanup removes end-of-turn exile. Live death-history filters, opaque, derived,
nil and unsupported mixed-domain rules remain unknown even beside a known
candidate. A live regeneration prohibition is unknown only if regeneration
would otherwise be available. No method callback, operand filter, choice,
effect or RNG runs. No replacement, shield, damage, counter, tap/combat state,
visibility, stack, cost or zone state changes.

RON's `compileTemporaryDeathExilePlan(Node, scope)` validates the existing
`CreateReplaceWouldPutIntoGraveyardUntil(APermanentWouldDie(SinglePermanent(ref)),
[ExileItInstead], UntilEndOfTurn)` into `temporaryDeathExilePlan`.
`build(instanceBindings) mage.Effect` uses shared
`ExileIfWouldDieThisTurn`; the existing history shape retains its typed source
and filter through `ExileDealtDamageByThisTurn`. The private plan owns syntax,
validation and per-instance bindings; the engine owns destination semantics.
No new syntax, scope escape, global result slot or card-specific branch is added.

Native replacement execution, affected-controller ordering, rechecks, payment
rollback, source information/LKI, durations, clones and simultaneous zone batches
remain shared and unchanged. The old `InspectDestructionProposal` API and all
callers remain supported. This is one singular destination capability, not
sequential future-state or simultaneous-group analysis. Equinox stays rejected.
No production registry, card definition, startup path, generator or DSL API is
removed before its gate.

CR 614.1–8, 616.1, 701.8, 702.12 and 702.26 establish replacement rechecks,

bool)` adds these closed native cases:

  `LifeGainAction` proposals only. Its generated draws do not expand its input
  domain, nor do arbitrary actions in a draw replacement body.

The query calls no replacement method, operand, effect, filter or decision.

predicate is also declared. Context-free collection inspection still rejects
any combat descendant.

### Contract, lowering and reuse boundary

New APIs:

- `InspectOrderedDestruction(ResolvingEffect) (OrderedDestructionPredicate, bool)`.
- `OrderedDestructionPredicate.Certain(*EffectContext, []PermanentVisit) (certain, known bool)`.

The retained tree accepts complete `Sequence`/`CompositeEffects` trees of native
collection destruction instructions, including empty trees and regeneration
prohibition. Every collection must have a complete contextual pure declaration.
Singular subjects, result writes, opaque descendants and malformed operands
reject the whole tree. No opaque callback runs, including a masked unknown child.

`Certain` uses the action's current resolving controller and supplied exact
watched visits. The caller establishes current layers, source resolution and
target legality. These are instruction queries, not whole-spell predictions.
A watched member with only the graveyard destination supplies a proof within
its simultaneous group. Known complete alternatives do not supply that proof.
Unknown replacement behavior reports unknown. Empty groups permit the next
instruction. Any nonempty group without a proof stops before later instructions:
regeneration can change tap/combat state and consume a replacement without a move.
The second result distinguishes a complete query with no proof from unknown;
no proof does not assert that destruction is impossible.

RON already lowers `DestroyEachPermanent/1` and
`DestroyEachPermanentNoRegen/1` through `compileDirectDestructionPlan`, preserves
Boolean/contextual collections through `compileDestructionCollection`, and keeps
`ActionList` order. These exact AST adapters now feed the new engine query; no
new spelling or duplicate compiler executor is required. The retained native
instruction/collection declarations are the reuse boundary. Execution still
uses the existing simultaneous destruction and replacement pipeline. No card
branch, production fallback, global action slot or game-time panic was added.

to a successful prospective-spell predicate.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

Added `(*Game).InspectSpellDestruction(*StackObject, []PermanentVisit)
(certain, known bool)`. Supply current layers and the exact live instant or
sorcery stack object, including an object below the current top. The method
inspects the complete announced effect tree with `InspectDirectDestruction`.
Singular subjects must be native type-only permanent target bindings. Collections
must pass `InspectContextualPermanentCollection`. All announced targets must
pass `InspectPermanentTarget`, including declarations unused by the actions.
Duplicate declarations, missing snapshots, unknown filters, unbound subjects,
unknown descendants, abilities and detached objects return unknown.

Every current target legality check precedes destruction analysis. All-illegal
targets prevent the whole spell from resolving, including untargeted collections.
With a legal remaining target, illegal singular instructions have empty groups.
Selections preserve exact declaration and announced visit identity; returned
objects cannot substitute. Phasing out removes a target and phasing in restores
that visit. The spell controller supplies the collection context. Shared source
characteristics establish protection legality; this spell-only API does not
change ability source LKI.

True/true proves a watched exact visit must move to the graveyard in a direct
destruction group. False/true means no proof in the supported tree; false/false
means unknown. It is not valid to interpret unknown as proof of no destruction.
`InspectDestructionDestinations` retains regeneration, cancellation, death return,
exile and competing destination behavior. Groups retain simultaneous membership.
Empty/illegal groups permit the next instruction. Any nonempty group without a
proof stops later analysis, including regeneration that makes no zone move.
No callbacks, replacement choices, shield use, RNG, speculative execution,
binding writes, layer updates or game mutations occur.

forms with exact per-factory references. `ActionList` keeps order. Their native

### Exact shapes, engine reuse and rules

Existing engine signatures `HasPowerEqual(int) PermanentFilter`,
`HasToughnessEqual(int) PermanentFilter` and `HasToughnessGTE(int) PermanentFilter`
now retain immutable numeric nodes in the shared permanent filter tree.
`fixedNumericPermanentFilter(string, permanentCollectionFilterOperation, int)`
constructs each native filter and its query from the same comparison method.
`InspectPermanentTarget(PermanentRef) (PermanentTargetPredicate, bool)` accepts
these complete numeric trees. Its existing `Select(*Game, *StackObject)
([]PermanentVisit, bool)` contract supplies exact declared and announced visits.

RON `compileInspectableTargetFilter(Node) (mage.PermanentFilter, bool, error)`
now retains the existing fixed adapters in these supported target contexts:

- `PowerAndToughnessIsEqualTo(PT(integer, integer))`.
- `ToughnessIs(EqualTo(Integer(integer)))`.
- `ToughnessIs(LessThanOrEqualTo(Integer(integer)))`.
- `ToughnessIs(GreaterThanOrEqualTo(Integer(integer)))`.
- Complete nested `And`/`Or` trees with the other supported target predicates.
  Engine `Not` trees retain the same numeric nodes.

The upper bound remains a union of less-than and equality without arithmetic,
so machine-limit operands cannot overflow. Negative and zero values retain
normal numeric comparisons. Malformed operands and unsupported descendants
reject at compilation; source-relative comparisons keep their separate scope
adapter. RON owns syntax and scope; the engine owns current numeric reads.

Shared collection inspection can also read these fixed nodes. Layers must be
current. Base values, modifications, counters and switches use existing P/T
services. The shared target service retains current protection, shroud, control,
visit and phasing rules. No target LKI or global action slot was added. Factory

### Contract and reuse boundary

New engine signatures:

- `DirectReturnInstruction{Subject PermanentRef, Subjects PermanentSet}`.
- `(DirectReturnInstruction).Effect() ResolvingEffect`.
- `InspectDirectReturn(ResolvingEffect) ([]DirectReturnInstruction, bool)`.

Exactly one subject field must be present; malformed and typed-nil declarations
build no effect. Complete nested native return sequences and composites retain
order, declaration identity and simultaneous collections. Unknown children
reject the entire inspection without callbacks.

RON signatures and contexts:

- `compileDirectReturnPlan(Node, scope) (directReturnPlan, error)`.
- `directReturnPlan.build(instanceBindings) mage.DirectReturnInstruction`.
- `compileDirectReturn(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)`.
- Resolving `PutPermanentIntoItsOwnersHand(PermanentRef)` and
  `PutEachPermanentIntoItsOwnersHand(ContextualCollection)` retain their current
  lexical scopes, reference validation and per-instance bindings.

RON owns syntax, validation, scope and lowering. The engine owns instruction
retention, pure target/collection selection and exact-visit proofs. Execution
reuses `ReturnToHand`, `ReturnEachToHand`, native owner destinations and the
simultaneous zone-change service. No second zone executor, state simulation,
card-name branch, fallback, global action slot or partial registry was added.

`Game.InspectSpellDestruction` validates the entire return/destruction tree and
all announced targets before analysis. A return can remove watched current exact
visits from later destruction. When none remain, false/true proves no direct
destruction of those visits in the suffix. Return-only tails have no direct
destruction. Empty or illegal return groups permit the next instruction.
A nonempty return with remaining watched visits and later destruction returns
false/false: departure can change layers, attachments, membership and replacement
sources. It must not infer later state from the former battlefield. Other
nonempty destruction barriers remain. Positive direct-destruction proofs use
the existing destination and replacement inspection services.

Current layers and target legality apply. Returned objects cannot replace visits;
phasing suspends selection without changing identity. Copies use their own stack
controller and targets. Clones and independent factories keep separate state.
Queries do not execute effects or callbacks, make choices, consume shields or
RNG, move cards, change bindings or update layers. Native payment rollback,
replacement order, simultaneous events and APNAP are unchanged.

rulings for Boomerang, Remove Enchantments and Equinox. All three

Enchantments have explicit empty rulings arrays. Equinox's seven wotc rulings
require current certainty and distinguish direct destruction from damage,
sacrifice, indirect effects and choices. No scryfall note was treated as a
wotc ruling. No source defect or fetch failure was found.

This is a shared prerequisite, not a claim of complete collection gameplay.

### Exact contract and engine reuse

New engine declarations:

- `TapOperationKind` with `TapOperation`, `UntapOperation` and
  `MayTapOrUntapOperation`.
- `TapInstruction{Subject PermanentRef, Subjects PermanentSet, Operation TapOperationKind}`.
- `(TapInstruction).Effect() ResolvingEffect`.
- `InspectTapInstructions(ResolvingEffect) ([]TapInstruction, bool)`.

Exactly one subject field must be non-nil, including typed-nil checks. Ordinary
tap and untap accept singular or simultaneous collection subjects. Optional
tap-or-untap accepts only a singular subject. Invalid operations return nil.
Complete sequences and composites retain instruction order and group identity;
unknown children and result-bearing native instructions reject the whole tree.
Inspection neither calls operand/filter/effect callbacks nor offers choices.
Result slices contain declarations and do not alias mutable selection state.

RON uses `compileTapInstructionPlan(Node, scope) (tapInstructionPlan, error)` and
`tapInstructionPlan.build(instanceBindings) mage.TapInstruction`. Existing
resolving `TapPermanent/1`, `UntapPermanent/1`, `TapEachPermanent/1`,
`UntapEachPermanent/1` and `MayAction(TapOrUntapPermanent/1)` paths build these
plans. The optional spelling stays scoped to its existing wrapper. Costs,
result-producing paths and lexical restrictions keep their separate adapters.
Factories build fresh bindings; no chosen state lives in the compiled plan.

Native effects reuse `TapSubject`, `UntapPermanent`, `TapEach`, `UntapEach` and
`MayTapOrUntap`. No parallel tap, event, replacement or choice executor was added. The typed
boundary forwards native metadata and delayed source/stack-binding inspection.
Existing delayed tap and collection source tests initially exposed the missing
source forwarding; those tests passed after the wrapper delegated both marker
contracts. The wrapper stores no chosen state.
The new typed instruction boundary wraps one native action and refreshes continuous layers after its
full transition group and native events, before the next instruction. Untap also
refreshes when a stun counter replaces the transition. Legacy actions, costs and raw tap/untap
callers retain their existing contracts. Event-time layer refresh is not newly
established by this slice.

`Game.InspectSpellDestruction` validates complete native permanent targets and
pure contextual collections before considering any instruction. A tap-only tree
has no direct destruction proof and returns false/true. Nonempty tap/untap
instructions before later destruction return false/false, including optional
choices and currently tapped subjects. Empty collections and illegal subjects
can pass through when another target permits resolution. A supported tap suffix
does not invalidate an earlier destruction proof. Exact visits, source identity,
phasing, all-illegal resolution gates and complete-tree rejection remain intact.
No projection of changed layers or replacement choices is claimed.

### Exact contract and boundaries

- `PacketDamageInstruction{Source DamageSourceRef, Packets []DamagePacket}.
  Effect() ResolvingEffect`: one nonempty simultaneous group; missing or typed-nil
  operands return nil. Reuses `DealDamagePackets`, which copies its packet list.
- `InspectPacketDamageInstructions(ResolvingEffect)
  ([]PacketDamageInstruction, bool)`: complete native packet, sequence and
  composite trees; independent returned packet slices; unknown children reject
  the entire tree without callbacks.
- `InspectDamageRecipient(DamageRecipientRef) (DamageRecipientPredicate, bool)`
  and `DamageRecipientPredicate.Select(*Game, *StackObject)
  (DamageTargetSelection, bool)`: singular native any-target, any-player and
  opponent targets, `You`, and `ActivePlayer`. Native targets retain exact
  declaration identity and current legality. Missing/repeated/foreign bindings
  are unknown; illegal targets are empty known selections. Nil contexts and zero
  predicates are unknown. History, chooser, union-domain, saved and permanent
  references remain outside this bounded query.
- RON `SpellDealsMultipleDamage(source, [DamageToRecipients(amount, recipient),
  ...])/2` and `PermanentDealsMultipleDamage/2` retain existing complete spelling,
  source contexts, per-factory bindings, scope rejection and value adapters. The
  final lowering builds `PacketDamageInstruction.Effect()`. Other valid runtime
  operands still execute; pure inspection accepts only native `This` sources
  with fixed or X amounts and the recipients above.
- `Game.InspectSpellDestruction` validates every instruction, target and damage
  binding before all-illegal gating or an early destruction proof. Damage does
  not directly destroy a permanent. Any legal damage prefix, including zero,
  blocks later destruction proofs. An illegal packet recipient is skipped when
  another target is legal; all-illegal targets also prevent controller damage.
  Execution preserves simultaneous groups. Inspection may flatten packets since
  there is no intervening destruction instruction inside a group.

### Supported contract and boundaries

- `LifeInstruction{Subject PlayerRef, Amount ResolutionValue, Gain bool}.Effect()
  ResolvingEffect` builds the existing singular gain/loss action. Missing or
  typed-nil operands return nil. Current callers remain valid.
- `InspectLifeInstructions(ResolvingEffect) ([]LifeInstruction, bool)` retains
  complete native sequence/composite trees without callbacks. Unknown children,
  incomplete declarations and all result-bearing life actions reject the tree.
  Returned slices do not share mutable declaration storage.
- Ordinary RON `GainLife(amount)` / `LoseLife(amount)` and explicit
  `PlayerAction(playerRef, action)` scopes lower through the declaration.
  Snapshot-based `LoseLife_ThatPlayer` retains its existing contract and executor.
  Existing dynamic life expressions still execute; they are not accepted by the
  new pure query policy.
- `Game.InspectSpellDestruction` accepts fixed or native X amounts with complete
  native any-player/opponent target declarations, `You` or `ActivePlayer`.
  It validates every operand and exact declaration before an early destruction
  proof or the all-illegal gate. Missing, foreign and duplicate declarations,
  history/saved subjects, callback references and opaque amounts remain unknown.
- Life-only trees return false/true. A legal life prefix blocks later destruction
  proofs, even at zero or negative amounts. An illegal life subject is skipped
  when another target is legal. Supported life suffixes preserve an earlier
  direct destruction proof. No life, shield, replacement, choice or RNG is used
  during inspection. Repeated queries and cloned games retain the same result.
- Fixed/X amount classification is shared with native damage inspection through
  `pureFixedOrXAmount`. Execution still uses shared life permissions,
  replacements, history and events. Damage prevention does not prevent life loss.

  exposes `Effect() ResolvingEffect`, which returns nil for missing/typed-nil

  accepted shape: `CreateFuturePreventDamage(

  [PreventThatDamage])`. Existing arity, scope, operation and value checks remain.

  reject; zero and in-scope X remain valid. Existing dynamic execution remains.

  any-target or player targets, `You` and `ActivePlayer`. It checks the entire

  amounts. Illegal recipients are skipped when another target is legal.
  Supported suffixes preserve earlier proofs. Saved/history/opaque recipients,
  dynamic amounts and other prevention forms remain unknown to this policy.

  validates the complete announced count, distinct identities, exact aligned

- `Game.InspectSpellDestruction` validates plural declarations and builds the
  complete target frame before instruction bindings, the all-illegal gate or any
  earlier proof. No announced targets permits resolution; all announced targets
  becoming illegal prevents it. Illegal members cannot reappear through filters.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

- `mage.PermanentExileInstruction{Subject PermanentRef, Subjects PermanentSet}`
  requires exactly one non-nil subject field. `Effect() ResolvingEffect` returns

  ([]PermanentExileInstruction, bool)` reads complete native sequences/composites
  without callbacks or reference resolution. Unknown descendants, missing/typed-nil
  operands and result-bearing exile reject the complete tree. Returned slices
  are independent; declaration and group identity are retained.
- The live `Game.InspectSpellDestruction` query accepts singular native permanent
  target bindings and complete contextual permanent collections. It validates
  every declaration, filter and binding before target gates or earlier proofs.
  Missing, foreign and repeated declarations remain unknown. Native plural target
  and collection services preserve partial legality, exact visits and phasing.
- Exile alone cannot directly destroy a permanent. A nonempty exile prefix blocks
  later destruction proofs, even for the same watched visit. An empty or illegal
  selection permits later proofs. A supported suffix preserves an earlier proof;
  an unknown suffix rejects the complete tree. Inspection does not project later
  state, run replacements, use shields, make choices or advance RNG. Current
  layers remain the caller's responsibility.
- Resolving RON `Exile([Permanent(ref)], [])` and
  `Exile([EachPermanent(collection)], [])` use the descriptor for ordinary
  battlefield exile. RON retains spelling, arity, scopes and fresh per-factory
  bindings. Linked permanent exile, grouped producers, costs, delayed death
  graveyard exile and other zones retain their existing execution paths.
- No new zone-change or replacement system was added. Group execution reuses
  replacement processing before departures and the shared simultaneous event
  batch. Singular execution reuses the existing singular exile service. Clone,
  copy, casting/payment and target legality services are unchanged.

cards compile or that the full gameplay mapping is complete. Nested forms were

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

- `InspectPlayerCollection(PlayerSet) (PlayerCollectionPredicate, bool)` retains
  `EachPlayer`, the internal empty set, `OnePlayer(PlayerRef)` and
  `OpponentsOf(PlayerRef)`. References can be `You`, `ActivePlayer` or complete
  singular native player targets. Nil, typed-nil, saved and opaque references
  reject. The predicate copies selection metadata without calling callbacks.
- `PlayerCollectionPredicate.Select(*EffectContext) ([]uuid.UUID, bool)` reads
  current player presence with the same active-first order as execution. The
  resolving controller must be present. Targets require the exact declaration
  in a legal resolving frame. Missing/foreign/repeated/malformed frames are
  unknown. Empty bindings and absent players select nobody, including opponents.
  Player identity has no departure LKI. Results do not share mutable slices.
- `InspectDamageRecipientCollection` accepts player-only as well as mixed native
  damage recipients. Mixed permanent children must remain fully inspectable.
  Current visits, phasing, characteristics and permanent frame checks are reused.
  Spell inspection checks both frames before target gates and earlier proofs.
- Nonempty damage prefixes retain changed-state barriers, including zero damage.
  Supported suffixes preserve earlier destruction proofs. Unknown descendants
  and unbound players remain unknown even before an earlier proof or when all
  announced targets are illegal. Inspection runs no amounts, effects, shields,
  replacement callbacks, choices or RNG; it reads no predicted damage total.
- `ron.compileDamageHistoryPlayers` now reuses
  `compileDamageOutcomePlayers(Node, scope)
  (func(instanceBindings) mage.PlayerSet, error)` for nonhistory mixed player
  sets. This shares `AnyPlayer`, `Opponent` and `Other(player)` syntax checks and
  per-instance scoped references. Mixed `Player(player)` retains `OnePlayer`.
  `Opponent` remains relative to the resolving controller. Explicit active-player
  spelling is `TheActivePlayer`. No RON source spelling or record changed.
- Execution reuses `DealDamageEach`, `PlayerDamageRecipients`, `DamageRecipients`,
  actual post-replacement totals and native life gain. No new global result,
  replacement, payment or simultaneous-operation service was introduced.
  Recipient-dependent `DealDamageEachPlayer` trees remain a separate pure-query
  contract, including Typhoon. No Go fallback or partial registry was added.

### Exact contract, engine reuse and boundaries

- Added `Game.InspectTapStateChange(TapOperationKind, []PermanentVisit)
  (mayChange, known bool)`. Inputs are already selected, legal current visits.
  Nil games, invalid operations, absent or phased visits and stale incarnations
  return unknown. The full visit list validates before a result is returned;
  duplicate visits are harmless and empty groups cannot change state.
- Tapping already tapped visits and untapping already untapped visits cannot
  change state. A possible transition or nonempty optional tap-or-untap group
  reports possible change without predicting a choice or replacement. No
  callbacks, events, layers, bindings, RNG or counters change during inspection.
- Native spell instruction plans now retain `TapOperationKind` rather than a
  Boolean. `Game.InspectSpellDestruction` permits later destruction proofs only
  when the selected tap group cannot change state. One possibly changing visit,
  including an unwatched visit, retains the state barrier. Complete declaration
  validation, target frames, legality, current layers, phasing, copy controllers,
  earlier proofs and all-illegal gates retain their existing contracts.
- AST lowering reuses `compileTapInstructionPlan(Node, scope)` and
  `tapInstructionPlan.build(instanceBindings) mage.TapInstruction`. The compiler
  already preserves the exact per-instance operation and singular/group subject.
  New end-to-end tests establish its use by the changed-state query; no adapter
  rewrite, syntax expansion or card-name branch is needed. Supported resolving
  forms are `TapPermanent/1`, `UntapPermanent/1`, `TapEachPermanent/1`,
  `UntapEachPermanent/1` and `MayAction(TapOrUntapPermanent/1)`. Costs and result
  producers retain their separate adapters and are not admitted by this query.
- The shared `untapWithoutEvent` service previously removed a stun counter from
  an already untapped permanent through singular actions. Failing-first tests
  established this engine defect. It now checks tapped status first. This is
  required by CR 701.26b and 122.1d, and makes singular and collection no-change
  behavior agree. Tapped subjects still lose one stun counter instead of
  untapping; that changes state and therefore still blocks a later proof.
- Execution reuses existing tap/untap actions, simultaneous batches, replacement
  services, events, layer refresh and source-tapped durations. The pure query
  projects no later state, runs no replacement and uses no LKI. CR 608.2b/c and
  702.26b establish legal targets, ordered resolution and phasing. Riptide and
  Reset have explicit empty local rulings. Twiddle's WotC rulings retain its
  resolution-time choice. Equinox's complete WotC rulings retain certainty and
  direct-destruction requirements. No Scryfall note was treated as a WotC ruling.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

Added `Game.InspectDestructionStateChange([]PermanentVisit) (mayChange, known bool)`.
The caller establishes current layers and legal selected subjects. Every visit
must be a current unphased battlefield incarnation. Nil games, absent visits,
phased visits and stale incarnations return unknown; the complete list validates
even after a possible transition. Empty groups and groups of current
indestructible visits return false/true. Repeated visits are harmless. Every
other valid group returns true/true without predicting replacements.

The query follows the existing pre-proposal indestructibility guards in
`Game.DestroyPermanent` and `moveGraveyardBatch` (CR 701.8 and 702.12b). A known
no-move destination is insufficient: regeneration can tap, remove damage and
remove combat membership (CR 701.19), cancellation can consume a replacement,
and hand/exile destinations can move objects. These retain barriers with either
regeneration restriction. The query executes no callbacks, choices, replacement
rules, events, RNG, LKI reads, shield use, layer changes or binding writes.

`InspectSpellDestruction` and `OrderedDestructionPredicate.Certain` use this
shared service after a direct group fails to prove a watched graveyard move.
A group that cannot propose destruction permits a later proof. One possibly
changing member, including an unwatched member, preserves the barrier. Complete
tree/binding validation, target legality, all-illegal gates, earlier proofs,
current controllers, phasing and incarnation identity retain their contracts
(CR 608.2b/c, 702.26b). Execution and simultaneous replacement ordering are reused.
No hypothetical later state is projected.

Existing RON AST lowering is reused end-to-end:
`compileDirectDestructionPlan(Node, scope) (directDestructionPlan, error)` and
`directDestructionPlan.build(instanceBindings) mage.DirectDestructionInstruction`.
The four supported resolving forms remain `DestroyPermanent/1`,
`DestroyPermanentNoRegen/1`, `DestroyEachPermanent/1` and
`DestroyEachPermanentNoRegen/1`. The adapter already retains exact factory-local
references, simultaneous collections and regeneration restrictions; no rewrite,
new syntax, card-name branch or fallback is needed. RON integration tests prove
those declarations reach the changed engine contract. Cost and saved-result
forms remain separate contexts. No source defect or RON change was found, so
the vocabulary snapshot is unchanged. API and rules-contract docs describe only
this bounded contract.

### Established contract and implementation

`InspectPlayerHandSize(ResolutionValue) (PlayerHandSizePredicate, bool)` accepts
native `HandSizeOf` over You, ActivePlayer or a singular native player target.
It uses `InspectPlayerCollection(OnePlayer(ref))`; saved/loop references,
arithmetic, opaque operands and nil declarations remain unknown without
callbacks. `PlayerHandSizePredicate.Read(*EffectContext) (int, bool)` reads the
current selected hand without reference callbacks. Missing, foreign, duplicate,
nil-ID and incarnation-bearing target frames are unknown. Empty/absent players
supply zero. Zero predicates and invalid contexts are unknown. Players use no
permanent LKI. Predicates hold no game state and work independently with clones.

`Game.InspectSpellDestruction` accepts the native scalar in singular source
damage. It validates the exact declaration binding before legality gates or
proofs, without reading hand sizes. Unknown suffixes or missing bindings remain
unknown even with all-illegal targets. Damage alone supplies no direct
destruction proof (CR 120.5). A legal damage prefix retains the changed-state
barrier even with an empty hand. Illegal recipients can be skipped when another
target remains legal; earlier destruction proofs survive supported suffixes.
Inspection executes no damage, choices, replacements, prevention or RNG.

RON `compilePlayerRecipientDamage(Node, scope, damageSourceFactory)
(effectFactory, error)` now builds `SingularDamageInstruction.Effect` for the
singular `Player(ref)` branch. Existing `compileInstanceValue` lowers
`TheNumberOfCardsInPlayersHand/1` to `HandSizeOf`; `DealsDamage_ThatPlayer`
resolves to that exact factory-local player declaration. RON owns spelling,
arity, roles and scope. The shared engine owns native inspection and execution.
No card-name branch, fallback, alternate damage executor or global result slot
is added. Collection/loop-local recipient amounts retain separate contracts.
Resolution still reads current information (CR 608.2h) and uses shared damage,
target legality, prevention and copy/clone services (CR 608.2b/c).

### Exact contract, ownership and reuse

- `CounterInstruction{Subject StackObjectRef}.Effect() ResolvingEffect` reuses
  `Counter`; nil and typed-nil subjects return nil. Current callers stay intact.
- `InspectCounterInstructions(ResolvingEffect)
  ([]CounterInstruction, bool)` retains complete native spell counter trees,
  `Sequence` and `CompositeEffects`, exact operand identity and order. Unknown
  children, missing operands and ability counters reject without callbacks.
- `InspectSpellTarget(StackObjectRef) (SpellTargetPredicate, bool)` accepts
  singular native declarations with unrestricted/card-type predicates and
  complete Boolean type trees. `SpellTargetPredicate.Select(*Game,
  *StackObject) (uuid.UUID, bool)` reads the exact declared stack ID, recorded
  zone and current spell types. Nil/absent targets, departed spells and abilities
  are illegal. Recasting cannot restore a stack target. Missing/duplicate
  declarations and missing zone snapshots remain unknown; no source-ID fallback
  or LKI is used. Opaque descendants, malformed filter writes, colors/subtypes,
  mana restrictions and battlefield/contextual predicates remain unknown.
- `Game.InspectSpellDestruction` validates all these operands before target gates
  or proofs. Countering does not directly destroy a permanent. A legal counter
  prefix blocks later destruction proofs, including uncounterable spells. An
  illegal prefix permits later proofs when another target is legal. A supported
  suffix preserves an earlier proof; an unknown suffix rejects the whole tree.
  No outcome/trigger projection, replacement, choice, callback, frame write or
  RNG is used. Copies/clones retain exact declaration and target-frame identity.
- RON `CounterSpell(spellReference)` builds this native descriptor after existing
  arity, reference and scope validation. Other accepted execution references
  remain available even when the narrower pure query returns unknown. No card
  name branch, fallback registry, alternate counter executor or global result
  slot is introduced. Shared uncounterability, owner/graveyard movement, legality
  and payment services retain normal execution (CR 608.2b/c, 701.6a/b, 701.8a/b).

proof. A legal production prefix blocks later state proofs, even at zero. An
illegal player target is skipped when another target is legal. A supported
production suffix preserves earlier destruction proofs. Production alone cannot
directly destroy a permanent. Private mana-loss and mana-production plans share
one `manaSubject` field because their subject gates and state barriers agree.

### Exact contract, engine reuse and boundaries

RON retains `AddManaRepeated(fixedProduction,
ManaValueOfTheSacrificedPermanent)` and lowers it through
`ManaProductionInstruction{Subject: You, Color, Amount}.Effect()` in
`compileBoundRepeatedMana(Node, scope) ([]effectFactory, error)`.
`compileSavedManaAmount(Node, scope) (valueFactory, error)` adds nested
`Plus(left, right)` and `Twice(value)` amounts for fixed-type production. Leaves
are nonnegative Integer values or the exact scoped sacrifice value. Invalid
arity, kind, operand and unbound reads fail compilation. Existing counter-payment
and activated callers keep their behavior. RON owns spelling and lexical scope;
the engine owns native operands, payment capture and pure inspection.

`Game.InspectSpellDestruction(*StackObject, []PermanentVisit) (bool, bool)` now
accepts saved casting-sacrifice mana amounts and nested native addition and
multiplication. Private `castingManaReads(ResolutionValue)
([]*NumberBinding, bool)` retains exact saved identities without resolving values.
`validCastingManaReads(*StackObject, []spellPermanentInstruction) bool` requires
one mandatory native single-permanent additional sacrifice cost with mana-value
capture, the matching NumberBinding, and a present nonnegative captured value.
Use the current spell text definition after revisions. No text-continuation
marker or diagnostic name can replace the exact producer identity.

Optional, multiple, missing, foreign and incompatible producers remain unknown.
A resolution writer of that binding, before or after the read, rejects the full
tree. Native destruction/damage result writes and discard-member writes cannot
replace the paid result. Validate unknown children and producer provenance
before any earlier destruction proof or all-illegal-target gate. Inspection
runs no effect, value, filter, choice or replacement callback. Existing target
selection and conservative ordering remain: a supported production suffix keeps
an earlier proof; a legal prefix, including zero production, blocks later state
proofs. Mana production alone is known to supply no direct destruction proof.

Shared payment transactions, mana-value capture, owner destinations, replacement
ordering, production history, spell copies, text remapping and game clones remain
the execution services. CR 601.2h/i establishes payment before responses;
CR 118.11 retains payment after replacement; CR 202.3 establishes battlefield
mana value and zero X; CR 106.3/4 establishes spell production and pools;
CR 608.2b/c establishes resolution legality and order; CR 707.10 retains the
original paid objects for a spell copy. No new replacement or simultaneous batch
rule is introduced. Required-tap paid branches, chosen-color restricted mana,
forced activation/transfers and delayed production remain explicit separate
inspection contracts. No source defect is found; no RON or vocabulary edit.

### Contract, lowering and reuse boundary

Extend `mage.ManaProductionInstruction{Subject PlayerRef, Color core.Color,
Amount ResolutionValue}` with `Restriction core.ManaRestriction`.
`Color: core.AnyColor` means one of the five colors for the complete amount at
resolution and requires `Subject: You`. Concrete restricted production requires
`You` and a positive native fixed amount. Accept only native value restrictions
`core.CreatureSpellsOnly{}` and `core.ArtifactSpellsOnly{}`. Invalid combinations,
nil operands, typed-nil restrictions and unknown restriction types return nil.
Existing unrestricted explicit-player and fixed-type callers remain supported.

`InspectManaProductionInstructions(ResolvingEffect)
([]ManaProductionInstruction, bool)` retains chosen-color operands and native
restrictions from existing effects. Fixed restricted batches return components
in order with separate slice storage. The original native effect still owns
one production event. Inspection never reconstructs the batch as sequential
production. Unknown or malformed children reject the entire tree. Raw invalid
`AddMana(core.AnyColor, ...)` remains invalid; only the native choice effect
establishes a color choice.

RON `compileResolvingMana` lowers `AddMana(AnyManaColor)` and fixed-count
`AddManaRepeated(AnyManaColor, Integer(n))` through the declaration.
`compileRestrictedRepeatedMana` lowers
`AddManaRepeatedWithModifiers(AnyManaColor, amount,
CanOnlySpendOnSpells(IsCardtype(Creature|Artifact)))` through the same declaration.
`compileRestrictedFixedMana` retains its exact native fixed batch. RON keeps
spelling, arity, scope and per-factory bindings. No new syntax, source correction
or vocabulary refresh is required. Native dynamic amounts retain execution;
retention alone does not make an opaque amount queryable.

The existing `Game.InspectSpellDestruction` consumer now recognizes these
components through its shared inspector. No parallel query or execution path
is added. It checks native scalar arithmetic and exact saved casting producers
before target gates or an earlier proof. Missing, foreign, negative,
incompatible or overwritten paid bindings stay unknown. A legal production
prefix blocks a later proof, including zero production. A supported suffix
preserves an earlier proof. Production alone supplies no destruction proof.
Queries make no choices and run no amount, player, restriction, effect or
replacement callback. They do not change pools, RNG, history, stack or bindings.

CR 106.1a/b distinguishes the five colors from the six mana types. CR 106.3/4
retains source identity and pools; CR 106.6/6a retains restrictions on production
and replacement amounts. Existing CR 601.2h/i payment, CR 118.11 replacement,
CR 202.3 mana-value, CR 608.2b/c legality/order and CR 707.10 copying contracts
remain unchanged. Shared execution keeps decisions, payment rollback, solver
metadata, source identity, event grouping, replacement order, production history,
text remapping and clone isolation. No new replacement or simultaneous rule is
introduced. There are no Go-card fallbacks, card-name branches, declaration
panics, global result slots or production registry changes.

SearchLibrary([FindAGenericCard, PutFoundCardsIntoHand, Shuffle])

### Exact supported contract and reuse boundary

`LibraryProcedureInstruction{Chooser, Library PlayerRef; Count int; Reorder,
OptionalShuffle bool}.Effect() ResolvingEffect` retains one fixed private look
with optional top ordering, or one optional shuffle. Missing or typed-nil
operands, negative counts, and shuffle declarations with ordering or a nonzero
count return nil. Zero-card looks remain valid. No mutable choice is retained.
`InspectLibraryProcedureInstruction(ResolvingEffect)
(LibraryProcedureInstruction, bool)` reads the existing native effects without
execution. Nil, typed nil, dynamic counts and composite effects are rejected.

RON lowers these existing forms in resolving bodies through the declaration:

- `LookAtTheTopNumberCardsOfPlayersLibrary(player, Integer(n), [operation])`,
  with nonnegative n and exactly one bare
  `PutTheRemainingCardsOnTopOfLibraryInAnyOrder` or
  `LeaveRemainingCardsOnTopOfLibraryInSameOrder`.
- `MayHavePlayerAction(player, Shuffle)`, with a bare Shuffle symbol.

The controller is the viewer/order chooser or optional-shuffle chooser; the
explicit player supplies the library. Existing arity, scope, ordering and
context checks remain in RON. Dynamic counts retain existing execution and
remain unknown to this pure query. Existing engine callers remain supported.

Pure spell inspection accepts You, ActivePlayer and exact singular native
player targets for both operands. Foreign and duplicate declarations and opaque
references reject before the all-illegal gate or an earlier proof. Native
player legality is checked without LKI. Copies use their own controller and
exact declarations; clone state is independent. If either operand is illegal,
the procedure cannot run, and another legal target can permit a later proof.
A legal prefix blocks later destruction proofs even for a zero-card look or
optional shuffle; no hidden library state or choice outcome is projected.
Supported suffixes preserve earlier proofs; unknown suffixes reject the complete
tree, including before all-illegal gates. No query reads a library, reveals or
orders cards, makes choices, shuffles, uses RNG, or changes zones or frames.

Execution reuses `LookAtLibraryTop`, `LookAtLibraryTopNumber`,
`MayShuffleLibrary`, private look history, player choices and shared library
services. Target validation reuses `InspectPlayerTarget` and
`InspectPlayerCollection` with exact declarations and the legal resolving frame.
No parallel execution subsystem, card-name branch, fallback or registry is added.
This slice introduces no new permanent identity, phasing, payment rollback,
replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation service.

### Exact contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

`PTAdjustment{Power, Toughness int}` retains one fixed signed layer 7c pair.
`TemporaryPTInstruction{Subject PermanentRef, Subjects PermanentSet,
Adjustments []PTAdjustment}.Effect() ResolvingEffect` requires exactly one
non-nil subject form and at least one adjustment. Invalid declarations return
nil. Zero and negative changes are valid. The constructor copies the list and
builds one native wrapper around the existing `untilEffect` installation with
end-of-turn duration. All adjustments share that installation.
`InspectTemporaryPTInstruction(ResolvingEffect) (TemporaryPTInstruction, bool)`
returns a copied list without callbacks or subject selection. Nil/typed-nil
native effects, raw Until declarations and composite effects are unknown to
this single-instruction inspector. The complete spell query handles sequences.

RON lowers these shapes in instant and sorcery resolving bodies:

- `CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil(permanent, [AdjustPT(power, toughness), ...],
  UntilEndOfTurn)` with fixed integer pairs and a nonempty list.
- `CreateEachPermanentLayerEffectUntil(filter, [AdjustPT(power, toughness), ...],
  UntilEndOfTurn)` with the existing complete collection filter contract.

RON keeps spelling, arity, scope and duration validation. Mage keeps exact target
identity/legality, collection selection, fixed membership, layer installation,
cloning and cleanup. Permanent ability callers retain their previous lowering.
Other durations, dynamic values and mixed modifications keep existing execution
and require separate native inspection contracts. Blood Lust's fixed child can
retain a declaration, but its unsupported conditional parent remains unknown.

The complete native spell query validates exact singular permanent target
bindings or supported contextual collections before all-illegal gates and prior
proofs. Foreign/duplicate declarations and opaque subjects reject. Legal nonempty
P/T prefixes block later destruction proofs, including zero changes. Empty or
illegal subjects permit later proofs when another target remains legal.
Supported suffixes preserve earlier proofs; unknown suffixes reject the full
tree, including before an all-illegal gate. Inspection never installs layers,
changes characteristics, calls filter callbacks or predicts state-based actions.
P/T changes alone do not directly destroy permanents.

Execution reuses layer 7c, `ModifyPT`, `ModifyEachPT`, `untilEffect`, exact visit
capture, resolution-time collection membership, cloning and end-of-turn cleanup.
There is no parallel execution system, card-name branch, fallback or registry.
No new LKI, payment, replacement-ordering or simultaneous-operation rule is
introduced. Public API and rules-contract docs describe only this capability.

### Contract, ownership and dependencies

Engine API:

- `TemporaryKeywordInstruction{Subject PermanentRef, Subjects PermanentSet,
  Keywords []core.Attr}.Effect() ResolvingEffect`.
- `InspectTemporaryKeywordInstruction(ResolvingEffect)
  (TemporaryKeywordInstruction, bool)`.

Exactly one non-nil subject form and a nonempty keyword list are required.
Invalid values, rule permissions, type attributes and prepared state return nil.
The constructor and inspector copy the list. Nil and raw Until declarations do
not acquire native inspection support. Composite trees are traversed separately.

RON retains keyword-only AddAbility lists, including multiple operations and
multiple keywords, in CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil and
CreateEachPermanentLayerEffectUntil with bare UntilEndOfTurn in instant and
sorcery bodies. Permanent abilities retain their previous lowering. Protection,
rampage, mixed modifications and other durations keep their execution and need
separate native inspection contracts. No syntax or source data changes.

Execution uses GrantKeywordModification, GrantEachKeyword, untilEffect, layer 6,
exact visit capture, fixed resolution-time collection membership, cloning,
phasing and end-of-turn cleanup. Definition metadata, AI properties and saved
source-read declarations are inherited from untilEffect. RON owns syntax and
instance bindings; mage owns execution and pure native inspection. There is no
parallel layer system, callback analysis, card-name branch, fallback or partial
production registry. Existing callers and Go card definitions are preserved.
No DSL removal gate is met, so no DSL function is removed.

The shared spell query now marks both retained P/T and keyword instructions as
temporary layers. It validates complete target declarations and contextual
collections before all-illegal gates or earlier destruction proofs. A legal
nonempty keyword prefix blocks later proofs, even when the grant is redundant.
Empty or illegal subjects permit later proofs. Supported suffixes preserve
earlier proofs; unknown suffixes keep the complete tree unknown. Queries do not
install layers, run callbacks or triggers, change state, or predict later layers.
Keyword grants do not directly destroy permanents. No new LKI, payment,
replacement-ordering or simultaneous-operation rule is introduced.

CR 608.2b/c, 611.2a/c and 613.1f establish legality, order, duration, fixed
membership and the ability layer. Read all local rulings for Jump, Rapid Fire,
Berserk, Howl from Beyond, Blood Lust and Equinox. Jump's WotC ruling requires
flying before blockers to provide evasion; it does not undo an existing block.
Rapid Fire's WotC ruling limits casting to before the first declare-blockers
step. Berserk's WotC ruling retains delayed destruction if the recipient stops
being a creature. Blood Lust has a WotC ruling about its fixed toughness change.
Howl has an explicit empty array. Equinox's seven WotC rulings require certain
direct destruction at resolution. No Scryfall notes are involved.
`go run ./cmd/fetchset -check -card` passes for Jump, Rapid Fire, Berserk, Howl
from Beyond and Equinox. No source defect or fetch failure was found.

### Exact shape, dependencies and engine boundary

New API:

- `PTValueAdjustment{Power, Toughness ResolutionValue}`.
- `TemporaryPTValueInstruction{Subject PermanentRef, Adjustments
  []PTValueAdjustment}.Effect() ResolvingEffect`.
- `InspectTemporaryPTValueInstruction(ResolvingEffect)
  (TemporaryPTValueInstruction, bool)`.

The constructor requires one non-nil subject and at least one pair of non-nil
values, copies the list and delegates to ModifyPT and one untilEffect through
EndOfTurn. Typed-nil operands return nil. Inspection returns a copied list;
raw Until, nil and composite trees are not this declaration. Complete sequences
are traversed by the existing shared spell query.

RON retains singular CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil with bare UntilEndOfTurn
in instant/sorcery bodies when all modifications are AdjustPT or AdjustPTX.
Fixed-only lists keep their existing native declaration. AdjustPTX coordinates
remain PlusX, MinusX, Zero or Integer(signed literal). Values remain Integer,
announced ValueX, ManaValueOfPermanent, PowerOfPermanent,
ToughnessOfPermanent and recursive Minus. ActionPermanent is local to its
modified subject. Per-instance typed bindings and existing lexical checks stay
in ron. The old private compileTemporaryPTX helper has no remaining callers;
a repository search confirmed its single former caller before the rename to
compileTemporaryPTAdjustment. No public composable DSL service is removed.

native target current mana values and LKI-capable target power/toughness/mana
operands, and complete subtraction/multiplication trees. It verifies every
value target belongs to the spell's exact native declarations before target
gates or earlier destruction proofs. It does not read those values or LKI,
resolve references, call callbacks or predict characteristics. Unknown value
children invalidate the whole tree even with all targets illegal. A legal
layer prefix blocks later proofs, including zero amounts. Illegal subjects
permit later proofs; supported suffixes preserve earlier proofs. Toughness
reduction does not prove direct destruction.

Execution captures all values before any adjustment applies and saves exact
subject visits. Resolution-time characteristics and announced X become fixed
amounts. Existing layer 7c, definition reads, AI properties, clone/copy frames,
phasing, returned-object identity and cleanup services are reused. Existing

execution retain their previous adapters. Conditional and mixed parents remain

RON spell-body CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil accepts the complete mixed list of keyword AddAbility grants

keywords return nil. Its inspector returns (TemporaryMixedLayerInstruction, bool), copying both lists

prior execution adapters and separate native inspection gates.

CreateFutureTrigger(AtTheBeginningOfTheNextEndStep, ActionList(actions)) lowers to
NextEndStepInstruction{Body ResolvingEffect}.Effect() ResolvingEffect.
InspectNextEndStepInstruction(ResolvingEffect) (NextEndStepInstruction, bool) retains the complete body
without scheduling it. Missing/typed-nil bodies reject. Repeat, cleanup expiry, other steps, new targets,
modes and intervening-if options remain outside the native declaration. Existing callers remain supported.

Native spell inspection validates complete delayed trees of singular target destruction, sequences and
native permanent branches, including nested and alternative paths. All conditions, values and destruction
subjects must use the inspected spell's exact native declarations. Unknown children or filters reject before
legality and earlier proofs, including an unchosen branch or all-illegal targets. AttackedThisTurn now

domain gates stay separate. Inspection evaluates no condition or value and creates no layer or trigger.

Mixed execution shares one untilEffect operation with separate layer 6 and 7c entries. All amounts are saved
before installation. Mixed prefixes block later state proofs, while supported suffixes preserve earlier
proofs. A supported delayed body cannot prove immediate destruction, and scheduling it cannot change a later
direct proof. Future destruction uses the shared captured frame, exact visit and resolving controller; it

regeneration, replacement ordering and cleanup apply. No payment or simultaneous-operation contract changes.

### Contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

`CombatSourcePreventionInstruction{Subject PermanentRef}.Effect() ResolvingEffect`
builds the shared singular combat-source prevention installation until end of
turn. Missing and typed-nil sources return nil.
`InspectCombatSourcePreventionInstruction(ResolvingEffect)
(CombatSourcePreventionInstruction, bool)` reads the exact declaration without
resolving references or installing shields. Existing PreventCombatDamageByThisTurn
callers remain compatible. Source sets, other durations, recipient unions and
noncombat prevention have separate contracts and reject this inspector.

RON CreatePreventDamageUntil(CombatDamageWouldBeDealtByCreature(ref),
[PreventThatDamage], UntilEndOfTurn) lowers through this declaration, preserving
current reference scopes in supported resolving contexts. RON owns spelling,
arity, operation, duration and binding validation. The engine owns the retained
declaration, execution and native query. No parallel damage service is added.

Game.InspectSpellDestruction validates the complete tree and exact native
singular target declaration before legality gates or earlier proofs. Foreign,
opaque and duplicate declarations reject. An opaque suffix cannot hide behind
an earlier proof or an illegal target. Prevention alone is known without a
direct-destruction proof. A legal prevention prefix conservatively blocks later
state proofs. An illegal source prefix permits an independent later proof; a
supported suffix preserves an earlier proof. Inspection performs no damage,
choice, callback, RNG operation, layer installation or replacement installation.

Execution shares combatSourcePreventionInstallation and its replacement service.
The source visit is captured at resolution. Repeated combat damage to players
and permanents is prevented; unrelated and noncombat damage is permitted.
Prevention persists across combats, phase cycles, control and creature-type
changes, and expires at actual cleanup. It does not follow a returned object.
Clones retain independent replacement state; spell copies retain their own frames.
Existing replacement ordering, unpreventable damage and legality apply. No new
payment, rollback, LKI or simultaneous-operation semantics are introduced.
CR 400.7, 608.2b, 611.2a, 615.1–4, 615.6 and 615.12 establish the contract.
There are no source-data corrections. RON sources and vocabulary are unchanged.

### Exact supported signatures, boundaries and rules

`TurnAttackRuleInstruction{Filter PermanentFilter, Player PlayerRef, Require bool}`
exposes `Effect() ResolvingEffect`. A requirement must supply a player; a
restriction must not supply one. Invalid player combinations return nil.
The filter's zero value preserves its existing execution meaning, all permanents.
`InspectTurnAttackRuleInstruction(ResolvingEffect)
(TurnAttackRuleInstruction, bool)` reads one structurally complete declaration
without calling operands, selecting creatures or installing a rule.
Singular rules and other durations remain separate contracts.

RON retains these existing exact forms in resolving action lists:

- `CreateEachPermanentRuleEffectUntil(filter, [CantAttack], UntilEndOfTurn)`:
  supported source-independent static filters, without controller/source exclusion.
- `CreateEachPermanentRuleEffectUntil(And([filter, ...,
  ControlledByPlayer(TheActivePlayer)]), [MustAttack], UntilEndOfTurn)`:
  exactly one active-player selector and one or more supported filters.

RON owns spelling, arity, duration and selector validation. Both lower through
the native instruction. No source record, vocabulary snapshot or Go card
changes. Existing public attack-rule constructors and callers remain compatible.

Complete spell inspection accepts native filter metadata and You or ActivePlayer
for a requirement. It rejects opaque or nested opaque filters, saved players,
foreign player targets and unknown children before the all-illegal gate or an
earlier destruction proof. It does not evaluate even a known filter or player.
A rule-only body is known and has no direct-destruction proof. A rule prefix is
a conservative barrier before later destruction, even with no current members;
a complete supported suffix preserves an earlier proof. No future member set,
combat outcome or delayed-body execution is predicted.

Execution uses the existing `turnAttackRuleEffect`, live matching, saved player,
source-independent duration, attack legality/payment and effect-manager cloning.
CR 508.1c/d, 608.2b/c/h, 611.2a/c and 514.2 establish the contract. The complete
local rulings were read for Festival, Siren's Call, Cleansing and Equinox, and
all four `fetchset -check -card` commands pass. Festival and Cleansing have
explicit empty ruling arrays. Siren's four WotC rulings preserve tapped/unable
creature destruction, haste and first-combat cast timing. Equinox's seven WotC
rulings distinguish direct certain destruction from damage, indirect destruction,
randomness and optional choices. There are no Scryfall notes in these entries.
No source defect or environmental failure was found. No new LKI, replacement,
simultaneous-operation, payment or rollback mechanism is needed.
