### Exact contract, lowering and engine reuse

`SavedPlayerInstruction{Subject PlayerRef, Binding *PlayerBinding,
Body ResolvingEffect}.Effect() ResolvingEffect` builds the existing ordered
SnapshotPlayer/Sequence mechanics. Missing or typed nil operands and unnamed
bindings return nil. Definition validation retains exact producer dominance.
`InspectSavedPlayerInstruction(ResolvingEffect) (SavedPlayerInstruction, bool)`
reads the exact two-child snapshot/body shape without reading players or bindings.
It does not introduce a new engine lexical lifetime: the existing resolution
frame owns values, and each delayed schedule captures that frame separately.

RON PlayerActions(player, actions) now lowers through this declaration with a
fresh binding for every factory instance. The compiler retains spelling, arity,
lexical ActionPlayer scope and existing invalid-declaration diagnostics.

Complete pure spell inspection accepts You or ActivePlayer followed only by
nonempty sequences of next-end-step schedules. Each schedule must contain a
complete nonempty direct-destruction tree over native contextual collections.
Saved player reads must name the exact local binding. Singular destruction,
target-dependent collections, foreign bindings, nested saved scopes, other
schedules and unknown children remain unknown in this context. These boundaries
are specific to pure inspection; existing execution shapes remain available.

The exact Siren's Call shape is PlayerActions(TheActivePlayer,
[CreateFutureTrigger(AtTheBeginningOfTheNextEndStep,
ActionList([DestroyEachPermanent(And([IsNonCreatureType(Wall),
IsCardtype(Creature), ControlledByPlayer(ActionPlayer), DidntAttackThisTurn,
ExceptFor(NotControlledSinceBeginningOfTurn)]))]))]).
Native collection differences retain both complete operands. DidntAttackThisTurn
and ControlledSinceCurrentTurnStart now retain native filter metadata. Current
visits, attack history and continuous current-turn control preserve existing
semantics. A phase cycle retains history; a return starts a new visit.

Every descendant is validated before all-illegal target gates or an earlier
proof. Inspection does not resolve the snapshot, select future members, schedule
triggers, call unknown operands, consume RNG or change state. A validated
schedule supplies no immediate destruction proof and permits later direct proofs.
The live attack requirement remains a separate conservative prefix barrier.

Execution reuses SnapshotPlayer, Sequence, FromPlayer, AtNext/EachEndStep,
capturedDelayedBody, contextual collections, shared turn history and the
simultaneous destruction/replacement/regeneration pipeline. There is no parallel
player, duration, zone or replacement system. CR 603.7a-d, 608.2b/c/h, 701.8 and
702.26b/d establish timing, saved context, destruction and phasing. No new LKI,
payment, rollback or replacement ordering service is required.

All complete local ruling files for Siren's Call, Cleansing and Equinox were
read; all three fetchset -check -card commands passed. Siren's Call has four

Cleansing has an explicit empty array. Equinox has seven WotC rulings separating
certain direct destruction from random, optional, indirect and damage outcomes.
There are no Scryfall notes in these three files. No source defect or environment
failure was found. No RON source changed, so no vocabulary refresh was needed.

### Contract, signatures and reuse boundary

`ObjectColorInstruction{Subject *SpellOrPermanentTargetBinding, Color core.Color}`
provides `Effect() ResolvingEffect`; invalid native declarations return nil.
`InspectObjectColorInstruction(ResolvingEffect) (ObjectColorInstruction, bool)`
retains the exact target and fixed actual color. Existing SetObjectColor callers
keep their execution and definition-validation behavior.

`InspectObjectTarget(*SpellOrPermanentTargetBinding) (ObjectTargetPredicate, bool)`
reads a complete singular native union declaration. Its
`Select(*Game, *StackObject) (ObjectTargetSelection, bool)` returns separate
`Spell uuid.UUID` and `Permanent PermanentVisit` fields. `Empty() bool` reports
an illegal target. Missing snapshots, repeated/foreign declarations, wrong counts
and inconsistent stack incarnations are unknown. Departed, phased, protected or
shrouded targets are known and illegal when native legality can be established.
Opaque protection/global restrictions remain unknown. Stack targets use exact
stack IDs, with no physical-card fallback or LKI. A later cast cannot replace a
departed stack object.

RON retains its exact two-branch fixed-color Targeted_Modal shape and declaration
errors, but now lowers through ObjectColorInstruction.Effect. Each factory keeps
its own binding. Branch order is free; both branches require the same one actual
color, one target and one action. General modal effects, extra actions, filters,
other color forms and contexts keep their existing diagnostics.

Pure spell destruction inspection validates the complete tree and all bindings
before legality gates or proofs. A color action cannot prove destruction. A
legal color prefix blocks later proofs; an illegal prefix permits an independent
later destruction if another target remains legal. A complete supported suffix
preserves an earlier proof. Opaque suffixes reject even with all-illegal targets.
No inspection executes callbacks, changes colors or installs effects.

Execution reuses union target frames, ChangeObjectColor, layer 5, timestamps,
exact visits, stack-to-permanent color carry, phasing and clone services. Native
permanent inspection supplies shared source/protection/global legality checks.
No parallel payment, zone, replacement, LKI or simultaneous-operation mechanism
was added. CR 105.3, 112.4, 400.7a, 608.2b/c, 611.2a/c, 613.1e and 702.26b/d
supply the rules contract. API and rules-contract docs describe only this slice.

### Exact contract and implementation

`RandomDiscardInstruction{Subject PlayerRef, Amount ResolutionValue}.Effect()
returns `ResolvingEffect`; missing or typed-nil operands return nil.
`InspectRandomDiscardInstructions(ResolvingEffect)
([]RandomDiscardInstruction, bool)` retains complete native primitives,
sequences and composites. Unknown or incomplete children reject the whole tree.
The returned instruction list does not share effect storage. It does not resolve
players, read amounts, consume RNG, request choices or move cards.

`compileRandomDiscard` lowers existing `DiscardACardAtRandom` and
`DiscardNumberCardsAtRandom(value)` contexts through the declaration. Existing
fixed, X, dynamic, activated, triggered and delayed execution remains compatible.
No new RON signature, lexical binding or global state was introduced.
`Game.InspectSpellDestruction` accepts fixed/X amounts and native player operands.
Saved or opaque operands remain unknown. The query validates the full tree and
exact target declarations before all-illegal gates or earlier proofs. A legal
random-discard prefix blocks later destruction proofs even with an empty hand,
zero or negative native amounts. An illegal discard target does not block a
later proof when another target is legal. A supported suffix preserves earlier
proofs. Inspection does not simulate replacement choices or discard triggers.

Execution reuses DiscardAtRandom, distinct random selection, discardActionsTogether,
shared zone replacements, discard events, spell copying and game cloning.
Current hands are read at resolution. Selection precedes all moves; all moves
precede discard events. Short hands discard as much as possible. No new LKI,
phasing, rollback or replacement ordering service is needed. CR 608.2b/c, 609.3,
701.9 and 616.1 establish the contract. API and rules-contract documentation
records this bounded behavior; Equinox's broader adapter remains unsupported.

### Contract, dependencies and reuse

`ManaPaymentInstruction{Player PlayerRef, Cost core.ManaCost,
Amount ResolutionValue, Paid, Unpaid ResolvingEffect}.Effect() ResolvingEffect`
retains an optional payment. Amount is required only for X. At least one branch
is required; a nil branch has no action. Missing or typed-nil operands, negative
cost fields, malformed hybrid symbols and inconsistent X fields return nil.
`InspectManaPaymentInstruction(ResolvingEffect) (ManaPaymentInstruction, bool)`
retains fixed and X native declarations without reading amounts, players or
choices. Construction and inspection copy hybrid-cost storage. Required,
repeated, alternative and non-mana payment inspection remains separate.

`compileResolutionPayment` lowers existing MayCost/PlayerMayCost PayMana and
PayManaX with adjacent If/Unless and CostWasPaid/CostWasntPaid through this
service. Fixed mana is parsed at declaration time. Existing syntax, dynamic
resolution operands, binding scopes and diagnostics remain compatible.
The compiler owns RON spelling; the engine owns payment and branch behavior.

Execution reuses IfPaid, UnlessPaid, PayOrElse and resolutionManaPayment.
The shared transaction retains mana abilities, affordability, rechecks, rollback,
zero-payment acceptance and separate operation results. Both fixed and X
two-branch execution is validated with synthetic cards. Source reads and delayed
frame capture keep their existing implementations. No global result slot, new
replacement ordering, LKI store, cost system or card-name branch was added.

`Game.InspectSpellDestruction` now accepts the controller of a native singular
spell target, fixed/X amounts, and complete branches containing counters for
that exact declaration. A branch can save the same controller with spell LKI
and tap native collections without target reads or clear that saved player's
unspent mana. Foreign member bindings and other unknown children reject the
complete tree. HasManaAbility now retains a native collection predicate and
shares its current-ability classifier with execution. No payment or output
condition is evaluated to classify the ability.

All branches validate before target legality gates or earlier proofs. Optional
countering supplies no direct destruction proof. A legal optional-payment
prefix blocks later proofs even for zero costs; an illegal payer target skips
the payment when another target is legal. Supported suffixes preserve earlier
destruction proofs. Inspection makes no offers, reads no payment amount,
activates no mana abilities and changes no stack, taps, mana, RNG or zones.
The Equinox adapter remains unsupported.

CR 118.12/118.12a and 608.2b/c/g/h establish the payment, target, order, mana
ability and LKI contracts. Both local rulings files were read completely through
the exact-name index. Force Spike has one WotC ruling; Power Sink has three.
Neither has Scryfall notes. `fetchset -check -card` passed for both names.
No source-data defect or environment failure was found. RON and the vocabulary
snapshot are unchanged.

### Contract, signatures and reuse boundary

`mage.NextUntapInstruction{Subject PermanentRef, Subjects PermanentSet, Count int}`
exposes `Effect() ResolvingEffect`. Exactly one subject is required. Singular
counts are nonnegative; collections require count one. Invalid shapes return
nil. `InspectNextUntapInstruction(Effect) (NextUntapInstruction, bool)` reads the
native one-step, counted and collection declarations without selecting subjects
or installing restrictions. Player-captured restrictions remain separate.

RON `compileNextUntaps(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` retains all three
existing signatures: `PermanentDoesntUntapDuringControllersNextUntap(ref)`,
`PermanentDoesntUntapDuringControllersNextNumberUntaps(ref, Integer(n))`, and
`EachPermanentDoesntUntapDuringControllersNextUntap(collection)`. Resolving
spells, activated and triggered bodies keep their existing lexical contexts.
Factories build fresh typed target bindings. Costs and entry operations do not
gain these declarations. Source capture and delayed-body services are retained.

`Game.InspectSpellDestruction` accepts exact native singular targets and complete
contextual collections. It validates every child and binding before legality
gates and earlier proofs. Positive-count nonempty prefixes conservatively block
later destruction proofs. Zero-count, empty or illegal prefixes permit them.
Supported suffixes preserve earlier proofs. Foreign bindings, opaque predicates,
nil declarations and unknown children reject the whole tree, including after an
earlier proof and with all targets illegal. Queries make no callbacks, choices,
RNG changes, taps, stack changes or untap restrictions.

Execution reuses `SkipNextUntap`, `SkipNextUntaps`, `SkipNextUntapEach`, exact visit
capture, current-controller tracking, step consumption and departure cleanup.
CR 502.3, 608.2b/c, 611.2, 400.7 and 702.26 establish the rules boundary. A phase
cycle preserves the visit but removes combat membership. No LKI store, payment
transaction, replacement order, simultaneous-operation or clone service changed.
Existing callers, Go definitions and DSL exports remain; removal gates are unmet.
RON source and vocabulary are unchanged.

by Wheel of Fortune (six records), Contract from Below (six), Knowledge Vault
(one) and Nicol Bolas (one): four unique names and fourteen records. Complete
records, including nested forms and all reprints, were read before edits.

player selection and focused integration tests. Existing execution already
supports these cards. Estimated new compilation/gameplay acceptance: zero.
Estimated complete native spell-tree gain: Wheel alone, one name / six records.
Contract retains a separate ante instruction; Vault retains required sacrifice
and linked-exile transport; Nicol's discard is inside a damage trigger. These
are not additional complete spell-tree unlocks. The shared declaration also
removes a remaining hand-refresh prerequisite for later Equinox inspection.

Candidate #1 meets the selection rule, so no lower-ranked alternative was
selected or expanded into a second slice. Distributed damage and library
recycling remain separate work. Their first-error counts are not unlock claims.

rulings arrays. Vault has three WotC rulings about resolution payment, source
control and hidden exile; Nicol has one WotC ruling that includes noncombat
damage. There are no Scryfall notes for these cards. Targeted vocabulary reads
confirmed DiscardHand symbol/0 (14 occurrences), EachPlayerAction tuple/2 and
PlayerAction tuple/2. No source defect or fetch failure was found. RON and the
vocabulary snapshot are unchanged.

### Signatures, engine contract and reuse

`mage.WholeHandDiscardInstruction{Subject PlayerRef, Subjects PlayerSet}` exposes
`Effect() ResolvingEffect`. Exactly one non-nil operand is required; missing,
typed-nil or conflicting operands return nil. Singular execution uses
`DiscardEntireHand`, plural execution uses `DiscardEach`.
`InspectWholeHandDiscardInstruction(ResolvingEffect)
(WholeHandDiscardInstruction, bool)` reads one exact native leaf. It invokes no
operand callbacks. Filtered discards, composite parents, result bindings and
malformed result options remain outside this declaration contract.

`ron.compileHandPlayerAction` lowers symbolic DiscardHand for implicit, explicit
and saved player contexts. `ron.compileEachPlayerAction` lowers
EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer, DiscardHand). Existing resolving spell, activation,
trigger and delayed contexts retain their typed per-instance bindings. Tuple
spellings, unbound targets/events and leaked loop references still reject.
No cost, entry or replacement-operation syntax was added.

The adapter change exposed one engine prerequisite: DiscardEntireHand formerly
moved cards through separate actions, whereas the former RON hand-filter adapter
used one batch. DiscardEntireHand now uses `Game.discardHandsTogether` for its
one selected player. Existing count results remain valid. Both shapes prepare
all replacements and destination orders before moves and send discard events
only after the batch. Replacement rechecks, prevention, hidden destinations,
actual counts and graveyard/library ordering use the existing services.
The singular effect now supplies its source-controller read to waiting delayed
source inspection. Plural source tracking already exists and is regression-tested.
CR 701.9a/c, 101.4, 608.2b/c/e and 616.1 establish this contract.

Pure `Game.InspectSpellDestruction` reuses OnePlayer, InspectPlayerCollection,
exact legal target frames and the existing player-action barrier. It validates
all children and bindings before all-illegal gates and earlier proofs. A prefix
with selected players blocks later destruction proofs, without reading hands.
Empty legal collections permit proofs. Supported suffixes preserve earlier
proofs. Unknown players, foreign bindings, unknown siblings and result-bearing
forms remain unknown without callbacks, choices, RNG or state changes.
No new mutable game state, LKI service, clone map or payment path was introduced.
No Go card, generator, registry or DSL function was removed; removal gates are
still unmet. Existing callers and filtered hand operations remain supported.

## 2026-10-18 — NATIVE-EQUAL-DIVISION-DAMAGE

### Selection, dependency evidence and scope

Selected the dependency-ready equal-division part of the previous ledger's
first candidate. Complete RON records, nested forms and vocabulary signatures
were inspected. Reprints count once in this comparison:

| Candidate | Distinct cards | Estimated complete native trees / new loader accepts | Other dependencies and downstream value | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native equal division at resolution, selected | Fireball; Dwarven Catapult | 2 names / 7 records; 0 accepts | Native plural damage-target inspection is missing; existing division, X, target surcharge and damage services are reusable. Enables two more complete instruction trees for the future Equinox contract. | Small declaration, target query, compiler lowering and contract/gameplay tests |
| Native allocation at announcement | Pyrotechnics | 1 name / 1 record; 0 accepts | Must retain locked shares and target positions, distinct from resolution division. Shares the plural-target prerequisite but requires its own allocation query contract. | Medium |
| Native hand/graveyard shuffling | Timetwister; Winds of Change | 2 names / 6 records; 0 accepts | Timetwister's fixed draws are already native; Winds needs independent per-player shuffled-count receipts. Enables complete shuffle/draw trees. | Larger receipt and shuffle declarations, purity/RNG and gameplay tests |

The selected slice has multi-card value at lower effort. Pyrotechnics was read
and checked to establish the reuse boundary; its announcement allocation is not
part of this slice. No excluded-card capability was considered. Baseline build
and fresh RON short tests passed. Baseline loader: 2,438 compiled / 7 rejected
records; collection rejection was distinct from a build/test failure.
Local rulings checks passed for Fireball, Dwarven Catapult and Pyrotechnics.
Their complete local files contain WotC rulings and no Scryfall notes.
No source defect was found. No RON data or vocabulary snapshot was changed.

### Established declarations and engine contract

`EvenDamageInstruction{Source DamageSourceRef, Recipients DamageRecipientSet,
Total ResolutionValue}.Effect() ResolvingEffect` rejects missing/typed-nil
operands and reuses `DealDamageEvenlyToRecipients`.
`InspectEvenDamageInstructions(ResolvingEffect)
([]EvenDamageInstruction, bool)` reads exact leaves and complete sequence or
composite trees without callbacks. Result-bearing, malformed and unknown trees
reject. Announcement allocations remain separate. Inspection returns fresh lists.

RON lowers `SpellDealsDamageDividedAmongRecipientsRoundedDown(ThisSpell,
total, recipients)` in its existing ordinary resolving-spell contexts:
`Ref_AnyTargets` from one AnyNumberOfAnyTargets group, or a supported
EachPermanent collection, including creatures controlled by a target player.
The adapter retains existing arity, scope, source and value checks and fresh
per-instance bindings. Deferred/replacement, activated and triggered contexts,
unbound references and malformed declarations remain errors.

`InspectDamageTargets(*DamageTargetsBinding) (DamageTargetsPredicate, bool)`
and `DamageTargetsPredicate.Select(*Game, *StackObject)
([]DamageTargetSelection, bool)` provide the missing shared native group query.
Fixed/optional DamageAnyTarget groups retain declaration identity, unique IDs,
recorded zones and permanent visits. Shared permanent target inspection checks
current types, protection, shroud, phasing and source characteristics/LKI.
Empty groups need exactly one matching card declaration. Missing/foreign frames,
missing visits/zones and duplicate IDs are unknown. X bounds and chooser wrappers
remain outside this query. Selection returns fresh storage and executes no callback.
The recipient collection query now accepts legal group frames, validates their
shape, and rejects missing, malformed and foreign bindings.

The shared destruction query validates complete trees and bindings before its
all-illegal gate or earlier proofs. Native source fixed/X division uses supported
collections or legal union frames. Nonempty damage prefixes conservatively block
later destruction proofs, even for zero totals; empty groups permit them.
Supported suffixes preserve prior proofs. Unknown operands/siblings remain unknown.
No damage, allocation, replacements, shield reads or state prediction occur.

CR 608.2b/c/f and 120.2b establish legality, ordering and simultaneous execution;
card rulings establish division at resolution and rounding. CR 601.2d distinguishes
Pyrotechnics. Existing engine execution selects recipients once, rounds down,
then uses shared replacements/prevention and simultaneous events. No new mutable
state, payment protocol, clone map, LKI store or Go-card fallback was added.
No Go card, DSL function or generator was removed; cutover gates remain unmet.
